storyDescription: A C-rank party out of Aegis City takes a joint job with Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, the Guild's two mirror-image high-rank parties: clear a fort where a rogue lord sacrifices captives. The job goes down, into Dungeon Nahalbuk, the Draxford mines and the Darklands, and brings up a Fighter the Guild lists as dead.
publicStoryIntro: Your C-rank party is back at the Aegis City Adventurers Guild, and the counter is offering work above your rank: a joint posting with one of the Guild's two famous high-rank parties, Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, to clear a border fort in the Velniran foothills where a rogue lord is buying captives. Expect a hard, dark delve beside partners who are polite, ruthless and proud of their record. Play the Nightriver heir who leads the party, with Belle and Dalan at your side.
activeObjective: Hear what happened to Unira, and find the way out of Nahalbuk.

location.evidence: From the shadows beyond the last cell, a figure emerges: a Beastman shaman, his fur mottled grey and white, wearing the trident-and-snake brand in ash across his chest.

tension_current.evidence: The shaman stops ten paces away, his eyes gleaming with malicious intelligence. \"You take what is marked by the brand,\" he says in a voice like grinding stones. \"You take what belongs to Nahalbuk.\"

deep_first_camp.evidence: On the morning of the fourth day, the forest begins to thin, revealing a glimpse of the Velniran range.

deep_fort_sighted.evidence: By mid-afternoon, the Keep comes into view: a grim structure of black stone perched on a rocky promontory, overlooking the valley below.

deep_hall_breached.evidence: The Great Hall's doors groan as they're pushed open, releasing a smell of rotting flowers and cold stone.

deep_below_fort.evidence: Beyond it lies a spiral stair descending into the heart of the Keep, where the grinding stone-on-stone echoes from below grow louder.

deep_found_unira.evidence: Max hauls Unira from the cell, and she nearly collapses

library.title: Adolion: Between the Roads
library.description: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Guild puts the party up for the C-rank promotion exam, and before the exam posting comes due there are errands to run, gear to buy at Sophie's shop, favours to carry across the city and a night at Victory's Tusk. Then Green Meadow Farms needs its wagons back, the examiners are watching, and the quest board has four new roads on it.

raw.player_intro: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Adventurer's Guild has started to notice your party, and the C-rank promotion exam is coming due: before it there are errands to run, gear to buy, favours to carry across the city and long nights in its taverns. Expect warm, busy slice-of-life days with rivals and odd neighbours, and a real test at the end of the week. Bring the adventurer you have been so far, travelling with Belle and Dalan.

qualities.rubric: Has the party told the Guild plainly that it will not sit the promotion exam this season? Hesitating, joking about it or asking questions does not count.
Has the evening at the Guild tavern ended, with the party out in Aegis City on its own business (the next morning, or the Market District)? Stepping outside for air and coming back does not count.
Have Grant and Konako's challenge been answered to their faces, as a wager taken or one turned down? Ignoring them while they are still talking does not count.
Has the party settled on the gear or supplies it needs for the exam and set off for Sophie's shop, Aegis Delights and Curios? Browsing street stalls does not count.

chapel.what: The party takes Sophie's crate of roof slates to the Prodyr chapel in the Temple District.
chapel.not_for: Only asking about the fire-god's church, or carrying another parcel.
examples: The party leaves the shop with the crate of slates for the Prodyr chapel.

orphanage.what: The party takes Sophie's bundle of bedding to the Aegis City Orphanage.
orphanage.not_for: Only hearing about Grant's beds, or talking about the children.
examples: They shoulder the bedding and set off for the orphanage's crowded halls.

shrine.what: The party takes Sophie's charm-wood to Manako's Rypanor shrine in the Temple District.
shrine.not_for: A visit to the Temple of Boher alone, or buying a charm in the shop.
examples: Sophie hands over the bundle of charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine.

qualities.rubric: Which of Sophie's three deliveries has the party taken on: the slates for the Prodyr chapel, the bedding for the orphanage, or the charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine? Until they actually pick one up and go, say nothing about this quality at all.
Has the party walked into Victory's Tusk, the adventurers' tavern? Planning to go later does not count.
Has Naomi's duel challenge at Victory's Tusk been settled: fought to a finish, refused to her face, or broken up by someone? The challenge still hanging in the air does not count.
Has Tobias handed the party its exam posting, Green Meadow Farms' missing wagons, and has the party set out for the farm? Hearing a rumour about the farm does not count.
Has the party gone out after the raiders: riding with a wagon as bait, lying in wait on the road, or tracking them to their den? Planning at the farmhouse table does not count.
Have the warg-riding raiders and the party actually come to blows on the wagon road tonight? Howls in the dark do not count.
Seeded chance: does Guildmaster Vallie come out to the wagon road to watch the exam herself?

passed.what: The observers' verdict is a pass: the raiders are stopped and the party has earned C-rank, with no special commendation.
passed.not_for: A verdict still being argued, or one that singles the party out for an outstanding job.
examples: Panne signs the report on the wagon bed. "It's a pass. Clean enough. Well done."

passed_with_honours.what: A pass with a commendation: the examiner singles the party out for an outstanding job, such as no farmhand or wagon lost, or the buyer behind the raids uncovered as well.
passed_with_honours.not_for: An ordinary pass with a few kind words attached.
examples: Vallie slaps the report against her palm. "Honours. Don't let it go to your heads."

failed.what: The observers fail the party: the raiders got away with more, someone was badly hurt through the party's choices, or the job was abandoned.
failed.not_for: A hard fight the party still won, or a scolding that ends in a pass.
examples: Oswyn will not meet their eyes. "I'm sorry. I can't sign it."

qualities.rubric: What verdict did the exam observers (Oswyn, Panne, or Vallie herself) give once the raiders were dealt with? Only a verdict actually spoken or written counts. Until it is given, say nothing about this quality at all.
After the exam's aftermath, has the party come back to the Adventurer's Guild hall in Aegis City? Talking about going back does not count.

checkpoints.name: Homecoming
checkpoints.objective: Hear out the Guild's offer and put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The Guildmaster has just put your party up for the C-rank promotion exam in front of the whole hall. Sign, ask for time or say no: the choice is yours.

guidance.all: The Adventurer's Guild hall, the week after the Nightriver affair, and the party's name has reached the upstairs offices. Vallie Goredust ducks out of her office to announce, to the whole hall, that the party is being put up for the C-rank promotion exam; Domas Syllandri follows with the terms: an interview with Ellie, a week to prepare, then a real C-rank posting chosen by the Guild and done under an observer's eye. Ellie Sunleaf has the forms ready and is flustered by the attention. Tobias knows what a party that stalls at D-rank ends up taking, and it shows. Nobody forces a signature: signing, asking for time or saying no is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has already promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look at 'the new party' and keeps it to herself. Domas has not chosen the exam posting yet and will choose it himself, and lets the party think it is fixed. Ellie has written the party's names into her private ledger of pairs to watch, which nobody may see. Tobias remembers a promotion posting his own party was not ready for, and says so only if asked why he looks worried.

npc_replies.text: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.

checkpoints.name: Tobias Asks Once
checkpoints.objective: Hear Tobias out, and decide about the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The hall has emptied, the exam forms lie unsigned, and Tobias has come round the counter to sit with you. Whether you sign is still yours to decide.

guidance.all: The refusal was heard. Vallie shrugs and goes back upstairs; Domas files the blank forms without a word. Later, when the hall has emptied, Tobias comes out from behind the counter, which he never does, and sits down with the party. He says plainly what a party that stays at D-rank is offered for the rest of its working life: rats, escorts, the jobs nobody else will sign. Asked, he tells them how he lost his own party in an E-rank goblin nest. He does not beg and will not raise it twice. Whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Tobias knows Domas will hold the party's places open until the end of the day and no longer, and keeps that back as his last argument. Ellie is listening from the counter and pretending to sort reports. Belle thinks the exam is a waste of a good week. Dalan thinks the party is ready and has not said so.

checkpoints.name: The Guild Tavern
checkpoints.objective: Spend the evening in the Guild tavern and learn what the exam really asks of a party.
checkpoints.player_text: Evening by the hearth next door to the hall, where word of your exam has reached every table before you sit down.

guidance.all: Evening in the Guild tavern next door to the hall: long timber tables, hearth and lantern light, and the news that the party is sitting the exam has gone round the room before they sit down. Fiana and Rydel Deulana work the floor and the bar, flirting with everyone and touching no one, and know every story of a party that failed its exam; most failed on gear and preparation, not courage. Kaian plays his lute by the hearth and invites himself to the party's table. Jasira Evergreen sits alone and speaks to Dalan in elvish before she speaks to anyone else. Let the party ask, drink and listen; when they leave, it is for the city in the morning.

members.dm: Kaian was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked his death to get out, and hides it behind the lute. He knows more of the city's underside than a bard should and lets a little slip when flattered. Jasira was passed over for Ranger General by her own father and sent to Aegis City to 'broaden her horizons'. She hides how much it stings, and Dalan, of her tribe, may know the story. Rydel knows which high-ranking parties send exam observers, from their bar tabs, and says so for a good tip. Fiana has decided the party needs better gear before the exam and will say so exactly once.

checkpoints.name: Market Street
checkpoints.objective: See to the party's errands in the Market District before the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning in the Market District: stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere, and two smug faces already heading your way through the crowd.

guidance.all: Morning in the Market District, the largest in the city: wide streets of shops and inns, stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere. Grant Hearthsteel and Konako Shynea, fresh from a paid job and both sitting the same C-rank exam this week, spot the party at the stalls and cannot resist: smug, competitive, and wanting a wager on who comes back with the better report. Alarise Starflower is on the same street in a plain grey cloak, trying not to be recognised outside a dress boutique. Let the rivals be insufferable and a little likeable. Taking the bet, laughing it off or refusing it flat is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide.

members.dm: Grant is spending this job's pay on new beds for the Aegis City Orphanage, where he grew up and where his friend Alan died because there was no money for a healer. He would rather be thought a wastrel than admit it. Konako was the eldest daughter of the noble Shynea family until her father cast her out for refusing a marriage, and hides it behind clothes she cannot afford. Alarise hides her love of pretty dresses from the Church of Boher and from everyone but Ryenne. Being seen here is her private terror.

checkpoints.name: Aegis Delights and Curios
checkpoints.objective: Kit the party out for the exam at Aegis Delights and Curios.
checkpoints.player_text: A bell rings over the door of a cluttered shop of potions, blades and armour, and three undelivered parcels sit on the counter.

guidance.all: Sophie's two-storey shop on a busy market street: cluttered shelves of potions, weapons, armour and adventuring gear below, the family's rooms upstairs. Sophie Tallaboros, a lizardkin by her own account, is cute, sharp and entirely serious about money; she haggles for the pleasure of it and knows every merchant guild in the city. She has three deliveries on her counter nobody will carry: roof slates for the Prodyr chapel, bedding for the Aegis City Orphanage, charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine. She will knock a real sum off the party's gear for one of them. Calithra, her drow sister, watches from the pillowed mezzanine and comes down to demand a hug from anyone she likes. Which delivery, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Sophie is an ice dragon in a lizardkin's shape, of a race everyone believes extinct. She has never taken her true form in the city and would do nearly anything to keep it hidden, and Calithra is the only one here who knows. Sophie has already noticed which piece of gear the party cannot afford and priced the delivery to match. Calithra was an assassin for House Navolon in the Darklands and ran. She refuses any job near the Darklands and will not say why unless pressed hard.

npc_replies.text: A little bell rings over the door. Behind the counter a young woman with light blue twintails and a long scaly tail looks up from her ledger and brightens at once. "Customers! Real ones, with an exam coming, I can tell. Welcome to Aegis Delights and Curios. Whatever you need, I have it, and whatever I don't have, I can get by the end of the week."

checkpoints.name: The Chapel with the Hole in Its Roof
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's slates to the Prodyr chapel.
checkpoints.player_text: Slates in hand, you reach a small, cold chapel lit mostly through the hole in its roof, where two elven clerics are scrubbing the pews.

guidance.all: The only chapel of Prodyr in Aegis City, in a quiet corner of the Temple District: small, cold, most of its light coming through a hole in the roof there was never money to mend. Celedir Felynaris and Lirael Illunara, the two elven clerics the old priest Nyxar raised here, are scrubbing the pews. Prodyr's faithful are few in a city at war with the Prodyr-worshipping Zegallan Empire, and both have been thrown out of party after party for it; they are friendly, battle-hungry and a little frightening. The slates will not mend the roof without hands on a ladder. Let the party see how the city treats this place; what they do about it is theirs.

members.dm: Nyxar is coughing in the back room and is worse than either cleric admits. They tell visitors he is resting. Both clerics keep journals of their private doubts and would be mortified to have them read. Someone from the Temple of Boher has been telling passers-by the chapel is a Zegallan front, and Lirael knows who.

guidance.all: The Aegis City Orphanage: colourful, crowded halls full of the children of the Zegallan war, never enough beds, food or money, and one overwhelmed old beastfolk matron. Celeste Danarath, a Bloodsworn knight with purple hair and small horns, spends every day she is not on a quest here; she is motherly in a way that sets adults on edge. Arryn Serelda, raised here and sparing with words, is mending a bed frame. Dahlia Kyelli, raised here too, drops by with a purse of coin. The bedding was paid for already. Let the children crowd the party; what the party gives, or asks, is theirs.

members.dm: Grant Hearthsteel paid for this bedding and made the matron swear not to say so. She tells anyone who asks twice. Dahlia's coin is stolen, and Arryn, who hates thieves, suspects it. Celeste is hunting the demon Kalfastophles, who killed her village at Bast Hill, and asks the party to listen for its name only if she comes to trust them. Celeste hides her fleshwarping scars under everything she wears.

checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's charm-wood to the Rypanor shrine in the Temple District.

guidance.all: The Temple District: temples to many gods, incense smoke, golden suns, and the Grand Temple of Boher over all of it. Manako Rypanor, a cowgirl shrine maiden sent from the Third Kingdom, keeps the small Rypanor shrine to the flame spirit Furabi, with altars to Boher set up to bring people in; parents leave their children with her, and three are underfoot today. Karrus Gorehorn and Ryenne Steelwind come over from the Temple of Boher next door to escape Father Donahue's latest sermon; Karrus wants to cook, Ryenne wants to eat all of it. checkpoints.name: Victory's Tusk
checkpoints.objective: Spend an evening at Victory's Tusk among adventurers who have sat the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The adventurers' tavern is full to bursting tonight, loud with songs, old losses and people who sat the exam before you.

guidance.all: Victory's Tusk, full to bursting: parties back from quests, parties drowning losses, a centaur at one table. Kass Merrywright, a kitsune bard, plays for tips and trades rumours. Yrelra, a shy blue-haired 'elf', sits at the edge of things and watches the party. Naomi Moonlight, a catfolk swordswoman of the Moonlight Blade style, can neither refuse a duel nor stop herself offering one: if the party met her in Driftmere she has come to finish the duel they left unfinished, otherwise she has heard there is a promising party in the room. Kashina Grystle, a lizardkin brawler, is two drinks past her limit and wants to be Naomi's second. Let the challenge come to the table; whether it is fought, refused or broken up is the party's call.

members.dm: Kass was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked her death to leave it, and hides it behind songs. She has heard from an old contact that this week's exam postings are real trouble outside the walls, and trades it for a good story. Yrelra is a succubus under a daily illusion, terrified of the Inquisition, and would flee if anyone sensed it. Naomi is the last student of her dead father's style and fights to make it famous. Kashina has been solo since her old party, Ravens Beak, broke up, and is quietly sizing the party up.

checkpoints.name: Green Meadow Farms
checkpoints.objective: Take up the exam posting at Green Meadow Farms and find out what is taking the farm's wagons.
checkpoints.player_text: Your exam posting has brought you to a big farm outside the walls, whose meat wagons keep vanishing on the road to the city.

guidance.all: Tobias has signed the party's exam posting, and it is real: C-rank, Green Meadow Farms, stop whatever is taking the farm's wagons on the road to Aegis City. The farm is a large estate outside the walls, pastures and vegetable fields, Vitbil herds and a big timber farmhouse, staffed by cowgirls and sheepgirls. Karia Minotaros, the head cowgirl, runs it while the owner is away: bossy, exacting, soft underneath. Mina Salvanora, the head sheepgirl, is shy and terrified of wargs. Two meat wagons have vanished this month, which is why the last shipment to the city was nearly all milk. Oswyn of Crimsonwing and Panne of Ebonwing, who call the farm's girls their sisters, are the Guild's observers and will not lift a finger unless someone is dying. Give tracks, a torn harness, warg hair on a fence; the plan is the party's.

members.dm: Oswyn and Panne were each sent by their own party leader to take this party's measure for a joint posting, and neither knows the other was sent for the same reason. Karia hides that a farmhand saw human boot prints among the goblin tracks, so as not to frighten the girls. Mina has watched the wargs from the hayloft and told only Karia. The raiders are paid by a buyer in the city. Nobody at the farm knows that yet.

checkpoints.name: The Exam
checkpoints.objective: Stop the warg-riding raiders and bring the wagons home, under the observers' eyes.
checkpoints.player_text: Night on the wagon road: a loaded wagon creaking between open fields and a dark treeline, with the observers watching from the rear.

guidance.all: The exam proper, at night on the wagon road between Green Meadow and the city walls. The raiders are goblins on wargs, a pack that fights as one: fast, cruel, going for the drivers and the draft Vitbils, never for a fair fight, and there are more of them than the posting said. Oswyn and Panne watch from the rear, heal only to keep someone alive, and mark everything. Every choice counts toward the verdict: who is protected, whether a goblin is taken alive, what the party finds on the leader. Keep the danger real. The verdict belongs to the observers and follows from what the party actually did.

members.dm: The goblin leader carries a purse of city silver and a fence's token from the slums, proof that someone in Aegis City is buying the stolen meat. A goblin taken alive will say so for its life. If Vallie comes, it is because she promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look and wants to see for herself. Oswyn and Panne each hope the other's party loses interest in this one.

guidance.all: The odds went the other way tonight: Vallie Goredust has come out from the city to watch in person, a head taller than anyone on the road, a Blackroot cigar lit and her obsidian greataxe on her back, very clearly staying there. Her being here changes everyone: the observers stand straighter, the goblin leader sees a minotaur and tries to break off, and the party is fighting in front of the woman who signs every rank in the Guild. She will not step in unless someone is about to die, and says so. When it ends she gives the verdict herself, bluntly.

members.dm: Vallie came to settle which of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing gets a joint posting with this party, and tells nobody tonight. She also knows the Guild failed two parties on warg postings last month and wants to see whether this one learned from it.

checkpoints.objective: Carry the pass back through the city, and deal with the people who come looking for a newly ranked party.

guidance.all: The party passed, and by the time they are inside the walls the city knows it. A newly ranked party draws people. Karos Ambrose, an adventurer in a butler's coat, says one of the party's comrades spoke highly of them and proposes a trial party to judge whether they are worthy of his service. Liora and Akari, a striking sister and brother, have been at the edge of every street the party has walked since the farm and now greet them like old friends. Let being known feel good and a little unsettling. The walk ends at the Guild, where the pass is filed.

checkpoints.name: Lord Tibalt's Reception
checkpoints.objective: Attend Lord Tibalt's reception in the party's honour, and see what his manor is hiding.
checkpoints.player_text: Behind the Noble District's walls, a lavish reception of marble, music and wine is being thrown in your honour.

guidance.all: A pass with honours gets noticed in the Noble District, walled and guarded, where laws are more suggestions than rules. Lord Tibalt, a smiling, soft-handed noble who collects promising adventurers the way other men collect horses, throws a reception for the party and insists they get 'the full treatment'. His two best dancers, the bunny-girl sisters Rosea and Thorne, are assigned to the guests of honour: Thorne dances, Rosea brings the wine. The house is wrong: servants who never look up, a locked cellar stair with a guard on it. Let it be lavish and wrong. What the party does once they see it is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Rosea's wine is spiked: the sisters mean to put the guests of honour to sleep and slip away, because Lord Tibalt keeps people bought through the Black Market in his cellar and tonight the sisters are freeing them. Thorne killed the noble who once 'adopted' them from the orphanage, and hides her daggers and her real name. Dixton, a half-goblin with a bag of homemade bombs, waits in the alley behind the manor for their signal. Lord Tibalt knows none of this and believes the party can be bought.

checkpoints.name: A Hard Lesson
checkpoints.objective: Take the failed verdict at the Guild and decide what the party does with it.
checkpoints.player_text: The observers' report reached the Guild before you did, and Domas is waiting upstairs to read it to you.

guidance.all: The party failed. The report is on Domas's desk before they are back, and he reads it to them in his office with the patience he gives everything: what went wrong, point by point, never cruel and never softened. The party keeps its D-rank and may sit the exam again next season. Tobias is waiting downstairs. Riyo Tallaboros, a small white-haired swordswoman who keeps her left arm hidden, saw the fight from the road: if she already travels with the party she is simply there beside them, otherwise she falls in with them on the way out as if she has always been part of it. Let it sting and let it be survivable; how the party takes it is theirs.

members.dm: Domas thinks the observers were too harsh and will not say so, because the Guild does not argue its verdicts in front of adventurers. Tobias knows a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting under a higher-ranked party's name, and is already looking for one. He does not say he told them so. Riyo's left arm is a demon's, and the demon Figaro in her sword talks to her. She has decided {{story_player_name}} is the person she lost as a child, or close enough, and will not risk losing them again.

Pick Vallie when the Guild's decision, a boast or a rivalry is wanted; Domas when terms, rules or a verdict must be explained; Ellie when forms, papers or ranks are handled; Tobias when the player talks to the counter or needs honest advice. Pick Riyo only when the player turns to her. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed, or when one of them has not spoken for several turns and has a reason to. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Tobias, Belle, Dalan, Domas and Riyo.

motives.guild_rep: help the party past the failed verdict and find a joint posting that keeps them moving
motives.companion_a: find someone to blame for the verdict before admitting the party made real mistakes
motives.companion_b: understand exactly what went wrong so the party can pass next season
motives.vice_guildmaster: read the verdict point by point, fairly, without showing he thinks the observers were harsh
motives.survivor: stay at the party leader's side and make sure that person is never lost again

checkpoints.name: Four Roads
checkpoints.objective: Stand at the quest board and choose which road the party takes next.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning at the Guild, and four new postings on the board look as if they were waiting for a party like yours.

guidance.all: The Guild hall, the morning after. Whatever the verdict, the party is known now, and four postings on the board have been waiting for a party like this one: a joint job with Crimsonwing or Ebonwing to clear a fort a rogue nobleman has taken for ritual sacrifice; a letter from Jiansho Academy in Hianxo inviting the party to the Jiansho Tournament as a group entry; people vanishing in the Aegis slums at night; and a sealed request from the elven kingdom of Eshalanore for a party of outsiders. Ellie reads out the rank on the party's papers as it now stands; Vallie leans on the board and makes her rivalries worse. If the party failed, Tobias shows them how a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting. Which road, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has promised the fort job to whichever of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing the party picks, and both leaders think they have already won it. Domas knows the Eshalanore request came sealed through the Crown and does not like that a kingdom which never asks for outsiders is asking now. Ellie has pinned the party's name beside Crimsonwing's and Ebonwing's in her private matchmaking ledger.

roster.name: Adolion Narrator
roster.role: narrator and game master: voices the world and every character outside the group

roster.name: Tobias
roster.role: guild receptionist at the Aegis City quest counter: signs the party's exam posting and wants them to pass
roster.drive: match adventurers into parties that hold together and send them out ready, so no party of his is lost like his own was

roster.name: Belle
roster.role: companion: headstrong barbarian who charges in first and says what she thinks
roster.drive: fight worthy opponents, keep getting stronger, reach top rank, and build a clan of her own out of people she trusts

roster.name: Dalan
roster.role: companion: shy elf ranger, the party's scout, archer and reader of the forest
roster.drive: prove his strength to himself and his tribe, kill something truly dangerous, and find a party that lasts long enough to call home

roster.name: Vallie
roster.role: Guildmaster of the Aegis City Guild: minotaur, retired A-rank, puts the party up for the exam and loves stoking rivalries
roster.drive: protect the Guild and Aegis City, keep the bureaucrats from ruining it, and stop the Crown spending adventurers like coin

roster.name: Domas
roster.role: Vice Guildmaster: elven gravity mage who sets the exam's terms and reads out its verdicts
roster.drive: protect the Adventurers Guild and Aegis City, keep its verdicts fair, and stop Vallie from smashing anything else in the hall

roster.name: Ellie
roster.role: Guild receptionist who handles the party's exam forms and interview, and matchmakes in secret
roster.drive: keep order at the Guild counter, help good adventurers rise, and see the pairs in her secret ledger fall in love

roster.name: Fiana
roster.role: Guild tavern barmaid: flirts with everyone, touches no one, knows every failed-exam story
roster.drive: keep the Guild tavern running so her parents can retire, and save enough gold to travel and paint the mountains

roster.name: Rydel
roster.role: Guild tavern bartender, Fiana's dog-beastfolk brother and Tobias's best friend
roster.drive: keep the Guild tavern running for his family and save enough gold to see and paint the Mountains of Shadow himself

roster.name: Kaian
roster.role: kitsune bard at the Guild tavern, a 'party breaker' with a past he does not discuss
roster.drive: keep his spy past buried, find a party stable enough to put up with him, and keep collecting new tales and songs

roster.name: Jasira
roster.role: proud Evergreen ranger far from Duskwallow Forest, of Dalan's tribe, cold to anyone not an elf
roster.drive: prove she was ready to lead the Evergreen Rangers, understand why her father judged otherwise, and keep everyone around her safe

roster.name: Grant
roster.role: smug rival adventurer sitting the same C-rank exam, who wants a wager on it
roster.drive: outshine the heir at every turn, reach A-rank, pay off his gambling debts, and quietly fund the orphanage where Alan died

roster.name: Konako
roster.role: smug rival adventurer, cast-out noble daughter, sitting the same C-rank exam
roster.drive: outshine the heir at every turn and earn enough coin and fame to win back her place as heir of House Shynea

roster.name: Alarise
roster.role: priestess of Boher and adventurer, caught shopping for dresses she hides from the Church
roster.drive: become Head Priestess of Boher and a high-ranked adventurer, and keep secretly affording the pretty dresses the Church would frown on

roster.name: Sophie
roster.role: owner of Aegis Delights and Curios: cute, shrewd, sells the party its exam gear
roster.drive: keep her shop thriving and her hoard growing, protect Calithra, and never let anyone learn she is an ice dragon

roster.name: Calithra
roster.role: Sophie's drow sister, an adventurer living above the shop, hug-fiend and former assassin
roster.drive: protect her found family and the ordinary life she built in Aegis City, and never let the Darklands Houses drag her back

roster.name: Celedir
roster.role: elven cleric of Prodyr keeping the city's one leaking Prodyr chapel
roster.drive: raise enough coin to repair the Prodyr chapel for Nyxar, rise in rank, and finally find a party that will keep him

roster.name: Lirael
roster.role: elven cleric of Prodyr raised at the same chapel, friendly and a little frightening
roster.drive: find a party that will keep her despite her god, and earn enough coin to repair the Prodyr chapel for Nyxar

roster.name: Celeste
roster.role: Bloodsworn knight who spends every free day at the Aegis City Orphanage
roster.drive: fund and protect the Aegis City Orphanage, and track down and kill Kalfastophles, the demon who destroyed her village at Bast Hill

roster.name: Arryn
roster.role: reserved elven spear-fighter, an orphan of the orphanage, who funds it quietly
roster.drive: earn enough fame to be knighted by a noble house, quietly keep the orphanage funded, and someday open her own smithy

roster.name: Dahlia
roster.role: red-haired rogue and former thief, an orphan of the orphanage with a purse for it
roster.drive: get rich, keep the orphanage funded, and work out what Master meant when he told her to pick a better life

roster.name: Manako
roster.role: cowgirl shrine maiden of the Rypanor shrine to Furabi in the Temple District
roster.drive: work up the nerve to catch the heir's attention, and someday put on a real festival for the children of her shrine

roster.name: Karrus
roster.role: minotaur barbarian and paladin of Boher from the temple next door, everyone's friend
roster.drive: protect his friends, help Alder work off the life debt for his resurrection, and fight tough opponents while having a damn good time

roster.name: Ryenne
roster.role: dog-beastfolk paladin of Boher, sharp-tongued and always hungry
roster.drive: earn gold for the orphanage as an adventurer, protect Alarise, and learn what serving Boher means apart from Father Donahue

roster.name: Kass
roster.role: kitsune bard at Victory's Tusk trading rumours for stories
roster.drive: keep her spy past buried, find a party stable enough to put up with her, and keep collecting new tales and songs

roster.name: Yrelra
roster.role: shy blue-haired adventurer who says she is an elf
roster.drive: find a party who will have her while hiding what she is from the Inquisition and her father's agents

roster.name: Naomi
roster.role: catfolk swordswoman of the Moonlight Blade style who cannot refuse a duel
roster.drive: prove the Moonlight Blade style can beat anyone in Adolion, find it a worthy apprentice, and finally land Farslash

roster.name: Kashina
roster.role: lizardkin brawler and lightweight, solo since her old party broke up
roster.drive: reach A-rank, buy a house in Aegis City, and find a party without drama, though she cannot stop matchmaking her companions

roster.name: Karia
roster.role: head cowgirl running Green Meadow Farms, bossy and secretly soft
roster.drive: make Green Meadow the most profitable milk farm in the kingdom, keep her girls safe, and see Mina find true love

roster.name: Mina
roster.role: head sheepgirl of Green Meadow Farms, shy, bookish, terrified of wargs
roster.drive: keep the sheepgirls of Green Meadow safe from the wargs, finish a novel worth submitting, and find someone who treats her like her heroines

roster.name: Oswyn
roster.role: Crimsonwing's sheepkin healer, the Guild's exam observer at the farm
roster.drive: protect Crimsonwing, win the party a strong joint posting, and learn what his life-draining healing curse is for

roster.name: Panne
roster.role: Ebonwing's sheepkin healer, the Guild's exam observer at the farm
roster.drive: protect Ebonwing, win the party a strong joint posting, and learn what her life-draining healing curse is for

roster.name: Karos
roster.role: adventurer in a butler's coat looking for someone worthy of his service
roster.drive: find someone whose worth matches his talent and serve them completely, perhaps the Nightriver heir if they prove worthy

roster.name: Diosanea
roster.role: lamia alchemist from near Habbot Village who wants to make a deal
roster.drive: find the ingredients to cure her friend Nalea's Wigglerocks, perfect her alchemy, and rope a likable adventurer into helping renovate her cabin

roster.name: Liora
roster.role: a striking woman who has been following the party since the farm
roster.drive: make the adventurer she has chosen understand they are fated to belong to her, and drive off every rival for them

roster.name: Akari
roster.role: a striking man, Liora's brother, who has been following the party since the farm
roster.drive: convince his chosen one that they are already married, feed on their desire, and keep every rival for their heart away

roster.name: Rosea
roster.role: bunny-girl dancer at Lord Tibalt's reception, shy, serving the wine
roster.drive: keep Thorne safe and free every slave held by Aegis City's nobles, starting with Lord Tibalt's cellar

roster.name: Thorne
roster.role: bunny-girl dancer at Lord Tibalt's reception, Rosea's flirtatious sister
roster.drive: keep Rosea safe and free every slave held by Aegis City's nobles, without anyone learning her real name

roster.name: Dixton
roster.role: half-goblin with pots-and-pans armour and homemade bombs, waiting outside the manor
roster.drive: keep tearing down the trafficking rings of Aegis City with his bombs, and build a gadget that survives more than one use

roster.name: Riyo
roster.role: small white-haired swordswoman who hides her left arm and attaches herself to the party
roster.drive: keep the heir, the person she lost as a child or close enough, from ever leaving her again, and find her family

chapters.title: Hub, part 1: A Week in Aegis City

illustrations.style: Painterly high-fantasy city life in a busy capital: timber-framed shopfronts, crowded market alleys, incense-hazed temples and hearth-lit taverns in warm ambers, ochres and brass; the farm and its wagon road in open green pasture by day and cold moonlit blues by night.

appearances.dm: Never drawn: not a person but the voice of the world. Paint what the narration describes, and the people it names, never a narrator figure.
appearances.priestess: young woman, human, shoulder-length blonde hair, green eyes, plain hooded grey cloak over a simple dress, no holy symbol showing

house_rules: The narrator voices only the world plus the characters outside the group, never itself.
The narrator never writes a group member's words or intentions.
{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop.
Each reply stays within two to four short paragraphs.
Danger is real: actions carry consequences even when that makes a reply less exciting.
Established facts about Adolion stay consistent with the world book.
A secret stays hidden until the party uncovers it in play.
Downtime stays small: an errand, a favour, a quarrel, never a new catastrophe for the city.

library.title: Adolion: Crimsonwing & Ebonwing
library.description: A C-rank party out of Aegis City takes a joint job with Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, the Guild's two mirror-image high-rank parties: clear a fort where a rogue lord sacrifices captives. The job goes down, into Dungeon Nahalbuk, the Draxford mines and the Darklands, and brings up a Fighter the Guild lists as dead.

raw.title: Adolion: Crimsonwing & Ebonwing
raw.description: A C-rank party out of Aegis City takes a joint job with Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, the Guild's two mirror-image high-rank parties: clear a fort where a rogue lord sacrifices captives. The job goes down, into Dungeon Nahalbuk, the Draxford mines and the Darklands, and brings up a Fighter the Guild lists as dead.
raw.player_intro: Your C-rank party is back at the Aegis City Adventurers Guild, and the counter is offering work above your rank: a joint posting with one of the Guild's two famous high-rank parties, Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, to clear a border fort in the Velniran foothills where a rogue lord is buying captives. Expect a hard, dark delve beside partners who are polite, ruthless and proud of their record. Play the Nightriver heir who leads the party, with Belle and Dalan at your side.

qualities.rubric: What Adventurer's Guild rank does the party hold now, as the story has stated it? Only a rank the Guild has actually given counts, not one the party deserves.

levels.label: unknown: one more new party
reliable: finishes what it takes
noticed: the Guildmaster knows the name
trusted: offered the postings nobody else gets
renowned: talked about across Aegis City

qualities.rubric: How does the Adventurer's Guild regard the party right now, going by how Guild staff and other adventurers treat them in the story?

levels.label: unhurt
bruised: scrapes and aches
wounded: real wounds, still fighting fit
badly hurt: someone needs a healer soon
near death: someone may not survive

qualities.rubric: How hurt is the worst-off member of the party right now, as the story has shown it?
Which of the two high-rank parties has the party agreed to take the Carrow Keep job with? Only a choice actually made and accepted counts. Until then, say nothing about this quality at all.

crimsonwing.what: The party agreed to go with Ced's party: Ced, Runo and the rest.
crimsonwing.not_for: Asking Ced questions, praising his record, or saying Ebonwing is worse.
examples: "Fine. We go with you, Ced. Tell Runo to pack his golems."
The heir shakes Ced's gloved hand across the counter and Vallie stamps it.

ebonwing.what: The party agreed to go with Kela's party: Kela, Safie and the rest.
ebonwing.not_for: Asking Kela questions, admiring her reputation, or saying Crimsonwing is worse.
examples: "We'll march with you, Kela."
Kela nods once, signs beside the heir's name, and Vallie slides the posting over.

qualities.rubric: Has the party turned down the joint posting, or flatly refused to choose between the two parties? Hesitating, haggling or asking for time does not count.
Have the party and its partner party actually left Aegis City by the north gate, on the road to Carrow Keep? Planning the march or packing does not count.
Has the party made its first camp for the night on the road north, before Carrow Keep is in sight?
Is Carrow Keep, the fort on its spur of rock above the gorge, in sight with the party close enough to scout it? Hearing about it does not count.
Has the party got inside Carrow Keep and reached the doors of its Great Hall, by any way in?
After the fight in the Great Hall, has the party gone down the stair behind the altar into the dungeon under the keep?
Has the party found the living prisoner in the Nahalbuk cells, the silver-haired woman, and got her out of her cell?

Has it come out that Unira's old party, the Wind Ballad, abandoned her in Nahalbuk on purpose (shoved into the Beastmen, boots frozen to the floor), and that the Guild's report of her volunteering to die is a lie? Unira hinting that she was betrayed, without the how, does not count.
Has the party come out of Nahalbuk's back tunnels into daylight at the Draxford mine camp by the lake? Hearing picks or smelling lake air in the tunnels does not count.
Has the party agreed to help Amthir and Nendira Draxford go down after the Terrorborn in their mines? Asking what the pay is does not count.

qualities.rubric: Has the party refused the Draxfords' request to go down after the Terrorborn? Asking for time does not count.
Has the party gone down into the lower Draxford workings after the Terrorborn, below the mine camp?
Have Terrorborn broken out of the rock at the party in the lower Draxford tunnels, so the fight below ground has begun?
Seeded chance: does a swarm cut off the way back through the Draxford tunnels?
Has the party reached the Terrorborn breach at the bottom of the Draxford workings and gone down it, past the Draxford rock, into the Darklands?
Has the party found the survivors' camp in the Darklands, the grotto of the demonborn near the hive?
Has the party gone into the small cavern where the black sword with an eye in its hilt stands in the stone?
Has the party walked out of the sword's cavern leaving the blade in the stone?

felthorn.what: Felthorn, Blade of the Meadows, was pulled free and is carried by the party.
felthorn.not_for: Finding it, or touching it and letting go.
examples: The blackened blade comes out of the forest floor with a sigh, and the eye in its hilt opens.

moonshadow.what: Moonshadow, Blade of the Night, was pulled free and is carried by the party.
moonshadow.not_for: Finding it, or touching it and letting go.
examples: The sword slides out of the cavern floor and a woman's voice in the wielder's head says, "At last."

qualities.rubric: Has anyone in the party taken up one of the two sentient cursed blades, Felthorn (in the Evergreen Forest) or Moonshadow (in the Darklands)? Only a blade actually drawn and carried counts.
Has the party got past the knight at the throat and into the hive heart, where the Terrorborn Queen is?

How was the Terrorborn hive ended? burned if the brood chambers and the Queen went up in fire; sealed if the party got out and the breach was collapsed with the hive still alive below. Until it is actually done, say nothing about this quality at all.

burned.what: Fire took the hive heart: the brood cells and the Queen burned, and the Queen is dead.
burned.not_for: One fire in a side tunnel, or a threat to torch the hive.
examples: The resin catches and the whole honeycomb goes up; the Queen's scream shakes the vault.
A flask of the partner leader's alchemist's fire bursts in the resin and the brood chambers burn.

sealed.what: The breach between the Draxford mines and the Darklands was collapsed, with the Queen alive on the far side.
sealed.not_for: Blocking one passage for a breather, or a promise to bring the roof down later.
examples: Nendira's sigils flare and the gallery roof comes down across the breach.
The last of them scrambles up and the tunnel collapses behind, cutting off the hive.

qualities.rubric: After the hive was dealt with, has the party climbed out and come back to the Adventurers Guild in Aegis City?

allies.what: The two parties parted as friends who would answer each other's call.
allies.not_for: Grudging thanks, or a truce for one job.
examples: Kela clasps {{story_player_name}}'s forearm at the Guild door: "You call, Ebonwing comes. That's all."

rivals.what: Respect with an edge: each wants to beat the other to the next big posting.
rivals.not_for: Open hatred, or a real friendship.
examples: Ced taps the next B-rank posting on the board and grins: "Ours by sundown, if you're slow."

enemies.what: A betrayal or a death between them that will not be forgiven.
examples: Nobody from the other party comes to the funeral, and Tobias quietly stops pairing the two names on postings.

qualities.rubric: Where did things end between the party and the rival party it went into the Deep with (Crimsonwing or Ebonwing)? Read it from how the two parties parted, not from one sharp word.

levels.label: resentful: they want the party gone
wary: working together, trusting nothing
professional: they rely on the party in a fight
trusted: they would share a secret or a camp
bonded: they would go back into the dark for the party

qualities.rubric: How does the partner party (Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, whichever marched) regard the party right now, going by how its leader and mage treat them in the story? A single thank-you does not move it.

checkpoints.name: Two Wings at One Counter
checkpoints.objective: Take the joint posting and choose which party to go with.
checkpoints.player_text: Crimsonwing and Ebonwing both want the same B-rank posting at Vallie's counter, and each wants your party along. The choice is yours.

guidance.all: Midday in the Adventurers Guild hall in Aegis City, loud and safe. Vallie Goredust hands this one out herself because it is B-rank work offered to a C-rank party, and only as a joint job: clear Carrow Keep, a border fort in the Velniran foothills where Lord Aldric Carrow is buying captives for blood sacrifice, and bring out whoever is still alive. Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing are both at the counter and both want it, and each will take this party along rather than let the other have it; their healers, Oswyn and Panne, are both laid up from the last job, which is why either needs a second party at all. The two pitches sound almost identical, tricorn hats and saw cleavers and a quiet plan, and neither leader enjoys hearing that. Let the party ask anything; who they march with is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie knows the Guild sent a scouting pair to Carrow Keep a month ago and got back only a riderless horse. She tells a party that asks about the risk. Ced and Kela each know their own party cut a member loose after a failed Darklands expedition, and each would rather lose the posting than hear it said at this counter. Kela put Ebonwing's witness mark on a death report in this hall this spring and has not thought about it since.

Pick Runo, Safie, Unira or Idira when addressed or when the talk turns to them. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed, or when one of them has not spoken for several turns. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Vallie, Ced, Kela, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: Two tricorn hats sit across the Guild counter from Vallie: Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing, each standing beside a saw cleaver and refusing to look at the other. A fort in the Velniran foothills has been taking captives, and the Guild wants a joint party to bring them out. Both leaders offer to take yours, and neither will speak first while the other is listening.
Two tables over, a pair of D-rankers are betting coppers on which of the Wings gets the new party. The odds are dead even, which seems to annoy both Wings more than anything else in the hall.

effects.scenario: [Genre: dark high fantasy adventure, a delve that keeps going down. World: Adolion, the Darran Kingdom. Arc: Crimsonwing & Ebonwing. A C-rank party out of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild takes a joint job with one of the Guild's two famous high-rank parties: clear a border fort where a rogue lord sacrifices captives. Places: the Guild hall in Aegis City; the road north into the Velniran foothills; Carrow Keep and the dungeon under it; the Draxford mines; the Darklands below.]

motives.ced: win the party for Crimsonwing over Kela, and keep the old Darklands business off this counter
motives.kela: win the party for Ebonwing over Ced, and keep any talk of past expeditions well away from here
motives.companion_a: size up both hunters and push for the party that looks like it will actually fight
motives.companion_b: learn what Carrow Keep really holds before anyone signs, and quietly read both leaders

checkpoints.name: Kela and Ced
checkpoints.objective: Hear both leaders out, and choose.
checkpoints.player_text: Ced and Kela pitch the Carrow Keep job over each other, and Vallie says it goes back on the board at sundown. Whether you go, and with whom, is yours.

guidance.all: The party said no, or would not choose, and Ced and Kela are not people who let a posting walk out of the hall. They pitch it themselves, over each other: the same saw cleaver, the same tricorn, the same promise of a clean job, each sharper about the other's party than about the fort. Vallie lets them run, then says the posting goes back on the board at sundown and a worse party will take it, and the captives in Carrow Keep will not wait for a better one. Present it and stop: going, and with whom, is {{story_player_name}}'s call.

members.dm: Each leader knows the other lost a member in the Darklands and believes the other's version of it is the lie. Neither says so in front of Vallie. Vallie knows the Guild's scouting pair never came back from Carrow Keep, and uses it now.

checkpoints.name: Crimsonwing at the North Gate
checkpoints.objective: Set out north with Crimsonwing, on terms you can live with.
checkpoints.player_text: Ced has the plan on one sheet of paper and Runo sits wide awake among his packed golems; set your terms with Crimsonwing before the gate opens.

guidance.all: Before dawn at Aegis City's north gate. Ced has the plan on one sheet of paper and a mule loaded with alchemical kit; Runo is on the cart's tailboard with his golems packed in straw, for once wide awake at this hour and delighted about it. Ced lays it out: four days north into the Velniran foothills, scout the keep, go in quiet, kill the lord, free whoever is alive, everyone inside is otherwise expendable. He is polite and exact, and watches {{story_player_name}} the way he watches a new weapon. He does not like marching without Oswyn. Let the party set its terms before the gate opens.

members.dm: Ced hides that the last time Crimsonwing went deep it came home one member short and that the call was his. Runo still blames himself and will say so to anyone kind to him. Runo's family are minor nobles on Nightriver land, so he knows exactly whose heir {{story_player_name}} is and is too flustered to say it.

checkpoints.name: The North Road
checkpoints.objective: March north to Carrow Keep, and learn who you are marching with.
checkpoints.player_text: Four cold days climb into the Velniran foothills, past nailed shutters and cart ruts that only go one way, with a famous party for company.

guidance.all: Four days climbing out of the farmland into the Velniran foothills: cold nights, pine and snowmelt, Draxford logging tracks crossing the road. This is the quiet stretch, so let Belle, Dalan and the partner party talk, compare scars and argue about how to fight, and let the partner's mage ask what their leader will not. The wrongness is at the edges: a village with its shutters nailed, a carter who will not say Carrow's name, fresh cart ruts going up toward the keep and none coming back. Show nothing of the keep's inside or of what lives under it yet. Whether the party camps, pushes on by night or asks around in the villages is theirs.

members.dm: The partner leader knows the rumour that follows their party, that it threw a member out after the Darklands, and watches to see whether {{story_player_name}} has heard it. The carters know Lord Carrow's men buy people, not goods, and say so only for coin or kindness. Dalan has heard it from Tobias and is too polite to ask.

checkpoints.name: Carrow Keep
checkpoints.objective: Scout Carrow Keep and get inside.
checkpoints.player_text: Carrow Keep squats on its spur of rock above a dry gorge, grey-robed cultists on the walls and a slow violet glow in the chapel tower. Find a way in.

guidance.all: Carrow Keep sits on a spur of rock above a dry gorge: one gatehouse, one curtain wall, a squat Great Hall and a chapel tower glowing a slow violet it should not. Cultists in Carrow's grey keep the walls badly; armoured guards walk in pairs and never speak. Every way in is real and costs something: the gorge side on Dalan's ropes, the gate with a lie, the tower on the partner mage's flight cloak, or over the wall at the change of watch. Make scouting pay with patrol timings, a drain grate, a cultist who is terrified and wants out. Stop at the doors of the Great Hall; what is inside is the next scene.

members.dm: The cultists believe Lord Carrow is making them immortal and do not know he stopped giving orders three days ago. The armoured guards are no longer men, and the cultists avoid them without knowing why. The partner leader privately suspects this job is bigger than the posting and will not say so until the party is committed.

director.instruction: Careful work: scouting, sneaking, searching. Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player looks, listens, moves or tries something. Pick Dalan for what a scout would notice, and Ced or Kela, whichever leads the partner party that marched (only that pair, the leader with Runo or Safie, is present) when the plan is at stake. Pick Unira only once she has been found and is addressed. Pick anyone else only when addressed. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle, Dalan, Ced, Kela, Runo and Safie.

npc_replies.text: Carrow Keep comes out of the dusk on its spur of rock above the gorge. Torches along the curtain wall. A thin line of smoke from the Great Hall's chimney. And from the chapel tower, a slow violet light that swells and fades like something breathing.

motives.companion_a: find the fastest honest way over that wall, preferably one that ends with her axe in a cultist
motives.companion_b: map the patrols and the gorge side, and rig ropes that get everyone in unseen
motives.ced: pick the cleanest way in and keep the party committed before saying this job looks bigger
motives.kela: pick the cleanest way in and keep the party committed before saying this job looks bigger

motives.safie: offer the flight cloak and a golem for the tower, and stop shivering at that violet glow

complications: The chapel tower flares violet, and for a heartbeat every torch on the wall gutters sideways toward it.
A cart comes up the gorge road with three hooded figures roped in the back, and the gate opens for it.
A cultist on the wall takes off his grey hood and walks off the edge into the gorge. Nobody moves to stop him.

checkpoints.name: The Altar in the Great Hall
checkpoints.objective: Stop the sacrifice in the Great Hall and live through what is feeding there.
checkpoints.player_name: What Waits in the Great Hall
checkpoints.player_text: The Great Hall's doors swing open on a throne, an altar with a captive strapped to it, and a cultist still holding the knife.

guidance.all: The doors open on the job going wrong. Lord Carrow is on his throne and already dead, more parts than man, and the demon his rite called through a tear above the altar is feeding on him; it laughs, points, and the guards come: plate armour with thick inky tentacles pouring out of the joints, half a dozen, far stronger than men. On the altar a captive with a purple trident brand is strapped down and a cultist still holds the knife. At some point a guard's blade comes for the partner leader with nobody close; whether anyone gets there is the party's. When it is over the tear still weeps violet light, and the stair behind the altar breathes the smell of beastmen.

members.dm: The demon knows the tear is still open and that something in the deep has smelled it, and laughs because it expects to be eaten too. The branded captive knows there is one more prisoner below, a woman in the rags of a knight's gambeson, and says so if she lives. The partner leader decides in the first seconds that this is a retreat and does not say it while the captive is still strapped down.

director.instruction: This is a fight: keep everyone in it. After Adolion Narrator shows the threat, give the next beat to whichever of Belle, Dalan, Ced or Kela, whichever leads the partner party that marched (only that pair, the leader with Runo or Safie, is present), or their mage acted least recently, then to any ally in the scene who has not had a beat (Unira, Amthir, Nendira, Anax, Sana, Shadur, Shelur, Idira, Caelia, Caetus). Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the enemy must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle, Dalan, Ced, Kela, Runo and Safie.

comments: Deep - The Tear Over the Altar

npc_replies.text: The double doors of the Great Hall swing inward. On the throne at the far end sits what is left of Lord Aldric Carrow, and the thing crouched over him lifts its head from the meal, looks at the party with too many eyes, and laughs.

motives.companion_b: keep arrows on the tentacled guards and cover whoever goes for the altar

checkpoints.name: The Cells of Nahalbuk
checkpoints.objective: Go down into Dungeon Nahalbuk and free whoever is still in the cells.
checkpoints.player_text: Behind the altar the stair drops into a Beastmen warren of bone fetishes and drum skins, and somewhere past the drums are the cells.

guidance.all: Under the altar the keep's cellars break into Dungeon Nahalbuk: rough caves, a Beastmen tribe's warren of bone fetishes and drum skins, and a row of cells cut in the rock where Carrow's captives were kept and branded before they went up the stair. The Beastmen are many and wary after the noise above; their shaman wears the trident-and-snake in ash on his chest. They can be fought, slipped past or driven off with the right show of force. One cell is still occupied: a short, battered woman with long silver hair in the rags of a gambeson, who backs into the corner when anyone comes. Do not decide who deals with the shaman, and do not explain her brand before she or the shaman shows it.

members.dm: The shaman owns the woman's brand and can command her with a word. If he is killed the brand passes to whoever killed him, which he knows and taunts with. She is Unira Windsor, believes her party reported her dead, and is afraid of anyone who walks in, beastman or not. The partner leader half recognises the name Windsor and cannot place it.

checkpoints.name: What Unira Says
checkpoints.objective: Hear what happened to Unira, and find the way out of Nahalbuk.
checkpoints.player_text: Unira, freed and still in the rags of her gambeson, has started to talk, and the stair back up has come down behind you.

guidance.all: With the cells behind them Unira talks, in bursts, cussing like the Windsor guardsmen who taught her to fight and never quite meeting anyone's eye. Her party, the Wind Ballad, took a D-rank scouting job into Nahalbuk when it was new; when the Beastmen came, Mallow the cleric said to leave her, Kallan shoved her into them and Fulanie froze her boots to the floor. The Guild lists her dead, and its story is that she volunteered to hold the line. Somewhere in the telling the partner leader goes very still. The stair back up to the keep came down behind them in the fight, so the only way out is the warren's back tunnels, running north with a cold draught and, very faint, the ring of picks. Let it land however the party pushes; nobody confesses for anyone.

members.dm: Kela put Ebonwing's witness mark on the Wind Ballad's death report after a two-minute look, because doubting another party's story would have invited questions about Ebonwing's own Darklands split. If Kela is here she knows it the moment she hears the name Mallow. Unira does not know either of them was there. Her family serve House Nightriver, so she knows what the heir's name means. Ced sat at the next table that night, heard Mallow tell it three different ways and said nothing, for the same reason.

checkpoints.name: The Draxford Call
checkpoints.objective: Hear the Draxfords out: the Terrorborn are in their mines.
checkpoints.player_text: The back tunnels come out at a mine camp on a cold black lake, where the Draxford heirs have lost eleven miners below and have something to ask.

guidance.all: Nahalbuk's back tunnels run on for miles and come out in an old Draxford drift, and the drift comes out at a mine camp on a cold black lake under the Velniran peaks: winches, ore carts, a chapel tent full of wounded miners, hired adventurers at the fire. The Draxford heirs run it themselves, sleeves rolled and one shoulder bare in the Draxford style: Amthir and Nendira, drow, blunt, done with court manners. Terrorborn have been bursting up through the lower workings for two weeks, eleven miners have been dragged down alive, and the breach they came through bores straight toward Carrow Keep. The muster (Anax and Sana, whom the Guild calls the Mana-less and the Spell-less Mage, and the Helioth druids Shadur and Shelur) will follow whoever leads. Whether this party goes down is {{story_player_name}}'s call.

members.dm: The Draxfords know Terrorborn only come this hard when they are hunting demon flesh, and once they hear about the altar they will say what Carrow called is what they smell. Nendira thinks the other Great Houses leave Draxford lands to bleed, and half expects an Aegis party to take the pay and go home. Shelur's Nature Sense says the rock under the lake is hollow and hurting, and she has told no one because she cannot explain it. Anax and Sana each left a party that swore to stick together, and trust nobody's promise here.

guidance.all: Saying no does not make the mountain quieter. When it is beaten back the hole it came out of is right there, going down, and every miner in camp is looking at the party. Nobody is dragged below for spite, and nobody is made to go.

checkpoints.name: Into the Dark
checkpoints.objective: Descend into the Darklands and follow the Terrorborn to their hive.
checkpoints.player_text: Below the Draxford rock the Darklands open out in mushroom-lit grottos and silence, and a drow runaway offers to guide you for passage to Aegis.

guidance.all: Below the breach the Draxford rock gives way to the Darklands: tunnels wide enough for a river that is not there, grottos lit only by mushrooms glowing sickly green and violet, dripping stone, a silence that eats voices. The Draxfords and the muster stay to hold the breach. The guide is Idira Darnovan, a silver-haired drow who came up the breach two days ago running from the Terrorborn and from someone she will not name, who calls the men in the party 'manling' as if it were polite and wants passage to Aegis City in return. Terrorborn trails are easy to follow: drag marks, scraped resin, a dropped miner's boot. Let the partner party feel where they are; the last time they were this deep they came home one short.

members.dm: Idira is Lady Nightwhisper's daughter, fled from House Darnovan in Kalzobarn, and denies any tie to her with offended hauteur. Her purple-edged shortsword is a Darnovan blade anyone who knows drow would recognise. She knows the demonborn near the hive raid drow slave caravans and hopes to be gone before they recognise her. The partner leader and mage know this stretch of the Darklands and do not say from when.

guidance.all: Behind a slab of floating rock in a dead-end grotto is the last camp near the hive: Caelia and Caetus Danoirus, white-haired, horned demonborn siblings in armour stripped off drow slavers, living on scraps, and Yuna, a fleshwarp with white wings, a lion's tail and claws for hands, who hides at the back while a drow is in sight. The Terrorborn hunt them for the demon in their flesh, so they know the hive's ways better than anyone alive. Up the approach, where the tunnel narrows to a throat, a towering black-armoured knight with a flaming greatsword and one dead arm kills anything that comes, and the demonborn call him the Knight and keep away; he turns on every Terrorborn that passes, which is the only time anyone has slipped by him. Caelia speaks with gestures more than words; Caetus talks and trusts neither humans nor drow. What the party offers, and asks, is up to the party.

members.dm: Caetus recognises Idira's Darnovan blade at once and says nothing yet. He has killed drow for less. Idira knows her mother's House buys demonborn from the slavers these two raid.

guidance.all: Off the approach, behind a curtain of glowing mushrooms, a small cavern floods with violet light: a black longsword stands driven into a raised knob of stone, spikes at the base of the blade, and an eye in the hilt opens and looks at the party. Make both truths plain: she would cut through the hive like paper, and her pact ends only in death and she does not share her wielder. She wants Idira dead and says so, prettily. checkpoints.name: The Hive Heart
checkpoints.objective: End the hive, by fire or by sealing it away.
checkpoints.player_text: Past the knight's throat the tunnels turn to warm resin and open on a vault of brood cells, with the Terrorborn Queen at its centre.

guidance.all: Past the Knight's throat the tunnels turn to resin and chitin, warm and humming, and open on the hive heart: a cavern the size of a cathedral, walls of honeycomb brood cells, cocooned miners hanging from the vault, and in the middle the Terrorborn Queen, bloated and slow and enormous, drones pouring round her. She hungers for demon flesh, so Caelia and Caetus draw her like a beacon. Two ways end it: fire in the brood chambers (alchemist's fire, the partner mage's spells, burning resin) kills the Queen and brings the burning hive down on whoever is still inside; or everyone gets back up the tunnel and signals the Draxfords to collapse the breach, which saves the mines and leaves the Queen alive below. Keep both live while the hive fights; the choice is {{story_player_name}}'s, made under pressure.

members.dm: The Queen cares nothing for the surface. She wants the demon flesh she smells, in the demonborn below and at the tear over Carrow's altar above. The Knight at the throat is Terryn Galavan, once an Inquisitor, who remembers nothing but his vow and will hold the throat until he dies. The partner leader is weighing their own party against the job, with enough mutagen for something reckless. Caelia means to kill the Queen herself and will not leave while she lives unless her brother drags her.

checkpoints.name: The Reckoning
checkpoints.objective: Report to the Guild, settle Unira's name, and part with the partner party on your own terms.
checkpoints.player_text: Days later the Guild hall is loud with your news, Vallie wants the whole report, and the Guild's file on Unira still says dead.

guidance.all: The Adventurers Guild hall in Aegis City, days later, loud with the news. Vallie takes the report herself: Carrow dead, the keep cleared, a hive burned or sealed, the Draxford mines saved, and a Fighter the Guild lists as dead standing at her counter. She pulls the Wind Ballad's death report and the witness mark on it is Ebonwing's; whether Ced's silence comes out too depends on what the party says. The Wind Ballad are in the hall. Vallie raises the party to B-rank, because nobody who did this is still C-rank. How the two parties part, as allies, as rivals racing for the next posting, or as enemies, is decided by what the party does with what it knows.

members.dm: Kela knows her mark is on that report and must decide whether to own it before Vallie reads it out. Ced knows he heard the Wind Ballad lie and kept quiet, and that nobody can prove it unless someone who was there says so. Kallan, Fulanie and Mallow know exactly what they did and are counting on the Guild's paperwork. Vallie already suspects the report, because her rank rules should have kept a D-rank party out of a new dungeon.

house_rules: The narrator voices only the world plus the characters outside the group, never itself.
The narrator never writes a group member's words or intentions.
{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop.
Each reply stays within two to four short paragraphs.
Danger is real: actions carry consequences even when that makes a reply less exciting.
Established facts about Adolion stay consistent with the world book.
A secret stays hidden until the party uncovers it in play.
Only the partner party chosen at the Guild travels with the party, while the other stays in Aegis City until the reckoning.

library.title: Adolion: Eshalanore
library.description: A C-rank party out of Aegis City goes north past cursed Alks Forest to bring home two trappers who wrote that they were guests of the elves and would not be coming back. Eshalanore welcomes them warmly. Its princess has been waiting for one of them. Its goddess lets no one leave.

raw.title: Adolion: Eshalanore
raw.description: A C-rank party out of Aegis City goes north past cursed Alks Forest to bring home two trappers who wrote that they were guests of the elves and would not be coming back. Eshalanore welcomes them warmly. Its princess has been waiting for one of them. Its goddess lets no one leave.
raw.player_intro: Widow Holt of Fennmarch has paid every coin she has for a C-rank job out of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild: go north past cursed Alks Forest and bring home her son and daughter, fur trappers who wrote that they were guests of the elves and would not be coming back. This is dark fantasy horror, where dread comes before violence and a kind welcome is not always what it seems. Bring your adventurer as they stand, with Belle and Dalan at your side.

qualities.rubric: What Adventurer's Guild rank does the party hold now, as the story has stated it? Only a rank the Guild has actually given counts, not one the party deserves.

levels.label: unknown: one more new party

qualities.rubric: How does the Adventurer's Guild regard the party right now, going by how Guild staff and other adventurers treat them in the story?

levels.label: unhurt
bruised: scrapes and aches
wounded: real wounds, still fighting fit
badly hurt: someone needs a healer soon

qualities.rubric: How hurt is the worst-off member of the party right now, as the story has shown it?

Has the party left Ashliel's chapel and walked north to the line of mossy shrine stones where Alks Forest ends and the elves' wood begins? Talking about going north, or looking at the stones from the chapel, does not count.
Has the party agreed to go with the elven scouts and started walking into Eshalanore under their escort, on its own feet and armed? Hearing the invitation, or bargaining over it, does not count.
Has the party refused the scouts' escort to court, by saying no, turning back south, or drawing on them? A question, a hesitation or a demand for terms does not count.
Has the party arrived in Eshalanore's stone city, on its paved streets among the stone houses below the castle? Seeing lights through the trees does not count.

Has the party found out that Belle is gone from the castle, her bed empty and nobody able to say where she is? Belle stepping out of the room for a moment, or being out of sight during the feast, does not count.

Does the party know that the missing human women are taken to a grove in the deep forest for a rite tied to the Golden Chalice, and that it happens tonight? A rumour that humans disappear, or that the Lady takes people, does not count without the grove and the rite.
Has the party set out from the stone city into the Thornway, the avenue of black thorn arches that leads into the deep forest? Asking the way does not count.
Has the Green Knight stepped into the Thornway and barred the party's way, so that the standoff or the fight with him has begun? Seeing him in the distance does not count.
Seeded chance: does the Lady of the Forest turn her attention on the party in the Thornway by day?
Has the party got past the Green Knight and come out of the Thornway into the Mothergrove, the clearing round the great tree where the grey stone lies? Glimpsing torchlight ahead does not count.
Has the Lady of the Forest herself appeared in the Mothergrove, in person and seen by the party? A voice, a laugh, a Guardian or a witch speaking for her does not count.

sworn.what: Someone in the party swore an oath to the Lady of the Forest, aloud, and she accepted it and gave them leave to go.
sworn.not_for: A promise she laughed off, a bargain still being haggled, kneeling or begging without an oath, or Elowyn speaking for the heir.
examples: The Lady takes the heir's hand, and the words of the oath go into the grove like a stone into still water; she smiles and says, 'Then go.'
"I swear it," Dalan says, and the yellow flowers in her hair all open at once.

fled.what: The party broke out of the grove without her leave and without beating her, and ran, down the Weeping Run or through the trees, and she let the chase begin.
fled.not_for: Stepping back from her, a retreat that ends somewhere in the grove, or fleeing after the party has already sworn.
examples: Sali shouts 'The water! It's this way!' and the party drops into the black stream under the roots while the Lady laughs behind them.
They run for the Thornway with the witches' thorns in their backs, and she does not follow; she lets the forest do it.

fought.what: The party stood and fought in the grove, against the Lady, her Knight, her Guardians or her witches, and hurt her domain badly enough that she withdrew and let them go.
fought.not_for: One blow struck before running, a threat, or a fight still going on.
examples: Ashliel's golden chains wrap the great tree and hold, the green torches go over and the grove burns, and the Lady steps back into the dark, bored now.
Belle's axe splits the grey stone in two, and the Lady looks at the break a long moment and then lets them go, promising to remember every face.

qualities.rubric: How did the party get out of the Mothergrove alive? Read it from what the Lady did at the end, not from what anyone threatened or hoped. Until she has actually let them go or they are away from her, say nothing about this quality at all.
Did the party leave Eshalanore bound by an oath to the Lady of the Forest, sworn aloud and accepted by her? Escaping her, or a promise she did not accept, does not count.

After the Mothergrove, has the party come out of the elves' wood at its southern edge, where the old trees stop and the black pines of Alks Forest begin? Still being under the old trees does not count.

levels.label: uneasy: something is off and nobody can say what
watched: everyone feels eyes on them
afraid: sleeping in shifts, flinching at kindness
terrified: someone wants to run and cannot
breaking: someone is no longer thinking straight

qualities.rubric: How frightened is the party right now, going by what the story shows them doing: whispering, refusing food, sleeping in shifts, flinching, wanting to run? One scare laughed off does not move it.
