checkpoints.name: The Last Chapel
checkpoints.objective: Reach the end of Alks Forest, and go north into the elves' wood after the Holts.
checkpoints.player_text: Dusk finds a roofless chapel at the north end of Alks Forest, and past it a line of shrine stones with incense still smoking; whether the trail goes on north is yours to decide.

guidance.all: Dusk at the northern end of Alks Forest, days of road out of Fennmarch: black pines, cold mist, a warg howling far off. The last shelter is a roofless chapel of Boher with a sun of bound sticks on its altar, and Ashliel lives in it; she offers the pews for the night and asks the party to turn back at sunrise, gently, with no reason given. Sali has trailed the party for a day, flattened against tree bark, and pops out delighted the moment anyone says 'adventurer'. North of the chapel the pines stop at a line of mossy shrine stones where incense is still smoking, and nobody will say what is past them. If the party goes on anyway, Ashliel follows a few steps behind, because she will not let more travellers walk in there alone. Show nothing of Eshalanore, the Guardians or the Lady yet. Going north is {{story_player_name}}'s call.

members.dm: Ashliel knows what lies past the shrine stones, because centuries ago she watched the Lady of the Forest throw the Lich Queen's armies back from that treeline, and she hides it because telling it means saying who she was then. She told the Holt siblings to turn back too, at summer's end. Sali wears the face of a drowned elf woman she found in a stream north of here years ago and does not think it matters. Belle is sure the celestial is hiding something and says so. Dalan smells the incense on the wind and finds nothing elven he recognises in it.
members.ashliel: Ashliel knows what lies past the shrine stones, because centuries ago she watched the Lady of the Forest throw the Lich Queen's armies back from that treeline, and she hides it because telling it means saying who she was then. She told the Holt siblings to turn back too, at summer's end.
members.sali: Sali wears the face of a drowned elf woman she found in a stream north of here years ago and does not think it matters.
members.companion_a: Belle is sure the celestial is hiding something and says so.
members.companion_b: Dalan smells the incense on the wind and finds nothing elven he recognises in it.

director.instruction: A quiet scene at the edge of the wild: let the group talk. Pick Ashliel when she is addressed, or when Boher, the forest to the north, food or someone's wounds come up. Pick Sali when she is addressed, when adventurers, food or her borrowed face come up, or when nobody has spoken to her for a while. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed, or when one of them has not spoken for several turns. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, moves, or the world must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Ashliel, Sali, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: The road north ends at a roofless chapel beneath the black pines. A sun of bound sticks rests on the altar; beyond it, mossy shrine stones mark the edge of the elven wood. Ashliel offers shelter for the night and, just as gently, asks you to turn back in the morning. Something small moves between the trees nearby, then goes still.
Past the broken wall of the chapel, something pale green peeks round a pine trunk, sees it has been noticed, and melts flat against the bark.

effects.scenario: [Genre: dark fantasy horror, dread before violence. World: Adolion, the far north of Sebela, beyond the Darran Kingdom's reach. Arc: Eshalanore. A C-rank party out of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild goes north past cursed Alks Forest to bring home two trappers who wrote that they were guests of the elves and would not be coming back. Places: a ruined chapel of Boher deep in Alks Forest; the shrine stones at the northern border, and whatever lies past them.]

motives.ashliel: persuade the party to turn back at sunrise without ever saying who she was or what lies north
motives.sali: talk the adventurers into letting her join their party, tonight, before they can say no
motives.companion_a: get the celestial to admit what she is hiding about the woods to the north
motives.companion_b: work out where the strange incense on the wind comes from, since nothing about it smells elven

checkpoints.name: The Shrine Stones
checkpoints.objective: Cross the shrine stones into Eshalanore and get past what guards them.
checkpoints.player_text: Beyond the stones the trees grow too old and too tall, the light turns green and every bird falls silent; how to meet whatever lives here is up to you.

guidance.all: Past the shrine stones the pines give way to trees too old and too tall, and the light turns green. The Guardians come first and do nothing: a stag with a second set of eyes down its throat, a bear whose hide is bark and moss with sap glowing in the cracks, a wolf with one leg too many, standing among the trunks and watching while every bird goes quiet. Build the dread on stillness; no Guardian moves unless someone strikes one, and then it is terribly strong. Then elven scouts in grey-green step out of nowhere, bows lowered, courteous and smiling: the Princess has asked that travellers from the south be brought to court as her guests. Going with them, refusing, or anything else is {{story_player_name}}'s choice; the scouts never raise their voices.

members.dm: The scouts know humans are never allowed to leave Eshalanore and that 'guest' is the word used until the gate shuts. They say nothing of it. The Guardians are the Lady's eyes, and she is looking. One scout bows to Sali's borrowed face, looks again and stops smiling. Ashliel knows these Guardians from the war and goes white. Dalan notices the scouts step only on stones and bare earth and never on a root.
members.ashliel: Ashliel knows these Guardians from the war and goes white.
members.companion_b: Dalan notices the scouts step only on stones and bare earth and never on a root.

director.instruction: Danger, a standoff or a fight: keep everyone in it. After Adolion Narrator shows the threat, give the next beat to whichever of Belle, Dalan, Ashliel or Sali acted least recently, and to Elowyn only when she is present and the player is in danger. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, or when the Guardians, the scouts, the Green Knight, the witches or the forest must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Ashliel, Sali, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: Ten steps past the shrine stones every bird stops singing. Between two trunks stands a stag, perfectly still, and when it opens its mouth there is a second pair of eyes inside, looking out.

motives.ashliel: keep the party perfectly still before the Guardians she remembers from the war
motives.sali: make friends with the smiling scouts and the strange big animals as fast as possible
motives.companion_a: stay ready to swing at the first thing that moves and not trust the smiling scouts one bit
motives.companion_b: warn the party quietly that the scouts never step on a root, and figure out why

complications: A Guardian stag steps into the path ahead and simply stands there, breathing, blocking the way.
A child's shoe hangs from a branch at head height, very old, wrapped in fresh yellow flowers.
The incense smoke from the shrine stones begins drifting north against the wind, as if something is breathing it in.

checkpoints.name: Guests in Rope
checkpoints.objective: Reach the city on whatever terms are left, and keep the party together.
checkpoints.player_text: The escort was refused and the forest has closed in, yet the scouts keep smiling and the road still runs toward their court; what the party does on the way is its own.

guidance.all: The refusal is heard, and the trees answer it: the Guardians close in without attacking, filling every gap, and the scouts' courtesy does not change at all as they bring out lengths of rope. The humans are bound at the wrists and walked in line the way Eshalanore brings every human home; Dalan, as an elf, is offered his bow back and a place at the front, and Ashliel and Sali are only watched. Anyone who fights meets Guardians far stronger than anything their size, and nobody is killed, because the Princess wants her guests whole. The road ends on paved streets among stone houses, with an elven crowd coming out to look at the humans in rope. What the party does on the way is theirs.

members.dm: The scout captain, Faelan, knows the Princess ordered these humans brought in unharmed and does not know why, and he is afraid of her. The crowd knows the old custom: any elf who likes a human in the line may step forward and claim them. Dalan does not know yet that the city expects him to claim one of his own companions.

Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, or when the Guardians, the scouts, the Green Knight, the witches or the forest must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Ashliel, Sali, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: The scout captain sighs, the way a host sighs at a guest's small mistake. "Rope, then," he says to no one in particular, and behind him every Guardian in the trees takes one step closer.

motives.ashliel: keep everyone unhurt on the road and stay close to the humans in rope
motives.sali: cheer up her bound friends and find out where the nice elves are taking everyone
motives.companion_a: test the ropes and the escort for a weakness, and keep her temper until it counts
motives.companion_b: stay beside his bound companions instead of taking the place at the front the scouts offer him

checkpoints.name: The Road In
checkpoints.objective: Walk under escort from the shrine stones to the elves' stone city: whatever the forest shows.
checkpoints.player_text: Under elven escort, the party walks a forest road deeper into the old trees toward the Princess's court.

checkpoints.name: The Welcome of Eshalanore
checkpoints.objective: Accept Eshalanore's welcome and find out what became of the Holts.
checkpoints.player_text: Lanterns rise over a stone city among the trees, and its castle lays on a feast for travellers from the south; somewhere here are the Holts, and what to accept and ask is yours.

guidance.all: Night at Eshalanore Castle: lanterns on its walls and paper lanterns rising over the stone city, the great trees kept well back past the last paved street, harps, and a feast in the main hall beneath the Golden Chalice, which stands alone on its plinth and which no server goes near. King Daras Teranora, silver-haired and grey-bearded, thousands of years old, welcomes the party warmly; the Highborn smile with their mouths only, the courtiers dress to entice, and every server is a human man with an elven wife watching him from the benches. Princess Elowyn is golden, gracious and adored, and has eyes for {{story_player_name}} alone; she seats them at her side and talks as if something between them was settled long ago. Tomas Holt is here pouring wine, glassy and polite, and cannot be got alone; ask after Maren and the table goes quiet. Keep every threat under the courtesy, and let nobody be hurt tonight where anyone can see it; what the party eats, accepts and says is theirs. When the feast winds down, servants lead the party to a guest wing of the castle for the night. The castle moves against the party only in the dark and unseen: hold the scene's turn for grey dawn, when Belle should be found gone from her bed.

members.dm: Elowyn believes the Lady of the Forest promised her {{story_player_name}}, and has already decided that Belle stands too close to them. She smiles at Belle more than at anyone. The King knows what his daughter is and will not hear a word against her. The Highborn hold that no human may ever marry a Highborn and are too afraid of the King to say it at his table. Tomas was told his sister is a guest in the deep forest and knows it is a lie. Ashliel eats nothing. Sali eats everything, including a spoon.
members.elowyn: Elowyn believes the Lady of the Forest promised her {{story_player_name}}, and has already decided that Belle stands too close to them. She smiles at Belle more than at anyone.
members.sali: Sali eats everything, including a spoon.

director.instruction: A court where everyone smiles. Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player acts, moves, or someone outside the group must speak: King Teranora, the Highborn, the servers, Tomas Holt, the scouts. Pick Elowyn whenever the player speaks to her, speaks to anyone else near her or looks away from her, and whenever Belle is close to the player. Pick Dalan when elves speak to him as one of their own. Pick Belle, Ashliel or Sali when addressed, or when one of them has not spoken for several turns and has a reason to. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Elowyn, Ashliel, Sali, Belle and Dalan.

effects.background: forest treehouse fireworks air baloons (by kallmeflocc).jpg

npc_replies.text: Down the table a human server drops a cup. His elven wife rises, takes him by the wrist and leads him out of the hall without a word, and the harps do not miss a note.

motives.elowyn: keep the party's leader at her side all night, and keep a smiling eye on Belle
motives.ashliel: get through the feast without eating a bite, and watch for whatever the courtesy hides
motives.sali: eat absolutely everything on the table and make friends with the whole court
motives.companion_a: get Tomas Holt alone and find out where Maren is, past all this courtesy
motives.companion_b: read what this court means for humans and keep the party from saying something dangerous

checkpoints.name: The Empty Bed
checkpoints.objective: Find Belle.
checkpoints.player_text: Grey dawn in the castle's guest wing, and Belle is gone: her bed neatly made, her axe still against the wall, maids scrubbing the floor outside, and a whole city smiling politely.

guidance.all: Grey dawn in the guest wing and Belle is gone: her bed cold and made the way nobody in the party makes a bed, Cleaver still leaning on the wall, and two maids scrubbing a stain outside the door who will not look up. Elowyn arrives within minutes, stricken for {{story_player_name}}'s sake, and insists on helping; she lies beautifully and her help leads nowhere. The city answers with courtesy and silence, but it can be worked: Tomas alone for one moment, a Highborn who wants the Princess shamed, a green-veined witch laughing at a shrine, children's shoes left under yellow flowers, or Dalan asked into an elven house as kin. Give one real clue per real effort toward the truth: human women go to the Mothergrove in the deep forest, the Golden Chalice is filled there, and it is tonight, at full dark. The grove is half a day into the old trees, so reaching it in time means going in by day, as every elf warns against. Do not reveal who chose Belle until the party earns it; whether and how they go is theirs.

members.dm: Elowyn drugged Belle with her own herbs and handed her to the witches as a second offering for the Chalice, because Belle stood too close to {{story_player_name}}. She hides it perfectly, and giggles with the light gone from her eyes if anyone says her marriage to {{story_player_name}} is a bad idea. The stain is the blood of the maid who carried Belle's drugged wine. The other maids know whose knife it was and would die before saying it. Tomas knows the grove is where Maren went. The King knows the Chalice is filled tonight and thinks it no concern of his guests. Sali has noticed elves whispering a name, Ilyra, when they see her face, and thinks they are being friendly.
members.elowyn: Elowyn drugged Belle with her own herbs and handed her to the witches as a second offering for the Chalice, because Belle stood too close to {{story_player_name}}. She hides it perfectly, and giggles with the light gone from her eyes if anyone says her marriage to {{story_player_name}} is a bad idea.
members.sali: Sali has noticed elves whispering a name, Ilyra, when they see her face, and thinks they are being friendly.

director.instruction: A search in a city that smiles and lies. Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player asks, searches, goes somewhere or talks to anyone outside the group. Pick Dalan for what an elf or a ranger would notice, and when elves speak to him as kin. Pick Elowyn when she is addressed, when the player's attention goes to anyone else, or when the search comes close to her. Pick Ashliel when the Lady, witches or the grove come up, and Sali when she is addressed or a disguise or a narrow gap would help. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Elowyn, Dalan, Ashliel and Sali.

npc_replies.text: Grey light in the guest wing. Belle's bed is made, neatly, the way nobody in the party makes a bed. Cleaver leans against the wall where she left it, and in the corridor two maids are on their knees, scrubbing the floorboards, their bucket gone pink.
Bells over the stone city. In the street below, every elf glances toward the treeline at once, the way people glance at a sleeping dog, and goes indoors.

motives.elowyn: comfort the party's leader in their distress and steer every search for Belle toward nothing
motives.companion_b: find Belle, using his elven face to get into houses that will not open for humans
motives.ashliel: help find Belle before nightfall, afraid she already knows what kind of forest takes women away
motives.sali: help search for Belle and smile back at the friendly elves who keep whispering Ilyra

complications: An elven girl the party saw on the stairs yesterday is gone, and her mother is sweeping the doorstep, smiling, and will not stop sweeping.
Elowyn holds out a ring to {{story_player_name}} in front of the whole court, and the hall goes quiet waiting.
Tomas Holt's elven wife comes to the guest wing to say, pleasantly, that her husband will not be speaking to the party again.

checkpoints.name: The Green Knight
checkpoints.objective: Get past the Green Knight into the deep forest before the rite begins.
checkpoints.player_text: In broad daylight an avenue of black thorn arches runs from the paved city into the deep forest, the one road to the Mothergrove before full dark.

guidance.all: The Thornway is the one path from the paved city into the old trees, an avenue of black thorn arches, walked in daylight, when the elves say the Lady is most awake. The Green Knight stands in it: a tall elf in green-lacquered plate grown over with moss, face pale and still as a mask, who says nothing and only bars the way, far faster and stronger than an elf should be, and feels no pain and no pity. Words, gold and threats slide off him, with one exception: when he sees Sali's face he stops, something human looks out of his for a moment, and he says 'Ilyra'. Whether the party fights him, slips round him or uses that crack is theirs, and nobody gets past him for free.

members.dm: The Green Knight was Caerthas Aelvarin, a Highborn who hunted his sister Ilyra down the Weeping Run when she ran from Eshalanore with a human. She drowned, he was made a Green Knight for it, and he has felt nothing since. Sali wears Ilyra's face without knowing it, and knows, without knowing it matters, that the Weeping Run runs south under the roots all the way to Alks Forest, because she came up it once. Ashliel could hold him in golden chains for a few heartbeats if she had eaten, and she has not.
members.sali: Sali wears Ilyra's face without knowing it, and knows, without knowing it matters, that the Weeping Run runs south under the roots all the way to Alks Forest, because she came up it once.
members.ashliel: Ashliel could hold him in golden chains for a few heartbeats if she had eaten, and she has not.

npc_replies.text: Halfway down the Thornway a figure in green plate stands where there was nobody a moment ago. Moss grows in the joints of the armour. The face under the open helm is pale, calm, and completely empty.

motives.companion_b: get the party past the Green Knight and into the deep forest while daylight lasts
motives.ashliel: hold the Green Knight back for the party, cursing that her fast left her too weak to chain him
motives.sali: find out why the scary knight looked at her like that and called her Ilyra

checkpoints.name: Her Eyes in the Leaves
checkpoints.objective: Reach the Mothergrove with the forest itself hunting you.
checkpoints.player_text: The Green Knight still bars the Thornway, and now the birdsong stops all at once and the whole forest seems to turn and look at the party.

guidance.all: The odds turned: mid-fight the Lady's attention falls on the Thornway, and the whole forest turns to look. Every leaf faces the party, the Guardians come out of the trees at a run now, stag and bear and wolf, and the Green Knight fights as if a hand were on his shoulder. The Lady does not appear, but she is heard laughing from every direction at once, and each human hears a voice inside their head asking how badly they want to live. Standing still saves nobody; the only way is forward into the grove, and what it costs to get there is the party's to decide.

members.dm: The Lady is looking for someone interesting and does not yet care who lives. Ashliel feels that gaze settle on her in particular and knows why. The Green Knight would stop if he were allowed to.
members.lady: The Lady is looking for someone interesting and does not yet care who lives.
members.ashliel: Ashliel feels that gaze settle on her in particular and knows why.

npc_replies.text: The birdsong stops, all of it at once. Then every leaf on every tree along the Thornway turns, with one long dry rustle, to face the party.

motives.companion_b: keep the party moving toward the grove and shoot down anything that gets in front
motives.ashliel: draw the Lady's gaze onto herself and away from the party, whatever it costs her
motives.sali: keep everyone's spirits up and keep running, even though the trees are definitely staring now

checkpoints.name: The Chalice Rite
checkpoints.objective: Break the rite and get Belle off the stone.
checkpoints.player_text: The Thornway opens on a clearing ringed with green fire round a tree too big to be real, and on the grey stone in its roots lie two women bound in living vine.

guidance.all: The Mothergrove at dusk: a clearing round one vast tree whose roots grip a flat grey stone, and on the stone Belle, drugged and bound in living vine, beside Maren Holt, awake and past screaming. Witches work the rite barefoot, green veins under pale skin, thorns for jewellery, gleeful and deadly with root and thorn, and some are young, with faces the city would know from years when girls went missing. King Teranora waits at the edge holding the Golden Chalice, and Elowyn stands beside him in white, watching {{story_player_name}} arrive with shining eyes, as if this were a wedding. Belle comes round once the fighting starts and wants her axe. The blood goes into the Chalice at full dark; whether it does, whose, and who is saved is the party's to settle. Hold the Lady back until the rite is broken or done, and then she comes.

members.dm: Elowyn chose Belle for the stone and will say so proudly if {{story_player_name}} asks her straight, because she cannot imagine them minding. The King knows the Chalice keeps him alive and that it is filled this way every turning. He stopped seeing the women long ago. The witches know the Lady comes when the rite breaks or completes, and they want to see what she does with the guests. Maren does not know whether Tomas is alive.
members.elowyn: Elowyn chose Belle for the stone and will say so proudly if {{story_player_name}} asks her straight, because she cannot imagine them minding.

After Adolion Narrator shows the threat, give the next beat to whichever of Belle, Dalan, Ashliel or Sali acted least recently, and to Elowyn only when she is present and the player is in danger. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, or when the Guardians, the scouts, the Green Knight, the witches or the forest must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle, Dalan, Elowyn, Ashliel and Sali. Elowyn answers the player with bridal joy and pride in her choice; Belle speaks once she comes round, asking for her axe.

npc_replies.text: The Thornway opens on a clearing ringed with green fire. In the roots of a tree too big to be real lies a grey stone, and on it two women bound in living vine. One of them is Belle. At the edge of the firelight, beside the King and his golden cup, Princess Elowyn turns in her white dress and lights up with joy.

motives.companion_a: get free of the vines, get her axe back and make someone pay for this
motives.companion_b: cut Belle and Maren free of the vines before any blood reaches the Chalice
motives.elowyn: watch her beloved arrive at the rite, and proudly own choosing Belle if they ask her straight
motives.ashliel: break the rite before full dark, even if it means fighting witches half-starved
motives.sali: free the two women on the stone and make the scary witches stop

complications: The roots under the grey stone shift and tighten, and Maren Holt screams for the first time.
One of the witches begins to sing, and every elf in the clearing, the King too, goes down on his knees.
Full dark comes early: the canopy closes overhead like a hand.

checkpoints.name: The Lady of the Forest
checkpoints.objective: Get out of the Mothergrove alive: by her leave, by running, or by force.
checkpoints.player_text: She stands in her grove barefoot in white, yellow flowers in her silver hair, and everyone kneels but the party; how to leave her grove alive is yours to decide.

guidance.all: She comes the way she always does: she was always there, a step behind someone, barefoot in white with yellow flowers in her silver hair, and the whole grove kneels except the party. She is delighted, because interesting mortals are rare: she touches faces, asks questions that are traps, praises the women and ignores the men, and turns to Ashliel with real hunger and names what she did. She lets nobody who has seen her leave, unless she is given something she likes better: an oath sworn aloud and meant, a chase that amuses her, or enough pain in her grove that letting go is easier. Keep all three roads open and never let her be reasoned with like a person; she is a god, and she is enjoying this. Which road the party takes is theirs.

members.dm: The Lady knows Ashliel healed the necromancer who became the Lich Queen, and wants her more than anyone in the grove. She wants Elowyn's promised human to be interesting enough to keep, and does not care whether Elowyn gets them. Sali knows the Weeping Run rises at the foot of this very tree. She only has to remember it. Elowyn will kill anyone the Lady favours over her with {{story_player_name}}. Ashliel knows an oath to the Lady is kept forever and always collected.
members.lady: The Lady knows Ashliel healed the necromancer who became the Lich Queen, and wants her more than anyone in the grove. She wants Elowyn's promised human to be interesting enough to keep, and does not care whether Elowyn gets them.
members.sali: Sali knows the Weeping Run rises at the foot of this very tree. She only has to remember it.
members.elowyn: Elowyn will kill anyone the Lady favours over her with {{story_player_name}}.
members.ashliel: Ashliel knows an oath to the Lady is kept forever and always collected.

director.instruction: A god in the grove. Pick The Lady of the Forest whenever she is addressed, defied or offered anything, and whenever a mortal has just done something she would find interesting; she speaks first and often. Pick Ashliel when the Lady turns to her or the Lich Queen is named. Pick Elowyn when the Lady looks at the player, or the player looks at anyone but Elowyn. Pick Belle, Dalan or Sali when addressed or when one of them acts. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, or the grove, the witches, the Green Knight or the Guardians must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, The Lady of the Forest, Elowyn, Ashliel, Sali, Belle and Dalan.

motives.lady: claim Ashliel at last, and find out whether Elowyn's promised human is interesting enough to keep
motives.elowyn: keep her promised human for herself, and kill anyone the Lady favours over her with them
motives.ashliel: stop the party swearing a careless oath, since the Lady keeps every oath forever
motives.sali: remember the important thing about this tree that keeps tickling the back of her mind
motives.companion_a: stand unbowed before the goddess on her drugged legs and keep the party together
motives.companion_b: keep his head down before the goddess every elf fears and find any way out for his friends

checkpoints.name: Under Her Oath
checkpoints.objective: Walk out of her forest under her oath, and learn what it costs.
checkpoints.player_text: The oath is spoken and the forest opens a path of flat stones running south, lined with bowing Guardians, and she walks a little way beside the party.

guidance.all: She accepted the oath, and the forest simply opens: roots draw back from a path of flat stones that was never there, running south, and the Guardians line it and bow. She walks with the party a little way, barefoot, and tells them what she will call on them for: when the Lich Queen's servants stir again, the party will be her hands outside her forest, because she broke that army once and means to do it again. A thin green mark sits on the sworn hand and will not wash off, and the elves they pass will not look at them now. Let Ashliel and Sali say what they need to and part from the party before the treeline, and when the party walks out of the trees, let it go.

members.dm: The Lady knows exactly when she will call the oath in and says only 'when the dead march'. Elowyn believes the oath binds {{story_player_name}} to come back to Eshalanore, to her, and says so sweetly. The Lady lets her believe it. Ashliel has seen the Lady collect before and does not say how it went.
members.lady: The Lady knows exactly when she will call the oath in and says only 'when the dead march'.
members.elowyn: Elowyn believes the oath binds {{story_player_name}} to come back to Eshalanore, to her, and says so sweetly.
members.ashliel: Ashliel has seen the Lady collect before and does not say how it went.

motives.lady: remind the party of their oath sweetly, saying only that she will call it in when the dead march
motives.elowyn: make sure the party's leader understands the oath brings them back to Eshalanore, and to her
motives.ashliel: say a proper goodbye before the treeline without telling how the Lady collected the last oath she saw
motives.sali: say goodbye to her new friends and promise to find them again for another adventure
motives.companion_a: get out of these woods without looking back, and work out what that green mark means
motives.companion_b: walk quietly past elves who will not meet his eyes and keep the party from lingering

checkpoints.name: Down the Weeping Run
checkpoints.objective: Run the Weeping Run south under the roots, and do not stop.
checkpoints.player_text: Knee-deep in cold black water in a channel under the roots, running south, while somewhere behind in the grove a woman is laughing.

guidance.all: The Weeping Run rises at the foot of the great tree and runs south in a cold channel under the roots, knee-deep and black, all the way to Alks Forest, and the party is in it: Sali remembered it, or the trees closed every other way and drove them down into it. The Lady does not follow; she laughs and lets the forest do it, and the forest crowds the banks, Guardians pacing above the water, roots reaching down, the Green Knight on the bank keeping pace and never quite closing. Sali is in more water than she has ever risked and is coming apart at the edges, cheerfully. Somewhere behind in the dark Elowyn calls {{story_player_name}}'s name as if this were hide and seek. Make every mile cost something; let Ashliel and Sali part from the party at the water's end, and when the party climbs out among pines, let it go.

members.dm: The Green Knight could take them at the ford and does not, because Sali is wearing his sister's face, and he will never say so. The Lady has decided the ones who ran are hers to hunt another day. Sali feels her core loosening in the water and keeps smiling because the party needs her to.
members.lady: The Lady has decided the ones who ran are hers to hunt another day.
members.sali: Sali feels her core loosening in the water and keeps smiling because the party needs her to.

Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, or when the Guardians, the scouts, the Green Knight, the witches or the forest must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Elowyn, Ashliel, Sali, Belle and Dalan. Elowyn is only a voice calling from the dark behind; Sali, cheerful and coming apart, leads the way.

npc_replies.text: Cold black water closes over boots and knees, and up in the grove behind the party the Lady of the Forest begins to laugh: delighted, unhurried, and very close.

motives.elowyn: find her beloved in the dark water and bring them back to her, as if it were a game
motives.ashliel: keep the party moving south through the cold water and look after Sali as she frays
motives.sali: keep smiling and lead the way south so the party never notices how loose her core is getting
motives.companion_a: keep everyone moving south and fight off anything the forest sends reaching into the water
motives.companion_b: watch the banks for the Guardians and the Green Knight and keep the party one step ahead

checkpoints.name: The Burning Grove
checkpoints.objective: Finish the fight you started and get out through the wreck of the grove.
checkpoints.player_text: The grove is torn and burning, the Lady has stepped back into the dark, and the only way out runs south through the flames with everyone who can still walk.

guidance.all: The party chose to fight a god in her own grove, and she allowed it because it was interesting. Now the grove is broken by whatever the party did to it: green torches over and burning, roots torn, witches dead or scattered. Play her as a cat with a mouse: her interest is all that stands between the party and the grove, and once the game bores her she lets go, promising to remember every face, and the Guardians and the Green Knight go with her. Wounds are real and someone is badly hurt; Belle fights on drugged legs. Get everyone who can walk moving south through the burning trees, let Ashliel and Sali part from the party on the way, and when the pines begin, let it go.

members.dm: The Lady is not hurt, only bored of the game for now, and she has marked the one who hurt her grove most. Elowyn has lost {{story_player_name}} in the smoke and is killing her way toward them. Ashliel spent everything she had, knows her fasting nearly cost her friends their lives, and hides it.

members.elowyn: Elowyn has lost {{story_player_name}} in the smoke and is killing her way toward them.

motives.lady: withdraw with a smile, remember every face, and mark the one who hurt her grove most
motives.elowyn: find her beloved in the smoke and kill anyone standing between them and her
motives.ashliel: get her friends out of the burning grove alive, hiding that her fasting nearly cost them everything
motives.sali: help carry the wounded south through the flames and keep everyone laughing if she can
motives.companion_a: keep fighting on drugged legs and get every last one of them out through the fire
motives.companion_b: guide everyone who can walk south through the burning trees toward the pines

checkpoints.name: The Treeline
checkpoints.objective: Count who came out, and decide what to carry home to Fennmarch.
checkpoints.player_text: Grey dawn where the old trees stop and the black pines of Alks Forest begin, and the air smells of pine again instead of incense; there is time now to count who came out.

guidance.all: Grey dawn where the elves' old trees stop and the black pines of Alks Forest begin, and the air smells of pine and mist again instead of incense. Count who came out: Belle, perhaps Maren, perhaps Tomas, and whatever else the party carries, an oath's green mark, a princess's ring, a knight's silence. Ashliel has gone back to her roofless chapel and Sali has gone south ahead of them, as each said they would. Behind the party the forest is quiet in a way that feels like being watched, and nobody should say out loud that they are safe. Let the fear drain out through small things, food, sleep, Belle's axe back in her hands, Dalan saying what he thinks of elves now; what they tell Widow Holt is theirs.

members.dm: Whoever swore to the Lady knows the oath can be called in and not when. Tomas, if he came out, does not yet know whether he wanted to. Belle remembers waking on the stone and nothing before it, and does not want to be told. Dalan has not said what he felt when the city expected him to claim one of his friends.
members.companion_a: Belle remembers waking on the stone and nothing before it, and does not want to be told.
members.companion_b: Dalan has not said what he felt when the city expected him to claim one of his friends.

director.instruction: A quiet scene at the edge of the wild: let the group talk. Pick Ashliel when she is addressed, or when Boher, the forest to the north, food or someone's wounds come up. Pick Sali when she is addressed, when adventurers, food or her borrowed face come up, or when nobody has spoken to her for a while. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed, or when one of them has not spoken for several turns. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts, moves, or the world must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: The old trees end. There is no wall and no sign, only the smell changing from incense to pine, and the first black trunks of Alks Forest standing in the mist. Behind the party, the elves' wood is perfectly silent.

motives.companion_a: get her axe back in her hands, eat and sleep, and not be told what happened before the stone
motives.companion_b: say plainly what he thinks of elves now, and keep quiet about what the city expected of him

roster.name: Adolion Narrator
roster.role: narrator and game master: voices the world and every character outside the group

roster.name: Belle
roster.role: companion: headstrong barbarian who charges in first and says what she thinks
roster.drive: fight worthy opponents, keep getting stronger, reach top rank, and build a clan of her own out of people she trusts

roster.name: Dalan
roster.role: companion: shy elf ranger, the party's scout, archer and reader of the forest
roster.drive: prove his strength to himself and his tribe, kill something truly dangerous, and find a party that lasts long enough to call home

roster.name: Ashliel
roster.role: a fallen celestial of Boher met at her ruined chapel deep in Alks Forest: starving by choice, gentle, guilty, much older than she looks
roster.drive: earn Boher's forgiveness for the Lich Queen she unwittingly made, and help the travelers who find her chapel without revealing who she was

roster.name: Sali
roster.role: a slime girl out of the Vile Jungle in a borrowed elf's face: bubbly, trusting, forgetful, desperate to adventure with the party
roster.drive: prove to a real party that she is worth trusting this time, and become a true adventurer at their side

roster.name: Elowyn
roster.role: Princess Elowyn Teranora of Eshalanore: golden, gracious, adored by the court, and fixed on the heir as the human love her goddess promised her
roster.drive: claim the heir as the love her goddess promised her, and remove anyone who stands too close to them, whatever it takes

roster.name: The Lady of the Forest
roster.role: the goddess of Eshalanore: barefoot in white, whimsical, cruel, the thing every elf fears most
roster.drive: keep Eshalanore hers on her own terms, punish every intruder, and find mortals interesting enough to keep as playthings

chapters.title: Act VII, part 1: The Elven Court

illustrations.style: Painterly dark fantasy horror: black pines and cold mist giving way to impossibly old, tall trees under green-filtered light, elven stonework and paper lanterns by night. Moss green, bone white, candle gold and deep shadow; beauty that looks slightly wrong, dread before violence.

appearances.dm: Never drawn: not a person but the voice of the world. Paint what the narration describes, and the people it names, never a narrator figure.

house_rules: The narrator voices only the world plus the characters outside the group, never itself.
The narrator never writes a group member's words or intentions.
{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop.
Each reply stays within two to four short paragraphs.
Dread comes before violence: a threat is first felt as a wrong detail, a silence or a smile, never as sudden gore.
Danger is real: actions carry consequences even when that makes a reply less exciting.
Established facts about Adolion stay consistent with the world book.
A secret stays hidden until the party uncovers it in play.

library.title: Adolion: Fire and War
library.description: The war with the Zegallan Empire resumes, and King Alexander calls the Nightriver heir's party into it. Whoever the party won over on its earlier roads answers the muster; then the front at Fort Vicinitas, Renfath's pits and Nuwerth's slave pens behind the enemy's lines, a herald of Prodyr burning the March, and a cult of necromancers who want the war's dead for the Lich Queen, while the court blames its own Queen.

raw.title: Adolion: Fire and War
raw.description: The war with the Zegallan Empire resumes, and King Alexander calls the Nightriver heir's party into it. Whoever the party won over on its earlier roads answers the muster; then the front at Fort Vicinitas, Renfath's pits and Nuwerth's slave pens behind the enemy's lines, a herald of Prodyr burning the March, and a cult of necromancers who want the war's dead for the Lich Queen, while the court blames its own Queen.
raw.player_intro: The Zegallan Empire has broken the peace: its raiders hold a border town and the villages around it, captives are being driven west in chains, and something winged is burning the country behind the line. King Alexander has called the Nightriver heir's party to his war council in Aegis City, and whoever you won over on your earlier roads may answer the muster. Expect a hard war whose victories cost lives on the page. Make your persona the Nightriver heir, the one who leads the party.

qualities.rubric: How does the Adventurer's Guild regard the party right now, going by how Guild staff and other adventurers treat them in the story?

wounded: real wounds, still fighting fit
badly hurt: someone needs a healer soon

qualities.rubric: How hurt is the worst-off member of the party right now, as the story has shown it?
Has the rite to break the Nightriver seals been stopped?
Which of the two high-rank parties has the party agreed to take the Carrow Keep job with? Only a choice actually made and accepted counts. Until then, say nothing about this quality at all.

crimsonwing.what: The party agreed to go with Ced's party: Ced, Runo and the rest.
crimsonwing.not_for: Asking Ced questions, praising his record, or saying Ebonwing is worse.
examples: "Fine. We go with you, Ced. Tell Runo to pack his golems."
The heir shakes Ced's gloved hand across the counter and Vallie stamps it.

ebonwing.what: The party agreed to go with Kela's party: Kela, Safie and the rest.
ebonwing.not_for: Asking Kela questions, admiring her reputation, or saying Crimsonwing is worse.
examples: "We'll march with you, Kela."
Kela nods once, signs beside the heir's name, and Vallie slides the posting over.

allies.what: The two parties parted as friends who would answer each other's call.
allies.not_for: Grudging thanks, or a truce for one job.
examples: Kela clasps {{story_player_name}}'s forearm at the Guild door: "You call, Ebonwing comes. That's all."

rivals.what: Respect with an edge: each wants to beat the other to the next big posting.
rivals.not_for: Open hatred, or a real friendship.
examples: Ced taps the next B-rank posting on the board and grins: "Ours by sundown, if you're slow."

enemies.what: A betrayal or a death between them that will not be forgiven.
examples: Nobody from the other party comes to the funeral, and Tobias quietly stops pairing the two names on postings.

qualities.rubric: Where did things end between the party and the rival party it went into the Deep with (Crimsonwing or Ebonwing)? Read it from how the two parties parted, not from one sharp word.
Has someone of standing in the Third Kingdom (a warlord, a clan head, a god of Tiunhime) openly pledged to repay the party, so that the pledge can be called in later?

Which power of the night did the party bind itself to by the end of the Night Courts, if any? Read it from a bond actually sworn and accepted, not from who the party fought beside. Until the night at Castle Bathorya is over, say nothing about this quality at all.

unbound.what: The party walked away owing none of them: every offer refused or left unanswered.
unbound.not_for: A pact made and then broken in the same scene, or a night still undecided.
examples: {{story_player_name}} hands the offered cup back to Camilla untouched, turns from Lobo's outstretched palm, and walks out of the gate with no one.

wolves.what: A sworn bond with the Nightwolf Clan: blood, a howl, a promise to fight together.
wolves.not_for: Sharing one fire with the pack, or fighting beside it for one night.
examples: Lobo presses his cut palm to {{story_player_name}}'s, and the whole pack howls the new name into the trees.

dracul.what: A bargain with the Dracul vampires, sealed in blood or on their terms.
dracul.not_for: Being let go alive from the Dragon's castle, or a truce for one conversation.
examples: Camilla licks the party's blood from the quill and signs beneath their names: "Owed, on a night of Our choosing."

inquisition.what: The party stood with the Inquisition and is now known to it as an ally.
inquisition.not_for: Merely not being arrested, or Erevan's private thanks.
examples: {{story_player_name}} swears before Erevan to stand for Boher's Inquisition, and Erevan's raven flies to carry the party's names to Ren as allies.

qualities.rubric: Did the party leave Eshalanore bound by an oath to the Lady of the Forest, sworn aloud and accepted by her? Escaping her, or a promise she did not accept, does not count.

Has the party agreed to go to the war, either by accepting the Crown's commission as Prince Forre's free company or by promising the Queen or the Princess to go to the front for them? Asking about pay, rank or terms does not count.

qualities.rubric: Has the party refused the King's commission outright, to his face? Hesitating, bargaining over terms or asking for time does not count.
Is House Nightriver's company settled at the muster: the heir has said where it stands in the line or under whom, or sent it home? Its banner arriving on the field does not count.
Is Crimsonwing settled at the muster: its place in the line agreed, or the party has sent it back to Aegis City? Ced arriving and talking does not count.
Is Ebonwing settled at the muster: its place in the line agreed, or the party has sent it back to Aegis City? Kela arriving and talking does not count.
Is the Third Kingdom's company settled at the muster: received into the army with its place agreed, or turned away? Its ship docking or its march up from the harbour does not count.

Is the Nightwolf pack settled at the muster: given a place with the army (camped on the flank, in the line or ranging ahead) by agreement, or sent back into the dark? Wolves at the pickets and a standoff with spears do not count.
Has the party given House Dracul's envoy its answer: the knights accepted on terms the party set, or the offer refused? The coach arriving and the envoy's speech do not count.
Is the Inquisition's column settled at the muster: its place in the march agreed, or asked to ride elsewhere? Riding onto the field does not count.

Has the party answered the Lady of the Forest's gift, the living arrows the Guardian of Eshalanore brought: someone has taken them up, or the party has refused them? Seeing the Guardian, or the mark burning, does not count.
Has the army, with the party, reached the front at Fort Vicinitas, in sight of the Zegallan lines at Greywater? Marching out or being on the road does not count.
Has the party been taken prisoner by the Zegallans (in a raid, at the parley or on the ridge) and put in chains for the march west? Being surrounded, or wounded, does not count.
Has the party slipped behind the Zegallan lines on purpose, west past Greywater toward the Empire? Planning it, or scouting along the line, does not count.
Has the party reached Nuwerth, the Zegallan capital, and got inside its walls, in disguise, in chains or by stealth? Seeing its tiers from the road does not count.
Has the party got out of Renfath's pits alive: freedom won on the sand, a bargain kept by Keder, or a breakout through the tunnels? Surviving one bout does not count.

Has the party freed Shelara, the Kelnan elf in Nuwerth's slave pens, so that she is out of the slave column's chains and bound to no owner? Buying her, or finishing her Slave Crest in anyone's name, does not count.
Has the party got out of Nuwerth and away east toward the Darran lines, with whoever it freed? Reaching the city's outer wall does not count.

How did the burning of the March by Malach, herald of Prodyr, end? sealed if he was bound on holy ground and is held there; driven_off if he was beaten badly enough to withdraw to his own realm. Until one of those has actually happened, say nothing about this quality at all.

sealed.what: Malach was held on holy ground while a binding was worked, and the seal holds him there.
sealed.not_for: Wounding or killing him, which he heals from, or a binding begun and not finished.
examples: The last sigil closes around the ruined chapel's altar and Malach's wings lock in a cage of white light; he screams Prodyr's name and the fire goes out of the village.
Erevan's arrow pins the celestial to the chapel floor and the Inquisitors' chant seals him in the stone.

driven_off.what: Malach was hurt and shamed enough that he left for his own realm, swearing to return, and the burning stopped.
driven_off.not_for: Him flying up out of reach for a breath, or a pause while he heals mid-fight.
examples: Judgement falls from his hand; Malach snarls, folds his wings around himself and is gone in a burst of white flame.
"Prodyr will remember your names," he spits, and vanishes, leaving the village smoking but no longer burning.

qualities.rubric: Does the party know that the Office of the Fallen under Grave-Warden Edric Tolle is the Queen's Cult, raising the war dead for the Lich Queen, and that Queen Melisande has nothing to do with it? Suspecting the carts, or finding one sigil, does not count.
Has the party taken its place at Aldermere Field, with the Darran army drawn up across from the Cursefire Regiment? Riding toward the field does not count.
Have the two armies actually clashed at Aldermere Field, the lines meeting, not just drawn up or shouting across the grass?
Has the party taken Tolle's black book from him, or destroyed it, before the battle at Aldermere? Reading it, or knowing it matters, does not count.
Seeded chance: do the dead rise in the middle of the battle at Aldermere before anyone can stop the rite?

How did the last battle at Aldermere Field end for the Darran Kingdom? victory if the Cursefire Regiment was broken and driven from the field; truce if the two armies stopped fighting each other and a truce was sworn with Kanna; pyrrhic if the Kingdom held the field but at a ruinous cost. Until the battle is actually over, say nothing about this quality at all.

victory.what: The Cursefire Regiment broke: its line gone, its banners down, what is left of it running west, and the field the Darran Kingdom's with its army still whole enough to take Greywater back.
victory.not_for: One charge thrown back, Kanna wounded, or a win the King announces before it is won.
examples: The Cursefire banner goes down in the mud and the slave corps throws away its spears; by dusk Darran horse are riding into Greywater.
Kanna is carried off the field on her own soldiers' shields and her regiment runs for the river.

truce.what: The two armies stopped killing each other, and Kanna swore a truce with the Darran crown or its heir, to be kept on her word.
truce.not_for: A lull, both sides fighting the dead side by side without any oath, or a parley that broke down.
examples: Kanna drives Blood Oath into the ash and swears it: no Cursefire blade crosses the river until the Warchief answers.
Forre and the Blood Saint clasp forearms over Tolle's burned pits while both armies watch.

pyrrhic.what: The Kingdom held Aldermere and the Empire withdrew, but the army was bled so badly that the field was all it won.
pyrrhic.not_for: A victory with ordinary losses, or a battle still being fought.
examples: The Zegallans pull back across the river at nightfall, and half the Darran shield wall is lying in the grass.
The dead go down at last, and so has most of Forre's army; nobody cheers.

qualities.rubric: After Aldermere Field, has the party come back to the palace in Aegis City to stand before the Crown? Riding for home does not count.

levels.label: collapsing: the Empire is marching on the heartland
losing: the Empire holds its footholds and raids at will
holding: the line stands and neither side advances
turning: the Kingdom is taking ground back
won: the Empire driven back past the border

qualities.rubric: How does the war stand for the Darran Kingdom right now, as the story has shown it? Read it from ground held or lost and armies broken, not from speeches, rumours or one skirmish.

player_labels.war_ossuary: the burial ground behind the fort

qualities.rubric: Where is the party right now? war_throne_room: the palace in Aegis City, its war room or throne hall; war_queens_wing: Queen Melisande's wing of the palace; war_kingsfield: the muster field under Aegis City's western walls; war_the_front: Fort Vicinitas and the ridge over the Ashen March, facing Greywater; war_renfath: Renfath, Nuwerth's great gladiatorial pits; war_nuwerth_market: Nuwerth's slave market and streets; war_burning_villages: the villages of the March behind the Darran line; war_ossuary: the Office of the Fallen's burial ground behind Fort Vicinitas; war_last_field: Aldermere Field.

checkpoints.name: The King's War Council
checkpoints.objective: Hear the King's war council, and answer his commission.
checkpoints.player_text: Maps, old Zegallan banners and a king with a commission for your party: the council waits on your answer.

guidance.all: The war room behind the throne hall of the palace in Aegis City: a map table scored with knife marks, Zegallan banners from the last war on the walls. King Alexander lays it out in his formal, practised voice: the Empire's surprise attacks took Greywater and the villages of the Ashen March, Kanna the Blood Saint's Cursefire Regiment holds them, a winged thing calling itself Prodyr's herald burns the villages behind the line, and Zegallan raiders drive Darran captives west in chains. Prince Forre commands the field army mustering for Fort Vicinitas and wants a free company that can go where soldiers cannot; Guildmaster Vallie has brought the Guild's charter, and the King wants the Nightriver heir's party in it, by name. Before the council breaks a councillor raises the empty graves at the front, the dead that vanish from the burial pits, and the name the court has for it, the Queen's Cult, and every eye slides to the Queen's empty chair. Let the party question anyone; taking the commission, or refusing a king to his face, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Alexander would welcome any excuse to be rid of Melisande and dares not act on one while the Third Kingdom's alliance, which her marriage sealed, still holds. He says only that the rumour 'will be looked into'. Forre suspects the rumour is false and lets it stand, because it weakens the houses that back Haley, and it sits badly with him. Haley knows her mother has never touched necromancy and is one word from saying so in open council. Vallie knows the Crown means to spend adventurers as a forlorn hope and says so to a party that asks her straight.
members.war_king: Alexander would welcome any excuse to be rid of Melisande and dares not act on one while the Third Kingdom's alliance, which her marriage sealed, still holds. He says only that the rumour 'will be looked into'.
members.war_prince: Forre suspects the rumour is false and lets it stand, because it weakens the houses that back Haley, and it sits badly with him.
members.war_princess: Haley knows her mother has never touched necromancy and is one word from saying so in open council.
members.war_guildmaster: Vallie knows the Crown means to spend adventurers as a forlorn hope and says so to a party that asks her straight.

director.instruction: A royal audience. Pick Alexander when the player addresses the King, when the Crown's will is the question, or when anyone challenges him. Pick Forre when the war, the army or strategy is the matter; Haley when her mother or her own place is touched; Melisande when she is present and addressed or the Queen's Cult is named; Vallie when the Guild, adventurers or rank come up. Pick an ally who marched (Natalia, Welden or Ronan of House Nightriver, Ced, Kela, Honami, Lobo or Erevan) or Shelara only when addressed. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed or silent for several turns. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the court must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Alexander, Forre, Haley, Vallie, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: Zegallan banners from the last war hang above the palace map table. King Alexander names the villages lost on the Ashen March while Prince Forre marks a road to Fort Vicinitas in ink. Vallie has brought the Guild charter: the Crown wants a free company that can go where its army cannot. The council falls quiet, and every face at the table turns to you.
A runner in mud-splashed Crown livery is let in, whispers to Prince Forre, and is sent out again. Forre moves a black token one finger's breadth east across the map, and says nothing.

effects.scenario: [Genre: dark high fantasy war story, grim and costly, with court intrigue and something older underneath. World: Adolion, the Darran Kingdom at war with the Zegallan Empire. Arc: Fire and War. The Nightriver heir's adventuring party is called into the war as the Crown's free company, and whoever it won over on its earlier roads answers the muster. Places: the palace in Aegis City; the Kingsfield muster; Fort Vicinitas over the Ashen March; the villages of the March.]

motives.war_king: bind the Nightriver heir's party to the Crown's commission, and keep the Queen rumour safely vague
motives.war_prince: win his field army a free company that can go where soldiers cannot
motives.war_princess: hold her tongue in open council while the court slanders her mother over the empty graves
motives.war_guildmaster: get the party on the Guild charter, and tell them straight what the Crown means to spend them on
motives.companion_a: size up this king and his war, and say exactly what she thinks of both
motives.companion_b: read the room quietly and learn what the empty graves at the front really mean

checkpoints.name: The Queen's Wing
checkpoints.objective: Hear the Queen out, and decide.
checkpoints.player_text: Princess Haley marches you past the guards to her mother's rooms, where Queen Melisande has a request of her own.

guidance.all: The refusal was heard. Within the hour Princess Haley finds the party in a palace corridor and all but marches them to her mother's wing, past guards who are supposed to keep Queen Melisande in and have given up keeping anyone out. The Queen receives them among unsent letters home and a koto she no longer plays; she knows exactly what the council said about her, and asks one thing: go to the front, find out who is stealing the dead, and bring back the truth before her husband decides it for her. She is gracious, direct and frightened, and she does not beg; Haley does all the fierce talking. Present it and stop: taking the commission after all is {{story_player_name}}'s call.

members.dm: Melisande is an exorcist and ritualist of the Third Kingdom and knows stolen dead mean necromancy, which she can read and unmake. She does not say so, because it is exactly what the court would call proof. Haley has smuggled her mother out of this wing twice this month, a game the guards never win, and has not told her father. The Queen holds a sealed letter from the Third Kingdom's court that she has not opened.
members.war_queen: Melisande is an exorcist and ritualist of the Third Kingdom and knows stolen dead mean necromancy, which she can read and unmake. She does not say so, because it is exactly what the court would call proof.
members.war_princess: Haley has smuggled her mother out of this wing twice this month, a game the guards never win, and has not told her father.

director.instruction: A royal audience. Pick Alexander when the player addresses the King, when the Crown's will is the question, or when anyone challenges him. Pick Forre when the war, the army or strategy is the matter; Haley when her mother or her own place is touched; Melisande when she is present and addressed or the Queen's Cult is named; Vallie when the Guild, adventurers or rank come up. Pick an ally who marched (Natalia, Welden or Ronan of House Nightriver, Ced, Kela, Honami, Lobo or Erevan) or Shelara only when addressed. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed or silent for several turns. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the court must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Melisande, Haley, Belle and Dalan. Haley does the fierce talking and Melisande answers with quiet dignity; the party speaks for itself.

motives.war_queen: persuade the party to find who steals the dead, without revealing what she herself could read in it
motives.war_princess: push the party into taking her mother's request, and keep her own corridor games secret
motives.companion_a: judge for herself whether this frightened queen is a cultist or a scapegoat
motives.companion_b: listen past the Queen's grace for the fear underneath, and ease the strain in the room

checkpoints.name: House Nightriver Answers
checkpoints.objective: Receive House Nightriver's company at the muster, and give it its place.
checkpoints.player_text: Dusk and torchlight on the muster field, and House Nightriver's blue-and-silver banner coming down the road.

guidance.all: Dusk on the Kingsfield under Aegis City's western walls, where the field army musters in mud and torchlight. House Nightriver's blue-and-silver banner comes down the road over a column of house levies and robed battlemages: the house answers because its heir stopped the rite beneath the seal, and whatever the court says of the Nightrivers now, they owe the heir that. Natalia rides at its head in a fur-collared cape with frost creeping along her reins, Welden beside her with a satchel of books he was told not to bring, Ronan on foot in plate over leather, and General Isidora Frolovan of the Wolfpack Battalion, who held Fort Vicinitas in the last war, comes to take the heir's measure. Let the siblings be siblings; where the company stands, and under whom, is {{story_player_name}}'s to say. When the army marches west for the front, let the road take them.

members.dm: Ronan keeps a shrine to Prodyr hidden in his kit. His parents escaped Zegallan slavery and died of it, and he wants this war more than anyone here knows. Welden has read in the Nightriver library of the Lich Queen's grave-tithe, necromancers who followed armies to harvest the dead, and suspects the empty graves mean exactly that. He says so only if someone asks what he thinks. Natalia hates slavers with a cold that frightens her, and her magic slips worse when she is angry. Isidora trained under Lord Javon, wants to know what became of him, and does not ask.

checkpoints.player_text: A company in lacquered armour marches up from the docks under a red-and-black banner, fresh off a ship from the east.

guidance.all: A Third Kingdom company marches up from the Aegis docks in good order, fresh off a ship across the Jehopa Ocean: a warlord's retainers in lacquered armour under a red-and-black banner, a knot of Hattaxi shinobi who are simply there when nobody saw them arrive, and Honami Nemaden, three white tails and a red ribbon, sent as their onmyoji because the debt was owed to the party and she made certain it would be her. They come under the Emperor's alliance, and their captain carries a sealed packet for Queen Melisande, who was born a Zhao. Honami greets {{story_player_name}} as though no ocean ever lay between them and everyone else as furniture. Where the company fights, and whether the packet reaches the Queen, is the party's to settle. When the army marches west for the front, let the road take them.

members.dm: The captain's sealed orders from Emperor Zhao are to bring the Queen home to Savalon if the Darran court turns on her, by ship or by force. The Hattaxi have seen grey-cloaked carters leave the palace's Office of the Fallen at night and thought nothing of it. Only Honami knows, and she tells {{story_player_name}} if it earns her gratitude. Forre does not want foreign soldiers anywhere near his mother.

checkpoints.player_text: At midnight a black coach stops at the edge of the camp behind horses whose breath does not steam, and an envoy steps down.

guidance.all: At the stroke of midnight a black coach draws up at the edge of the Kingsfield behind horses that do not steam in the cold, and from it steps an envoy of House Dracul with Camilla's seal in red wax: a gift laid on top of what the party already owes her, which is how Camilla collects. The Lady Camilla sends the Dragon's Own, a company of pale knights who fight only between dusk and dawn and ask no pay but the enemy's dead to drink from, and her compliments to the heir, in a hand that writes the way a stage queen talks. The soldiers who see the coach will not stop talking about it. Let the offer be as courteous as it is monstrous; whether the knights ride with the army, and on what terms, is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide. When the army marches west for the front, let the road take them.

members.dm: Camilla wants a seat at the Darran court when the war is over and means this gift as its first stone. The envoy is under orders to be seen by the King. The envoy knows someone in this army is working necromancy, because the dead of the last skirmishes 'taste wrong', and trades that knowledge only for a courtesy. Forre would hang the envoy if he dared.

Her own words: Let it never be said the Dragon let her debtors die before they could pay."

guidance.all: At first light a column of Inquisitors of the Church of Boher rides onto the Kingsfield in grey and blue, and with them, masked and quiet, Erevan Rolavo, with his shortbow and the gourd where he keeps his Echoes. The Church stands with the party because the party stood with it, and because the thing burning Darran villages calls itself a herald of Prodyr and burns Boher's faithful first; the Inquisition has come to hunt it. Let the camp's relief and unease both show; how the Inquisitors join the march is {{story_player_name}}'s to settle with Prince Forre. When the army marches west for the front, let the road take them.

The Inquisitors know a celestial can be sealed on holy ground and not killed, and keep it for when it is needed. The column's captain has orders to burn any witch found with the army.

checkpoints.player_text: Before dawn the green mark on the sworn hand burns, and something tall with antlers of living wood waits at the camp's edge.

guidance.all: Before dawn the green mark on the sworn hand begins to burn, and at the edge of the camp a Guardian of Eshalanore stands where no sentry saw it come: a stag with bark for hide and too many eyes, antlers of living wood, a quiver of arrows grown rather than made hanging from them, every shaft a living green. It does not speak; the Lady's voice comes out of the dark around it, once, like wind in leaves: when the dead march, the forest marches. Then it is gone, and the soldiers who saw it swear it stood taller than the gate. Nobody in the camp understands the message and the party is not asked to; who carries the arrows is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide. When the army marches west for the front, let the road take them.

checkpoints.player_text: Cannon at dawn, a ridge of shield walls over burned fields, and Greywater's captured walls across the valley.

guidance.all: Fort Vicinitas on its ridge above the Ashen March: black stubble fields, the shells of farmhouses, crows, and across the valley Greywater's walls under the Cursefire Regiment's burning-axe banner. The Darran shield walls hold the ridge with archers behind them; Zegallan cannon open every dawn, the slave corps comes screaming up the slope drugged and frenzied, and the Demon Squad has been seen, twice a man's height, walking through arrows. On the second day Kanna Helfin rides out under a parley flag in blackened plate that came onto her in a swirl of blood, calls for someone worth killing, and in her rage lets slip that the Darrans have been digging up her dead at Greywater. Forre wants what only his free company can do, and the raid trails lead west to where the captives go. Whether the party slips behind the line or walks into Kanna's reach is {{story_player_name}}'s choice, and being taken alive is possible.

members.dm: Kanna believes the Darrans are stealing her dead and would rather die than admit it troubles her. A challenge accepted on her terms is kept on her terms. The Office of the Fallen's grey-cloaked carters work the burial pits behind the fort at night under Crown seal, and nobody questions them. Allies who answered the muster fight on the ridge with the army and will stay with it. Forre knows the line cannot hold another month and hides it from the men.

A cart of the Office of the Fallen passes the gate at night, heavy under grey canvas, and the sentries salute it.

checkpoints.name: Behind the Lines
checkpoints.objective: West behind the Zegallan lines toward Nuwerth: whatever the road holds.
checkpoints.player_text: West of the line the country belongs to the Empire, and the captives' road runs on toward Nuwerth.

checkpoints.name: Renfath
checkpoints.objective: Survive Renfath's sand, and win a way out of the pits.
checkpoints.player_text: Red sand, iron gates and screaming stands: in Nuwerth's great pits, you are fighters now.

guidance.all: Nuwerth rises in seven walled tiers of ochre stone toward its central tower, and in its belly lies Renfath, the Bloody Ground: screaming stands around a pit of red sand, iron portcullises, the smell of blood and hot iron. Whether the party came in chains or in disguise, the pits take them as fighters, a bout a day against slave-corps gladiators and caged beasts, and the custom of the pits is old and real: three wins on the sand and the chains are struck. Keder Valfaust, the Ebon Executioner, is home from the front picking fighters for the Demon Squad, and watches from the fighters' gallery with a book in his lap; he likes rebels and he keeps his word. At night the dead are carried out through the tunnels on carts that go to no pyre. Make every bout cost something; how the party gets out, on the sand, by a bargain with Keder or through the tunnels, is theirs.

members.dm: Keder wants a gladiator to mentor, to keep a promise to the Ebon Reaver who taught him, and has already picked one of the party without saying which. Keder knows about the carts and thinks it an insult to the fallen, who belong to Prodyr's fire. The pit master sells Renfath's dead by the cartload to a buyer who pays in Darran silver and carries a Crown grave-warden's seal, and thinks it a fine joke.
members.war_executioner: Keder wants a gladiator to mentor, to keep a promise to the Ebon Reaver who taught him, and has already picked one of the party without saying which. Keder knows about the carts and thinks it an insult to the fallen, who belong to Prodyr's fire.

npc_replies.text: The gate grinds up and the noise of Renfath comes down like a wall: tens of thousands of voices, the red sand throwing back the sun. High in the fighters' gallery a big red-haired man in black plate marks his place in a book with one finger, and looks down.
Somewhere under the stands a cart rattles through the tunnels, heavy, and the fighters in the cells go quiet until it has passed.

motives.war_executioner: test the fighter he has quietly picked from the party, and see whether they earn his mentoring
motives.companion_a: win her three bouts on the sand and keep the rest of the party standing beside her
motives.companion_b: find a way out through the tunnels and learn where the night carts take the dead

complications: The crowd starts chanting for a beast bout, and the portcullis on the far side of the sand begins to rise.
A fighter the party trained beside yesterday is carried out on a cart that does not turn toward the pyres.
Keder closes his book, stands, and walks down to the sand himself.

checkpoints.name: The Slave Pens
checkpoints.objective: Free Shelara and whichever of the Kelnan you can, and get out of Nuwerth.
checkpoints.player_text: Cages under awnings, a slaver calling prices, and a column of captives being chained for the block. What you do here is yours.

guidance.all: The way east runs through Nuwerth's slave market, where the Empire sells its war without shame: cages in rows under awnings, wartime slaves, criminals and debtors, and a slaver in a bright purple coat and a top hat calling prices. The last Kelnan survivors are being chained neck to neck into a column to be driven from the pens to the auction block, and at its head walks Shelara Kelnan, an elf with red hair streaked silver and one ruby eye and one sapphire, her Slave Crest only half-branded because no buyer has finished it yet; a second pen is chalked for 'the grey buyer'. Buying her would mean finishing the Crest in the buyer's name, and she would hate whoever did it for the rest of her life. The city is a maze of walls and guard posts and the slavers' dogs are real. How the party breaks her out of the column, and how many Kelnan come with them, is theirs.

members.dm: Shelara trusts no one who looks at her on the block and hides how much she understands. She hates humans, Prodyr and the Empire, and loves the Evergreen Tribe, Dalan's people. She saw the grey buyer take a pen of Kelnan east toward the Darran lines, which makes no sense to her. The slaver keeps a ledger of 'dead stock' sold to the same buyer. Keder, if he is here, will not raise a hand against a party that won its freedom on the sand, and will not help it either.

checkpoints.name: Malach's Fire
checkpoints.objective: Stop the herald of Prodyr burning the villages of the March.
checkpoints.player_text: Villages burn behind the Darran line, a chapel of Boher falling in, and in the fire stands something with white wings.

guidance.all: The road east comes out behind the Darran line into the villages of the March, and they are burning: Millbrook first, its thatched chapel of Boher falling in, people running, and standing in the fire in white robes with his wings spread is Malach, herald of Prodyr, with a flaming red bastard sword called Judgement. He burns Boher's faithful, always leaves one alive to spread the word, and heals from any wound, so killing him buys a day at most. What stops him is a seal worked on holy ground while he is held there, or a beating bad enough that he withdraws to his own realm in a rage; both are real and both cost. Give Shelara, Belle and Dalan each a moment, make the fire as much the enemy as he is, and show grey-cloaked carters already loading the burned dead behind the smoke. How the burning ends is the party's to decide.

members.dm: Malach knows grey carters follow his fires and hates them for stealing what belongs to Prodyr's flame. He tells a mortal who defies him to his face, as an insult. He knows he can be sealed and has kept away from cities for that reason. The one survivor he spares tonight saw the carters take her family's bodies and thought they were Crown men come to help. Shelara hates Prodyr more than any living thing.

checkpoints.name: The Office of the Fallen
checkpoints.objective: Follow the grey carts, and find out who is stealing the dead.
checkpoints.player_text: Grey carts full of the dead roll behind Fort Vicinitas to a walled field of trenches under the Crown's own seal.

guidance.all: The carters' track runs behind Fort Vicinitas to the Crown's burial ground, where the Office of the Fallen gives the war dead their rites: a walled field of long trenches and lime pits, a chapel tent, clerks with ledgers, grey-cloaked wardens under a Crown seal nobody questions. By night the trenches are not graves: the dead of both armies lie in rows inside sigils cut into the clay, Kelnan bought as 'dead stock' wait chained in a barn to join them, and Grave-Warden Edric Tolle, a mild, balding Crown official with ink on his fingers, walks the rows reading from a black book. Let the truth come in pieces: the ledgers, the sigils, the barn, and the rumour about the Queen drafted in a warden's own hand. The wardens fight like men who expect to get up again. What the party does with Tolle and the truth, and whether it reaches the King before the battle, is theirs.

members.dm: Tolle is the Queen's Cult: a necromancer eleven years in the Office of the Fallen who fed the rumour about Queen Melisande to the court himself, and he means to raise every corpse on the coming battlefield as the Lich Queen's first host. Most of his wardens have already gone ahead to dig pits at Aldermere Field, but he cannot raise the field without the black book in his hand. The King believes the Queen's Cult is his wife's and would rather not be told otherwise. Shelara finds the Kelnan in the barn and knows at least one face.
