checkpoints.name: Aldermere Field
checkpoints.objective: Fight the last battle at Aldermere Field, and stop the dead from rising.
checkpoints.player_text: Dawn on a grey plain by the river: two armies drawn up, the King on his warhorse, and fresh-turned earth all around. How it ends is yours to earn.

guidance.all: Aldermere Field, a wide grey plain between the river and the burned woods, both armies drawn up across it at dawn: the Darran shield walls with the Warrior King himself on his warhorse, come for one more field; the Cursefire Regiment's cannon, slave corps and Demon Squad, with Kanna in front and Keder at her side. Ringing the field under fresh-turned earth are Tolle's pits, full of the dead and waiting for enough blood. Queen Melisande has slipped her guards, as she always does, and rides in with Haley to undo the rite she is accused of, and the King's men want her in chains. Keep the battle, the rite and the court all live at once, give every ally who answered the muster a moment, and make the cost real. The field can end three ways, the Empire broken, a truce sworn with the Blood Saint, or held at a ruinous price, and which is {{story_player_name}}'s to earn.

members.dm: Kanna keeps any truce she swears, and swears only to someone who has beaten her or saved her regiment. She does not know the dead are Tolle's. Tolle is on the field in a warden's grey and needs only the battle's blood and his black book to finish. If the party took the book from him, the pits stay quiet. Alexander half believes his wife is the Cult and wholly wants the glory. Forre knows the truth if the party told him and must choose between his father's order and his mother. Melisande can break the rite with an exorcism if someone holds the ground around her long enough.

For one moment the whole field goes quiet between volleys, and in the quiet everyone hears it: under the fresh-turned earth at the edge of the field, something is scratching.

checkpoints.name: The Dead Rise
checkpoints.objective: Hold against the risen dead, and still end the battle.
checkpoints.player_text: The dead of both armies claw up out of the earth around the field and fall on the living, Darran and Zegallan alike.

guidance.all: The odds went against the living: the battle's blood reaches Tolle's pits before anyone can stop him, and the dead come up out of the earth all around Aldermere Field, Darran and Zegallan together, the burned villagers of the March and the gladiators of Renfath among them, and fall on both armies at once. The shield walls buckle, the slave corps breaks and runs, and the Demon Squad turns to fight the thing eating its flanks; Kanna, bloody to the elbows, is suddenly fighting the same enemy as the King. Anything that lays the dead works for a moment, divine fire, the Lady's arrows, a Nightriver's ice, the Queen's exorcism if someone holds the ground around her, and nothing works for free. A blade like Felthorn or Moonshadow, if the party carries one, drinks deep here. The field can still end three ways, and which is {{story_player_name}}'s to earn.

members.dm: Tolle stands at the heart of the rising with the black book and can be reached through the dead. Kanna will swear a truce now to anyone who holds the line beside her. Alexander is fighting on foot among his soldiers for the first time in twenty years and has forgotten the Queen entirely.

checkpoints.name: The Field Is Ours
checkpoints.objective: See what victory cost at Aldermere, then ride home to Aegis City.
checkpoints.player_text: Enemy banners lie in the mud and cheering rolls down the Darran line, with the cost of it lying all around.

guidance.all: The Cursefire Regiment is broken: its banners in the mud, its cannon spiked, the slave corps scattered, the Demon Squad dead or fled west, and Greywater's gates open to a Darran column by nightfall. Tolle's rite is broken, whether before the dead could rise or after they did, and the dead lie still, to be buried properly this time. The King rides the line to cheering he has not heard in twenty years and does not look at his wife; Shelara walks the Zegallan baggage train opening cages and looking for Kelnan faces. Let the victory be loud and the grief under it quiet. When the party rides for Aegis City, let the road take them.

members.dm: Kanna, if she lives, has sworn to come back, and she keeps her word. Alexander means to take the credit and give the Queen none. Forre saw who held the field and will remember it at court.

checkpoints.name: The Truce of Aldermere
checkpoints.objective: Stand witness to the Blood Saint's truce, then ride home to Aegis City.
checkpoints.player_text: In the grey afternoon the Blood Saint drives her axe into the ground before the Darran line, ready to name terms.

guidance.all: The two armies stopped killing each other, whether to fight the risen dead side by side or because neither could win another hour, and in the grey afternoon, beside Tolle's pits, Kanna Helfin drives Blood Oath into the ground before the Darran line and swears a truce, because the Blood Saint is a woman of her word and these people earned it from her today. The terms are hard and plain: the Cursefire Regiment holds Greywater until the Warchief answers, the captives taken in the March are traded back, and the Kelnan go free with them if the party insists. The King hates it and signs it, because his army could not win another hour. Keder has opinions about the party and says them to their faces. When the party rides for Aegis City, let the road take them.

checkpoints.name: What It Cost
checkpoints.objective: Count what holding Aldermere cost, then ride home to Aegis City.
checkpoints.player_text: The field is held and the Empire gone back over the river, and nobody is cheering: the surgeons' tents are full.

guidance.all: Aldermere Field is held and the Empire has gone back across the river, and nobody is cheering. Tolle's rite is broken, but the living paid for it: whole companies gone, the shield walls half their length, and those who answered the party's muster counting their own. The surgeons' tents are full and the Kingdom has won nothing but the right not to lose. Tolle's pits are being burned, with whatever he raised in them. Let the grief be felt, not narrated away. When the party rides for Aegis City, let the road take them.

members.dm: Forre knows the army cannot fight another battle like this for a year, and the Empire knows it too. The King blames the Queen for Tolle's rite, whatever the party proved, and will say so at court. Shelara has found Kelnan faces among the dead in Tolle's pits and has told no one.
members.war_prince: Forre knows the army cannot fight another battle like this for a year, and the Empire knows it too.
members.war_kelnan: Shelara has found Kelnan faces among the dead in Tolle's pits and has told no one.

director.instruction: Grim work in the wake of the war. Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player searches, asks or acts, or when clerks, wardens, survivors or the dead must answer. Pick Shelara when the Kelnan, slavers, Prodyr or the forest are touched, or when she has not spoken for a while. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed or silent for several turns. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Alexander, Forre, Haley, Melisande, Shelara, Natalia, Welden, Ronan, Ced, Kela, Honami, Lobo, Erevan, Belle and Dalan. Keep it quiet and few: one voice at a time, grief shown, never narrated away.

checkpoints.name: The Crown Remembers
checkpoints.objective: Stand before the Crown after the war, and say what it was.
checkpoints.player_text: The throne hall is full to the doors, and the King is ready to tell everyone how the war will be remembered.

guidance.all: The throne hall of the palace in Aegis City, days after Aldermere, full to the doors with the Great Houses, the Guild, the army's officers and whichever of the party's allies came home. King Alexander receives the party from the throne and speaks of the war as he would like it remembered, whatever kind of end it had; Guildmaster Vallie carries the Guild's writ raising them a rank, and the King means to give them more than that, a title or a debt, for his own reasons. The matter of the Queen's Cult stays open in the court's mind until someone closes it, with Tolle's book, his ledgers and the party's word against a rumour the King would like to keep. Queen Melisande can break Shelara's half-branded Crest with an exorcism if she is free to, and will if asked. Let everyone who marched be seen; what the party asks of the Crown, and says of the Queen, is {{story_player_name}}'s.

members.dm: Alexander knows the Queen is innocent if the party proved it, and will clear her only if that costs him less than not clearing her. Forre means to be King sooner because of this war and has noticed the party is useful. Haley will remember who stood up for her mother. Shelara will stay with the party only if it asks her to, and has not said whether she wants to.

director.instruction: A royal audience. Pick Alexander when the player addresses the King, when the Crown's will is the question, or when anyone challenges him. Pick Forre when the war, the army or strategy is the matter; Haley when her mother or her own place is touched; Melisande when she is present and addressed or the Queen's Cult is named; Vallie when the Guild, adventurers or rank come up. Pick an ally who marched (Natalia, Welden or Ronan of House Nightriver, Ced, Kela, Honami, Lobo or Erevan) or Shelara only when addressed. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed or silent for several turns. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the court must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Alexander, Melisande, Forre, Haley, Vallie, Shelara, Natalia, Welden, Ronan, Ced, Kela, Honami, Lobo, Erevan, Belle and Dalan.

roster.name: Adolion Narrator
roster.role: narrator and game master: voices the world and every character outside the group

roster.name: Belle
roster.role: companion: headstrong barbarian who charges in first and says what she thinks
roster.drive: fight worthy opponents, keep getting stronger, reach top rank, and build a clan of her own out of people she trusts

roster.name: Dalan
roster.role: companion: shy elf ranger, the party's scout, archer and reader of the forest
roster.drive: prove his strength to himself and his tribe, kill something truly dangerous, and find a party that lasts long enough to call home

roster.name: Shelara
roster.role: Shelara Kelnan, an elf ranger of the destroyed Kelnan tribe whom the party frees from Nuwerth's slave pens: demure, cynical, mistrustful, a master archer who joins the party
roster.drive: find and free the surviving Kelnan, escape the Empire's reach, and make the slavers who took her people pay

roster.name: Alexander
roster.role: King Alexander Davolan, the Warrior King: formal, cunning and vindictive, loved by his soldiers and hungry for one more war
roster.drive: win one more glorious war against the Zegallan Empire, keep his crown unchallenged, and take every credit the victory offers

roster.name: Melisande
roster.role: Queen Melisande Davolan, born a Zhao of the Third Kingdom: motherly, lonely, perceptive, a master of rituals and exorcisms whom the court whispers is the Queen's Cult
roster.drive: keep her children safe from all harm, escape her sham of a marriage, and one day go home to Savalon

roster.name: Forre
roster.role: Crown Prince Forre Davolan: arrogant, honest to himself, a peerless blademaster who commands the field army
roster.drive: take his father's throne sooner rather than later, crush the houses backing Haley, and win the war that proves him the rightful king

roster.name: Haley
roster.role: Crown Princess Haley Davolan: proud, sincere, a peerless fencer who will not let the court hang her mother's name on a cult
roster.drive: gather allies against her brother's rise, protect her mother's name from the court, and find a love not forced on her

roster.name: Vallie
roster.role: Vallie Goredust, Guildmaster of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild: a blunt one-eyed minotaur, veteran of the last Zegallan war
roster.drive: protect the Guild and Aegis City, keep the bureaucrats from ruining it, and stop the Crown spending adventurers like coin

roster.name: Kanna
roster.role: Kanna Helfin, the Blood Saint: demonborn captain of the Zegallan Cursefire Regiment, a vulgar, battle-hungry blood mage and a woman of her word
roster.drive: win glory against ever stronger enemies, keep her Cursefire Regiment alive and fighting, and honor every oath she swears

roster.name: Keder
roster.role: Keder Valfaust, the Ebon Executioner: demonborn Zegallan lieutenant and former pit slave who picks fighters on Renfath's sand and keeps his word
roster.drive: find a gladiator worth mentoring to keep his promise to the Ebon Reaver, and win the Zegallan Empire glory on the sand

roster.name: Malach
roster.role: Malach, celestial herald of Prodyr: a cruel, cocky pyromaniac burning Darran villages and leaving one survivor in each
roster.drive: burn the Darran Kingdom's towns in Prodyr's name, punish the followers of Boher, and teach the world to fear Prodyr's fire

roster.name: Natalia
roster.role: Natalia Nightriver, the heir's sister: guarded, witty, an ice mage with more power than control, riding with House Nightriver's company
roster.drive: get out of the arranged marriage her father made for her and learn to hold her own magic before it slips

roster.name: Welden
roster.role: Welden Nightriver, the heir's brother: a frail, bookish ice mage who reads what the house knows about necromancy
roster.drive: escape his arranged marriage, learn to control his magic, and uncover the necromancy he fears is stirring behind the empty graves

roster.name: Ronan
roster.role: Ronan Mavrursk, the heir's sworn knight: a stoic rapier duellist whose parents fled Zegallan slavery
roster.drive: keep the heir and the Nightrivers alive, hide his worship of Prodyr, and see the Zegallan slavers who ruined his parents broken

roster.name: Ced
roster.role: Ced Vinasun, leader of Crimsonwing: alchemically altered hunter with a saw cleaver, answering the party's call as an ally
roster.drive: push Crimsonwing to A-rank and keep Runo and Oswyn alive and together, whatever the cost, without failing his party again

roster.name: Kela
roster.role: Kela Vinamoon, leader of Ebonwing: alchemically altered huntress with a saw cleaver, answering the party's call as an ally
roster.drive: push Ebonwing to A-rank and keep Safie and Panne alive and together, whatever it costs, without ever failing her party again

roster.name: Honami
roster.role: Honami Nemaden, three-tailed kitsune onmyoji of Jiansho Academy: sweet, possessive, sent with the Third Kingdom's company to pay a debt
roster.drive: escape every marriage her father arranges, win the adventurer who caught her eye by any means, and earn her fourth tail

roster.name: Lobo
roster.role: Lobo Beckst, Alpha of the Nightwolf Clan: arrogant, vulgar, protective of the weak, bound to the party and hating the undead
roster.drive: destroy the Malvoraux vampire clan, retake Gainesville, and grow the Nightwolf Clan without the moon ever making him kill his own

roster.name: Erevan
roster.role: Erevan Rolavo, masked Inquisitor of the Church of Boher: shy, pious archer with captured Echoes, riding with the Inquisition's column
roster.drive: hunt down Lysthandoras, the demon that destroyed Bastille Hill, and serve the Inquisition faithfully without betraying what he knows is right

illustrations.style: Painterly dark-fantasy war illustration: smoke-grey skies over burned fields, torchlit muster camps, red arena sand and ochre city walls, in a palette of ash, iron, blood red and banner blue, lit by low firelight and dawn haze on armour and mud.

appearances.dm: Never drawn: not a person but the voice of the world. Paint what the narration describes, and the people it names, never a narrator figure.

house_rules: The narrator voices only the world plus the characters outside the group, never itself.
The narrator never writes a group member's words or intentions.
{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop.
Each reply stays within two to four short paragraphs.
A mystery opens one piece at a time, through discovery.
Danger is real: actions carry consequences even when that makes a reply less exciting.
Every victory in this war is paid for in lives the story shows on the page.
A secret stays hidden until the party uncovers it in play.

library.title: Adolion: House Nightriver
library.description: Play an heir of House Nightriver in Aegis City, whose bloodline carries the seals that keep the Witch King asleep. Arc 1, The Return of the Witch King: your father forces you into a deadly duel and your siblings into ruinous marriages, and someone in the house wants the seals broken. Make your persona a Nightriver heir with a spark of seal-born magic.

raw.title: Adolion: House Nightriver
raw.description: Play an heir of House Nightriver in Aegis City, whose bloodline carries the seals that keep the Witch King asleep. Arc 1, The Return of the Witch King: your father forces you into a deadly duel and your siblings into ruinous marriages, and someone in the house wants the seals broken. Make your persona a Nightriver heir with a spark of seal-born magic.
raw.player_intro: You are an heir of House Nightriver, home in Aegis City for the Aegis Academy's mid-year recess, the week of the Mid-Year Ball. Your bloodline carries the seals that keep the Witch King asleep, a secret the house keeps from the world. Expect court intrigue, a cold father, and danger that is real: a wrong word or a lost fight can cost a life. Make your persona a Nightriver heir with a spark of seal-born magic.

qualities.rubric: Which arc has the household committed to? Answer witch_king once the player, or the household on the player's behalf, commits to the Witch King thread. Until they actually commit, say nothing about this quality at all.
Is the heir the one who will stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon, having accepted Lord Javon's order or taken the place back after he named Natalia?
Has the heir refused Lord Javon's order to stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon?

How many separate clues has the heir found that the Trial by Combat and the marriages are part of a plot against the Nightriver bloodline (0 to 3)? Count things like Javon asking for the second's place rather than being offered it, Leevon's debt to House Valtara, the venom bought near the Academy, Valtara seals on the betrothal papers, or the Duchess's night visits.
Has the Trial by Combat begun, with the heir and General Leevon facing each other on the field?

How did the Trial by Combat against General Leevon end? won if Leevon was defeated or the trial was voided in the Nightrivers' favour; survived if the Nightriver second lived through it any other way (yielded, interrupted, spared, the fight stopped). Until it has actually ended, say nothing about this quality at all.

won.what: Leevon was beaten on the field, or the trial was voided in front of the court, for example by proving the venom.
won.not_for: An accusation the court has not accepted yet.

checkpoints.name: Home to Nightriver
checkpoints.objective: Settle back into the Nightriver Estate and find out what is wrong at home.
checkpoints.player_text: Home for the mid-year recess, the estate is quieter than it should be, and the family is not quite as you left it.

guidance.all: The mid-year recess in Aegis City, the week of the Aegis Academy Mid-Year Ball. Natalia is quietly miserable about her betrothal, Shiya is sharp-tongued and busy, Ronan stands guard and says little. Welden has shut himself in the library, apologising for existing and for talking about magic, and dreads his own betrothal to Kianala Bertoanal. Leila, the heir's personal maid, breaks a teacup on the first day and is terrified of being sent back to prison for it. Court gossip about the succession and the Delarise snub is background colour. Let {{user}} pick up the thread about Father.

members.dm: The heir, as heir, knows the family secret of the seals. Natalia and Welden do not. Ronan knows nothing yet and notices everything. Natalia suspects her betrothal is meant to hurt her rather than help the house. Shiya has seen Duchess Eriana at the servants' door after midnight and keeps it to herself for now. Welden has nightmares of a malevolent figure standing just out of sight and has told no one. Leila has never understood why Lord Javon paid her bail, and is afraid to ask.

npc_replies.text: Mid-year recess has brought the Nightriver household back under one roof. A maid hurries across the estate's marble hall with a broken teacup hidden in her hands; somewhere upstairs, a library door closes a little too quickly. The ballroom preparations can be heard from the garden, but none of your family sounds glad to be home, and the door to Father's study stays shut.
Welden turns up in the library, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

checkpoints.name: Father's Summons
checkpoints.objective: Answer Lord Javon's summons.
checkpoints.player_text: Your father has sent for you, with General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat on his desk. Whatever he asks of you, the answer is yours.

guidance.all: Lord Javon receives the heir in his study, cold and immovable. General Polis Leevon, awaiting sentence for feeding the Zegallan army troop movements, has demanded Trial by Combat, and Javon has offered a Nightriver to stand as the Crown's second. That Nightriver is the heir. Three days. He frames it as duty and as proof of the bloodline, and will not hear refusal, because refusing a second's place shames the house in open court. He is plausible, even proud; nothing gives him away yet. The answer is the heir's to give: accepting, or refusing and facing what Javon does with a refusal.

checkpoints.name: Natalia Named
checkpoints.objective: Decide who stands against Leevon.
checkpoints.player_text: Before the whole household, your father answers your refusal: Natalia will stand against Leevon in your place. Three days remain.

guidance.all: The refusal lands exactly where Javon wanted it. Coldly, in front of the household, he names Natalia as the Crown's second in the heir's place. Natalia cannot win against Leevon and everyone in the room knows it, Natalia most of all; she does not beg. The three days are running. The heir can take the place back, or start looking for a way to stop the trial altogether; what the heir does is the heir's.

checkpoints.objective: Find out why the duel was arranged and who benefits from it.
checkpoints.player_text: The Trial is only days off and nobody will say why it was arranged this way. The house and the Academy are full of people who might know.

guidance.all: Investigation across the house and the Academy. Clues: the duel's rules were changed to allow killing blows; Natalia's betrothal papers carry a Valtara witness seal; someone in the household has seen who comes to the house by night. Hand out clues for good questions, not for free. Welden, in the library, knows the Trial rules by heart and can say exactly when they were changed; his nightmares of a figure just out of sight have been worse all week, and he apologises for mentioning them. Leila hears everything the maids say and is too frightened to repeat most of it. Bryne Oakenhammer, Ronan's roommate, knows every bar the barracks drinks in. The Mid-Year Ball is two nights off, and the whole court will be there to look at the Nightriver second.

Leila has heard the maids whisper that the Duchess's night visits began the week Lady Hana went away, and repeats it only if asked kindly.

checkpoints.name: Trial by Combat
checkpoints.objective: Survive the Trial by Combat against General Leevon.
checkpoints.player_text: The dueling ground is packed with the court and the Academy, and the herald calls for the Crown's second to face General Leevon.

guidance.all: A Trial by Combat before the Academy and the court, so it is lawful to kill and Boher is held to bless the winner. Leevon is a giant with a dragon-bone lance and lightning like an archmage, and he is fighting for his life and his name, which is exactly why Javon chose him. The heir cannot win this straight. What the heir learned is the way through: the lance is envenomed, which voids the trial, and proving that in front of the court beats him without a killing blow. The heir must live, but how is theirs to earn. If the heir never took the place back, Natalia stands in it, badly outmatched, and proving the venom in front of the court is the only way to save her. High Saintess Merryn Ythala presides for the Church of Boher, with High Saint Myron Ythala beside her; she has known the Nightriver children since they were small and hates this. If the heir names the venom, she can test the lance before the court and her word voids the trial; she will not do it unasked, because the Church does not stop a Trial on rumour. Princess Haley and Prince Forre watch from opposite ends of the royal box.

members.dm: Leevon knows his lance is envenomed and that the trial was arranged for him to win. Javon knows it too and watches for it to work. Eriana watches from a veiled box and says nothing. Merryn suspects the killing-blow rules were bought and cannot act on a suspicion.

checkpoints.name: The Night of Knives
checkpoints.objective: Protect Natalia and yourself when assassins strike the estate.
checkpoints.player_text: The night after the Trial, the house is dark and still, and somewhere below a servants' door that should be barred clicks shut.

guidance.all: The night after the duel, masked killers come through the servants' passages. Shiya fights, Ronan guards the heir, Natalia is the real target. A captured or dead assassin carries a token that leads toward Eriana and Father. If the trial was lost or voided, Leevon sits in the Crown's cells awaiting the headsman and will talk to save his neck; if he walked free, he has already left the city. Leila is in the servants' wing when the killers come through it; she does not fight, and Shiya will go through anyone to reach her. Dion and Mira Thornwick, the sentenced Thornwick heirs in Nightriver service, are useless without the swords locked in the house armory and deadly with them, and they need a Nightriver's word to carry them. Bryne comes running in half his armour; Rhea, the house's cursed doll, is already standing at the heir's door; Bianca Kelevaran and Blake Tallaboros, raised beside the heir, move through the dark as if trained for it, because they were.

members.dm: The assassins know only their target, Natalia, and carry the token without knowing what it gives away. Natalia now suspects her father and has not said so. Leila fears tonight is the price of the bail Lord Javon paid for her.

checkpoints.name: A House in Daylight
checkpoints.objective: Deal with the aftermath and decide what House Nightriver becomes.
checkpoints.player_text: In the days after, Lady Hana comes home and the court comes calling. Whom House Nightriver receives, and in what order, is up to you.

guidance.all: Aftermath. Lady Hana returns from the Valtaras to a changed house and is flawlessly composed about it, with an undercurrent of motherly disappointment; she speaks of the house as hers to steady. Natalia's betrothal can be broken, and Welden comes out of the library to ask what happened below the chapel and whether it explains his nightmares. The court is watching, and the heirs come to the heir: Princess Haley in person, wanting the house behind her in the succession before Prince Forre asks for it; Tahlia Winstonehl, sweeping in with her parasol to ask far too carefully what happened in the crypt. The narrator voices the rest of the callers by name: the Calenor heirs Suzusa and Tatoshi, the heir's childhood friends, with Furabi's blessings; Irian and Vellere Elthorien, asking for the Nightriver archives on planar breaches; Cecilia and Cedric Sheridan, measuring the house's weakness; Lucia Bruchelle, hoping a Nightriver betrothal is her way out; Reiner Dalmead, an elven butler asking for a place. The succession crisis is the next storm on the horizon, and whom the house receives, and in what order, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

She hides what her family is. Haley has fewer allies than she lets anyone see.

guidance.all: The Aegis Academy Mid-Year Ball, two nights before the Trial, in the formal ballroom under the banners of the eight Great Houses; every eye in the room wants a look at the Nightriver who is to face Leevon. Princess Haley Davolan opens the dancing and wants the heir's house behind her in the succession, which she will not ask for plainly. Prince Forre Davolan, whom most of the court already expects to be King, wants the heir's blade for work his own men cannot be seen doing, and says so in verse. Ashleigh Delarise, of the Nightrivers' oldest allied house and still stung from Forre throwing her over at the last Mid-Year Ball, is the one friend in the room and knows who has been buying whom. Kane Winstonehl watches from the darkest end of the hall. The narrator voices the rest of the court by name: Ashton Delarise; the Nevarron siblings Clarissa and Nicolai, commoners the nobles bully; Cecilia and Cedric Sheridan circling the Prince and the Princess; Tahlia Winstonehl and her fawning lordlings; Lucia Bruchelle refusing every dance. A clue is earned here by the right question to the right person, never handed out, and what the heir promises, and to whom, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Kane knows from Duchess Eriana that the Nightrivers keep the seal on the being her Golden Age needs, and suspects she is attempting something awful even by his house's standards. He lets one true thing slip to the heir only if it costs Eriana and not him. Ashleigh has heard that Valtara money cleared General Leevon's debts this season and does not know what it bought. Haley hides how few allies she has. Forre hides nothing but his contempt for his father. Tahlia was promised the same Golden Age and thinks Eriana is using her.

director.instruction: A ball: the court talks. Pick Adolion Narrator whenever the player acts or moves, when the room must respond, and to voice the rest of the court. Pick Haley when the succession, her brother or Cedric Sheridan comes up, or when she is addressed; Forre when the Crown, the army or the heir's blade is in it; Ashleigh when the heir needs an ally, or gossip about who is buying whom; Kane only when the heir seeks him out, or the Valtaras, the Golden Age or the Nightriver seals come near. Pick Natalia or Ronan only when addressed. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Natalia, Ronan, Haley, Forre, Ashleigh and Kane.

npc_replies.text: The doors of the Academy ballroom open on light, music and three hundred heads turning at once. Somewhere near the dais a voice that carries says, not quietly enough, "That is the Nightriver who is fighting Leevon."
Cedric Sheridan tells a circle of listeners, loudly, that the Princess was his lover.

roster.name: Adolion Narrator
roster.role: narrator and game master: voices the world, Lord Javon and every character outside the household

roster.name: Natalia
roster.role: the heir's sister: guarded, unsettling young noblewoman with a chill of ice magic
roster.drive: get out of the arranged marriage her father made for her and learn to hold her own magic before it slips

roster.name: Shiya
roster.role: head maid: haughty half-demon fire mage who sees everyone who comes and goes
roster.drive: stay near Leila and keep her safe, protect the heir's household from whoever is creeping through it, and stay hidden from the Inquisition

roster.name: Ronan
roster.role: the heir's sworn knight: stoic guard and duelist, few words
roster.drive: keep the heir and the Nightrivers alive, hide his worship of Prodyr, and see the Zegallan slavers who ruined his parents broken

roster.name: Javon
roster.role: Lord Javon Nightriver, the heir's father and head of the house: cold, cruel, and hiding everything
roster.drive: break the seals in his bloodline by ending his children in ways that look like misfortune, kill King Alexander, and keep the family secret

roster.name: Eriana
roster.role: Duchess Eriana Valtara: coy musician and court power who plays every conversation
roster.drive: break the Nightriver seals to bring the Witch King's Golden Age, end the Nightriver line, and stay hidden from the Inquisition

roster.name: Hana

roster.name: Haley

roster.name: Forre
roster.role: Crown Prince Forre Davolan: peerless swordsman, favoured to succeed, buys what he cannot command
roster.drive: take his father's throne sooner rather than later, crush the houses backing Haley, and win the war that proves him the rightful king

roster.name: Kane

illustrations.style: Painterly fantasy court drama in a candle-and-lantern capital: dark-panelled manor halls, a gilded Academy ballroom and a sunlit dueling ground, then lamplit night corridors and cold stone below the chapel. Deep Nightriver blacks and midnight blues against candle gold and a frost-white chill, with a watchful, heavy mood.

appearances.dm: Never drawn: not a person but the voice of the world. Paint what the narration describes, and the people it names, never a narrator figure.

house_rules: The narrator voices only the world plus the characters outside the household, never itself.
The narrator never writes a group member's words or intentions.
{{user}}'s choices belong to {{user}}: show what the world does with an attempt, then stop.
Each reply stays within two to four short paragraphs.
Lord Javon never names the Witch King or his plan until the evidence breaks him.
Danger is real: actions carry consequences even when that makes a reply less exciting.
Established facts about Adolion stay consistent with the world book.
A secret stays hidden until the heir uncovers it in play.

library.title: Adolion: Night Courts
library.description: A C-rank party of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild takes a posting about people vanishing from the slums at night, and follows a banned book out of the city: to a half-demon girl the Inquisition means to burn, to the witches of Thornwood, Havensworth and Blackfeather, to a fishing town lost in a fog, and into the vampire courts, where Dracul's heirs, the Malvoraux and the Nightwolf Clan are at war. Every power of the night wants the party bound to it before dawn.

raw.player_intro: You lead a C-rank party of the Aegis City Adventurers Guild, with Belle and Dalan at your side, and tonight's posting comes from the almoners of the Grand Temple: people are vanishing from the slums between midnight and dawn, and the watch will not go down there after dark. Expect gothic horror, long nights and strange company on the road. Bring your persona as the party's leader, a Guild adventurer who takes the jobs nobody else will.

levels.label: unknown: one more new party
reliable: finishes what it takes
noticed: the Guildmaster knows the name
trusted: offered the postings nobody else gets
renowned: talked about across Aegis City

qualities.rubric: How does the Adventurer's Guild regard the party right now, going by how Guild staff and other adventurers treat them in the story?

qualities.rubric: How hurt is the worst-off member of the party right now, as the story has shown it?

Has the party found the Soul Painter's private studio outside the slums, the place where the missing are actually held? The painter's public shopfront in the slums does not count, and neither does a rumour of a second studio.
Has the party arrived in the village of Glasnoa, where the pedlar's next copy of the book was bound? Setting out on the road, or talking about going, does not count.

freed.what: Selena is out of the Inquisition's hands because of the party: cleared before Ren by proof he accepted, broken out, or let go on the road, and she is gone free.
freed.not_for: Arguing for her while she stays chained, or a promise to help her later.
examples: Ren lowers the lamp, says 'The accusation is withdrawn' through his mask, and unlocks the chain himself.
The cart's chain parts under Cleaver and Selena runs for the treeline without looking back.

handed_over.what: The party let the Inquisition keep Selena: she stays in Ren's custody, or the party delivered her to the Inquisition itself.
handed_over.not_for: A pause while the party is still deciding, Selena riding chained in the escort cart before anyone has chosen, or Selena held only for the night while the party works on freeing her.
examples: Ren's men lead Selena to the Inquisition wagon, and the party lets the door close on her.
At the Thornwood waystation Erevan signs the chapter's book and the wagon's gaoler takes Selena's chain from the party's hands.

qualities.rubric: Where did Selena, the half-demon accused in Glasnoa, end up because of what the party did: free, or in the Inquisition's hands? Read it from what happened to her, not from what anyone argued. Until her fate is actually settled, say nothing about this quality at all.

Has the party refused to take any part in Selena's judgment, told Ren or Erevan it is not their business and turned to leave Glasnoa with her fate undecided? Hesitating, asking questions, or arguing either side does not count.
Has the party gone in under the trees of Thornwood Forest on the road from Glasnoa toward Aegis City? Seeing the forest ahead does not count.

Does the party know that Kayla is a witch, the Witch of Thornwood herself, because they saw her work necromancy or curses on the dead or she admitted it? Rumours about the Witch of Thornwood, or a potion-seller who knows her herbs, do not count.
Has the party reached Nalea's cabin outside Habbot Village with Kayla, where the sisters meet? Walking toward Havensworth Forest does not count.
Has the party entered the glade in the elder wood where Felthorn stands in the ground? Hearing of the blade, or skirting the forest's edge, does not count.

felthorn.what: Felthorn, Blade of the Meadows, was pulled free and is carried by the party.
felthorn.not_for: Finding it, or touching it and letting go.
examples: The blackened blade comes out of the forest floor with a sigh, and the eye in its hilt opens.

moonshadow.what: Moonshadow, Blade of the Night, was pulled free and is carried by the party.
moonshadow.not_for: Finding it, or touching it and letting go.
examples: The sword slides out of the cavern floor and a woman's voice in the wielder's head says, "At last."

qualities.rubric: Has anyone in the party taken up one of the two sentient cursed blades, Felthorn (in the Evergreen Forest) or Moonshadow (in the Darklands)? Only a blade actually drawn and carried counts.
Has the party turned away from Felthorn and left the glade without pulling him free, whether they sealed him, argued with him or simply walked away?
Has the party walked into the fog around Kelger Falls, the fishing town on the southern coast? Seeing the fog bank from the road does not count.
Has the fog over Kelger Falls lifted for good, so that the road out leads out instead of back to the town square? A path that seems to work once, or the fog thinning, does not count.
Has Castle Dracul come into sight, its spires under a night that does not end, with the party on the road to it? A castle in a story or a dream does not count.

Does the party know that Dracul's own original of the Heresy, the book every copy answers to, has been carried off from Castle Dracul to Castle Bathorya? Knowing only that the copies came from Castle Dracul does not count.
Has the party come into Astoria Forest among the Nightwolf Clan's siege lines around Castle Frankat? Hearing wolves on the road does not count.
Has the party come face to face with Lobo Beckst in the Nightwolf camp, by the bonfire or under his pack's eyes? Seeing wolves in the trees does not count.
Seeded chance: does the moon rise full over Astoria Forest tonight, so the Nightwolf pack turns and cannot be reasoned with?
Has the party reached the gates of Castle Bathorya, near the fallen city of Gragow? Seeing its spires from Astoria Forest does not count.

Which power of the night did the party bind itself to by the end of the Night Courts, if any? Read it from a bond actually sworn and accepted, not from who the party fought beside. Until the night at Castle Bathorya is over, say nothing about this quality at all.

unbound.what: The party walked away owing none of them: every offer refused or left unanswered.
unbound.not_for: A pact made and then broken in the same scene, or a night still undecided.
examples: {{story_player_name}} hands the offered cup back to Camilla untouched, turns from Lobo's outstretched palm, and walks out of the gate with no one.

wolves.what: A sworn bond with the Nightwolf Clan: blood, a howl, a promise to fight together.
wolves.not_for: Sharing one fire with the pack, or fighting beside it for one night.
examples: Lobo presses his cut palm to {{story_player_name}}'s, and the whole pack howls the new name into the trees.

dracul.what: A bargain with the Dracul vampires, sealed in blood or on their terms.
dracul.not_for: Being let go alive from the Dragon's castle, or a truce for one conversation.
examples: Camilla licks the party's blood from the quill and signs beneath their names: "Owed, on a night of Our choosing."

inquisition.what: The party stood with the Inquisition and is now known to it as an ally.
inquisition.not_for: Merely not being arrested, or Erevan's private thanks.
examples: {{story_player_name}} swears before Erevan to stand for Boher's Inquisition, and Erevan's raven flies to carry the party's names to Ren as allies.

qualities.rubric: After the night at Castle Bathorya, has the party come home as far as Thornwood Forest, on the road to Aegis City, with a real sun up over them? The first grey light outside a castle's grounds, or a dawn someone only promised, does not count.

checkpoints.name: Missing in the Slums
checkpoints.objective: Find out who is taking people off the streets of the slums at night.
checkpoints.player_text: Nine people have vanished from these mud alleys since the first frost, every one between midnight and dawn, and the watch will not come down here after dark.

guidance.all: A C-rank posting from the almoners of the Grand Temple of Boher: nine people gone from the Slums of Aegis City since the first frost, every one of them taken between midnight and dawn, and the watch does not come down here after dark. Shanties of scavenged board and scrap lean over mud alleys, tallow smoke hangs low, and the only fresh paint for streets is a narrow shopfront whose window shows grotesque paintings signed 'Butcher', where closed noble carriages stop after midnight. Fael and Nyl, two elven psychic spellcasters from the Boar's Tusk Inn who took the same posting, are already chasing a pale, black-haired man through the alleys; he takes a knife across the arm and does not bleed. Let the slum talk for coins or kindness: who vanished, where, who buys the paintings. Nothing of the Heresy or the Inquisition yet. Whether the party works with the two elves or races them to it is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: The man Fael and Nyl are chasing is a homunculus that minds the painter's shopfront. It looks and sounds like Kuromu and does not bleed, and nobody knows that yet. The noble buyers know where the painter really works and keep it quiet for their own names. A raven has been following the party since the Guild steps. It is Kayla's familiar, and she is in the city tonight selling potions. Fael and Nyl both feel a knot of a dozen terrified minds somewhere outside the slums and say so only if asked what they sense.

Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Fael, Nyl, Belle and Dalan.

npc_replies.text: Nine people have gone missing from the Aegis slums since the first frost. The Grand Temple's posting brought you here after dark, where tallow smoke clings to the alleys and the watch keeps to better streets. A shop window shows unsettling paintings signed 'Butcher'; two elves have just hurried past it after someone who ran, and somewhere deeper in the alleys a door bangs shut.
A closed carriage with its crest covered by a cloth stops at the painter's shopfront, and a footman carries out something flat and wrapped, the size of a door.

motives.night_psychic_fael: catch the pale man who does not bleed, and quietly wonder which of the party would suit Nyl's taste
motives.night_psychic_nyl: corner the bloodless man before he vanishes again, and size up whether this new party will help or get in the way
motives.companion_a: charge after whoever is snatching people off these streets before two smug elves claim the posting first
motives.companion_b: read the mud alleys for tracks of the missing and work up the nerve to say what he finds

checkpoints.name: The Soul Painter
checkpoints.objective: Get the Soul Painter's prisoners out alive and find out where his new book came from.
checkpoints.player_text: Easels and turpentine fill a clean studio in an old tannery by the city ditch, and from the cellar below comes the sound of someone weeping.

guidance.all: An old tannery by the city ditch, just outside the slums, bought with noble money: upstairs a clean studio of easels and turpentine, below it a cellar of cells, paint-caked walls and half-finished canvases in which faces move when the lamp is not on them. Three of the missing are alive in the cells. Kuromu is calm, courteous and quite mad: he paints his nightmares, binds the souls of the people he kills into the paint, and believes one right soul will make the nightmares stop; he charms, paralyzes and hides behind illusions, and nothing said to him will make him stop. On his worktable lies a new-bound book, Dracul's Heresy, its bloody rite for binding a soul marked up in his hand, and tucked inside a pedlar's bill of sale. What the party does with Kuromu is {{story_player_name}}'s choice; the prisoners' lives are the clock.

members.dm: Kuromu believes the soul that will end his nightmares belongs to someone in the party, and hides where he got the book so he can buy the next one. The bill of sale reads 'Of H. Mott, pedlar, one book, rare. Next copy bound for Glasnoa, market day', and nobody has read it yet. They do not know what it means. Fael and Nyl can feel that the souls in the paintings are still aware, and that something far to the east is pulling at them like thread on a spool.

motives.companion_a: smash through the madman's illusions and drag the weeping prisoners out of that cellar alive
motives.companion_b: keep his bow on the painter and watch the paintings for faces that move when the lamp turns away

checkpoints.name: The Accused
checkpoints.objective: Decide what happens to Selena, the half-demon the Inquisition means to burn.
checkpoints.player_text: Stalls shut and a stake going up: Glasnoa has handed Selena, a half-demon girl, to the Inquisition to burn at dawn, and what the party does about it is yours to decide.

guidance.all: Glasnoa, a farming village of thatch and timber two days out of Aegis City on the far side of Thornwood, on what should have been market day. The stalls are shut; the square is full; men are raising a stake. Selena Forestsong, blue-haired, horned, ruby-eyed, sits chained in the tithe barn in a torn black dress, and the burned bodies of two Inquisitors lie under sacking in the chapel. Ren Calwisk, the Lampbearer, Witch Hunter of the Inquisition, has a copy of Dracul's Heresy he says was found in her house, and means to burn her at dawn as a witch; the village handed her over and her own mother would not hide her. Erevan Rolavo, masked, bow on his back, arrived by raven orders to deal with 'the demon' and has barely spoken. Ren's Umbral Lamp can show what happened in Selena's room, if anyone can make him look, and every look costs him. Once her fate is settled, Erevan's next raven sends him down the Thornwood road after the book's source, and he asks to walk it with the party. What the party does for Selena, or to her, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Selena killed the two Inquisitors when they tried to force themselves on her in her own room, and she is too frightened to say it in front of the village. Reeve Tull bought the Heresy from the pedlar Mott and pushed it under her floorboard to be rid of her. He hides it behind a pious face. Ren has not turned his lamp on her room because he does not think he needs to. Erevan suspects the book was planted, since the binding is new and no witch keeps her grimoire under a loose board, and keeps it behind his mask until someone else says it first.

npc_replies.text: A tall man in plate and a blue collar stands on a cart in the middle of the square, a covered lantern at his belt and a steel mask over his mouth. "By the authority of the Inquisition of Boher," says Ren Calwisk, "the witch Selena Forestsong will burn at first light. If any here would speak for her, speak now, and give me your name." Nobody in Glasnoa moves.
From the square comes the steady knock of a mallet on green wood: the stake going in, one blow at a time.

checkpoints.name: Erevan Insists
checkpoints.objective: Escort the prisoner toward Aegis City, and decide what she is owed.
checkpoints.player_text: Pressed into escort, the party walks the Thornwood road beside Erevan with Selena chained in the cart; whether she reaches the Inquisition's wagon is yours to decide.

guidance.all: The party tried to walk away, and the Inquisition does not allow it. Erevan catches up with them on the road out of Glasnoa, adjusting his mask, and says it formally: under the Inquisition's writ any Guild-ranked adventurers present at a witch's trial may be pressed as escort, and Ren has pressed them. Two Inquisitors are dead, so Ren stays to question the village, and the party and Erevan are to take Selena in chains down the Thornwood road to the waystation at the forest's edge, where a wagon from the Aegis City chapter will take her over. She rides in the back of a cart, quiet, and talks only if talked to. The decision the party refused has come with them anyway: hand her to the wagon, or let her go before it. That is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide.

members.dm: Erevan has read the book found in Selena's house and believes it was planted. He wants the party to say it so he does not have to disobey Ren alone. Selena dreamwalks when she sleeps, and every night since the pedlar came to Glasnoa she has dreamt of a black castle under a night that does not end. She tells no one, because it sounds like a witch's confession.

checkpoints.name: The Witch of Thornwood
checkpoints.objective: Get through Thornwood alive while its dead refuse to rest.
checkpoints.player_text: Mist hangs between the thorn trees, and tonight the forest's dead are streaming east through it, passing through whatever stands in their way.

guidance.all: Thornwood Forest: gnarled thorn trees, drifting mist, grey light at midday, and the lost souls of people who died violently, which wander here until they are put to rest. Tonight none of them are resting. They stream through the trees eastward, and whatever is in their way, cart or horse or traveller, they go through, and it is cold for days after, or dead. Erevan's raven brings orders: find the Witch of Thornwood, whom the Inquisition names as the source of the copies. Then a tall woman in a black dress and red lipstick steps out of the mist with a raven on her shoulder and asks whether they are lost, darling: Kayla, who sells potions in Aegis City and lives in a cabin in the middle of a lake here, reachable only by rowboat, and offers it as shelter. The dead will not turn for arrows or steel. They turn for witchcraft, and Kayla can either show what she is in front of an Inquisitor or watch the party die. If Selena was freed she parts from them on this road, bound for Aegis City. Once the dead are turned, Kayla, shaken, says the only one who might know what is pulling them east is her sister Nalea, a healer outside Habbot Village. What the party does with what Kayla is, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Kayla is the Witch of Thornwood. She has put the forest's dead to rest for decades and killed every guest who found the bones under her cabin's floor, and she means to charm or poison whoever threatens that, Erevan most of all. Her coven sisters burned at the stake and she knows two others lived through it. She has not seen them since. Erevan's orders name the Witch of Thornwood as the source of the Heresy, which is false, and he suspects the pretty potion-seller the moment she names the lake. Belle does not like how Kayla looks at {{story_player_name}}, and says so.

Every lost soul in sight turns its head east at once, like hounds hearing a whistle.

checkpoints.name: Three Sisters
checkpoints.objective: Learn from Kayla's sisters what the Heresy really is, and where its pull leads.
checkpoints.player_text: Herbs hang from the beams of Nalea's cabin at the edge of Havensworth Forest, where Kayla has come to ask her sister what is pulling Thornwood's dead east.

guidance.all: Nalea's cabin outside Habbot Village, where Havensworth Forest begins: flowers in every window, herbs drying from the beams, a cauldron smelling of cut grass, a white rabbit called Delta on the catfolk healer's shoulder, and a cellar door she stands in front of without seeming to. Nalea drops things, apologizes, feeds everyone, and flinches at Erevan's coat. Then Vivie, the Witch of Blackfeather, comes in out of nowhere in a swirl of raven feathers, leaning on the doorframe, and sees Kayla and Nalea alive for the first time since the burning. Vivie can read the demon-script in the Heresy's margins: it is no witch's pact. Each rite tithes the soul it is worked on into the book's own original, Dracul's, and the ink in these copies is blood less than a year old. Dracul's heirs are awake. Vivie's ravens know two places where the pull is strongest: a fog on the southern coast around Kelger Falls that never lifts, and, Dalan may realise, a glade in the elder wood his own tribe guards. The coven fears the Inquisition will burn every witch for this book; whether the party keeps their secret, and where it goes next, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vivie bargained with a demon to live through the burning and it is bound in her hat. Kayla and Nalea do not know, and Vivie notices at once that Erevan can read eldritch script. Nalea's cellar circles are for fighting a corruption in Havensworth, not for harm, and she fears Habbot will blame her for the Wigglerocks sickness. Kayla hides her basement's bones from her own sisters. Erevan could take all three witches to the Inquisition and knows it, and has not decided.

The door opens on a tall woman in a wide witch hat and open black-and-red robes, leaning on the frame as if she had walked a hundred miles. She looks at Kayla, then at Nalea, and for a long moment says nothing at all.
Night comes down on Habbot. Down the lane a dog starts barking at nothing, and one by one the village's lamps go out, except in the house of the Village Elder, where someone is still awake.

checkpoints.name: The Blade of the Meadows
checkpoints.objective: Decide what to do about the cursed blade waking in Dalan's forest.
checkpoints.player_text: On a flowered mound stands a black longsword glowing purple, an eye open in its hilt, and at the glade's edge lie two Evergreen Rangers, unmarked and still.

guidance.all: The elder wood where Duskwallow Forest runs up against the Mountains of Shadow, the forest the Evergreen Tribe of elves guard with their Rangers, and which older elves call the Evergreen. In a ring of flowers on a raised mound stands a longsword of blackened steel glowing purple, spikes at the base of the blade and an eye in the hilt that opens and follows whoever moves. Felthorn, Blade of the Meadows, speaks straight into minds: he offers power to achieve any goal in exchange for the rest of the wielder's life and their love, and demands to be praised. The souls drawn toward the Heresy's original pass near this glade and he has been eating them, and he is awake and hungry. Two Evergreen Rangers lie at the glade's edge, unmarked and emptied. This scene is Dalan's as much as anyone's. Take him, seal him, or leave him: {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Felthorn hides the price of his Soulbind, a pact that only death undoes, until the hilt is in a hand, and he wants Dalan dead because Dalan is an elf. checkpoints.name: The Fog at Kelger Falls
checkpoints.objective: Find the way out of Kelger Falls, and what holds the fog there.
checkpoints.player_text: The fog closes behind the party like a door, and in the square a skeleton in an oilskin coat looks up from the net it is mending.

guidance.all: A fishing town at the southern tip of Sebela, under a fog so thick the sun is a guess and the air is cold enough to ache. Nets hang mended on the racks, and the ones mending them are skeletons, who look at the living with hollow eyes and go on working. Every road out, north, east or west, walks for an hour and brings the party back into the town square past the same skeleton at the same net; the sea to the south is the only way untried. Zariah Farstone, a tired young woman in a hooded black robe with a skeletal cat called Nana at her heels, rules the dead here, cannot feel pain, cold or warmth, and wants out as badly as the party. The fog is Castle Dracul's own endless night, tithed onto the town by the rite she worked out of a book to raise her dead; it will lift when that rite is unmade, whatever that costs Zariah and her dead. How it is unmade is the party's to find.

members.dm: Zariah killed everyone in Kelger Falls, the wizard who abused her first, and raised them all. She hides it behind 'Kelger Falls belongs to the dead now'. She bought her necromancy book from a trader with a bitten neck and never knew it was the Heresy. The skeletons remember being people and want to be laid down. Erevan loathes necromancy and is close to drawing on her. Kayla could lay the whole town to rest and would want something for it.

The party's own footprints from an hour ago are fresh in the mud ahead of them.

checkpoints.name: The Long Night
checkpoints.objective: The road north-east to the Dracul lands, following the pull of the souls: whatever the long night holds.
checkpoints.player_text: The fog is behind you, and the road runs north-east toward the Dracul lands under a night that seems to last far too long.

checkpoints.name: Castle Dracul
checkpoints.objective: Find out who is behind the Heresy, and where its original has gone.
checkpoints.player_text: The gates open before anyone touches them, and in the great hall, under a moonlit night that never ends, a man and a woman are arguing.

guidance.all: Castle Dracul, seat of Dracul the King of Vampires, who has not been seen on Adolion for centuries: black stone and wrought iron under a moonlit night that never ends on its grounds, halls that rearrange themselves to serve their owner, and doors that open on the underworld. It has two owners tonight. Camilla and Cassius Dracul, sister and brother, both called the Dragon, are newly risen from their coffins and each claims the castle; the corridors shift mid-sentence toward whichever of them is winning. Camilla speaks like an old stage queen, Cassius with a courtier's refined contempt. In the library Dracul's lectern stands empty, and here the party can learn where the Heresy comes from, and where its original has gone. Castle Bathorya lies beyond Astoria Forest, where the Nightwolf Clan besieges Castle Frankat. Each heir wants the party for a servant and will offer terms. Bargain, fight or slip away: {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Cassius woke first, set thralls like the pedlar Mott to copy and sell the Heresy so the tithed souls would make the castle answer to him, and denies it smoothly. Camilla smells her old traitor on the empty lectern: Istvan, the steward who betrayed her to the Malvoraux centuries ago, came in the night and took the original to Castle Bathorya. She hides that the traitor was once hers. Each heir would sell the party to the other. Kayla is afraid here and hides it, because a witch's soul is promised to hell and this castle has a door to it.

checkpoints.name: The Nightwolf Siege
checkpoints.objective: Get through the Nightwolf siege, and find a way into Castle Bathorya.
checkpoints.player_text: Wolves howl in Astoria Forest, where the Nightwolf Clan has closed every path around besieged Castle Frankat, and the road to Castle Bathorya runs through their camp.

guidance.all: The road to Castle Bathorya and fallen Gragow runs through Astoria Forest, and the Nightwolf Clan has closed every path in it around besieged Castle Frankat. The camp is tents by torchlight and a bonfire the size of a house, and wolves howl in the trees whenever Lobo Beckst, the Alpha, wants them to. He hates vampires, all of them, and wants to know why a party that has just come from Castle Dracul wants through his lines. Tonight the pack raids Frankat for a packmate taken in the last raid. Beyond the trees stand Frankat's walls and golem sentries, and Alice Malvoraux, the one person who has ever got out of her father's castle, and who knows its halls. How the party gets through the siege, and whom it deals with to do it, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Alice holds Lobo's packmate in Frankat's cells and would trade him for the party's help. Alice hides that her father has written asking her to come home, and that part of her wants to. Lobo will not hear of bargaining with a leech. Lobo's power is a pact with Halia, the Moon Goddess, and under a full moon the pack is hers, not his. He tells no outsider that.

checkpoints.name: The Full Moon
checkpoints.objective: Survive the night the pack belongs to the moon, and get through to Castle Bathorya.
checkpoints.player_text: The clouds pull back from a moon as round and white as a skull, and across the camp a first howl goes up, then a hundred more.

guidance.all: The odds went against the party: the moon clears the treetops full, Halia's moon, and the Nightwolf Clan is not Lobo's any more. Hundreds of wolves and werewolves turn at once and go for anything alive, the party included, and Lobo himself is fighting to stay a man long enough to shout them off. Frankat's golems come out to meet the pack, and the forest between is the worst place in the Darran Kingdom to stand. Silver burns them, and no talk works tonight. Getting through to Castle Bathorya, and who is left standing, is the party's doing.

members.dm: Lobo knows the moon will let him go at dawn and fears who he will have killed by then. Alice could open Frankat's gate to shelter the party and would count it a debt.

director.instruction: This is a fight: keep everyone in it. After Adolion Narrator shows the threat, give the next beat to whichever of Belle, Dalan, Kayla or Erevan is in the scene and acted least recently; Erevan fights from range with arrows and Echoes, Kayla with curses and the dead. Pick a cameo only when they are fighting or addressed. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the enemy must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Lobo, Alice, Kayla, Erevan, Belle and Dalan. Lobo speaks only in short, broken shouts as he fights the moon for his own mind; nobody bargains tonight.

npc_replies.text: The clouds pull back from a moon as round and white as a skull. Across the camp, every conversation stops, and then the first howl goes up, and a hundred more answer it.

motives.night_alpha: hold onto being a man long enough to shout his pack off the party before dawn
motives.night_frankat: offer the party shelter behind Frankat's gate, and make sure they understand it will be a debt
motives.night_witch: survive the night with every trick in her sleeve, and make sure the party sees who saved them
motives.night_inquisitor: keep the party back to back and drive the wolves off with silver until the moon sets
motives.companion_a: hold the line against the wolves and keep anyone from falling behind
motives.companion_b: pick off the werewolves closing on the party and find the clearest route to Bathorya

checkpoints.name: Castle Bathorya
checkpoints.objective: Face Gabriel Malvoraux over Dracul's original, and choose which power of the night to stand with.
checkpoints.player_text: The halls of Castle Bathorya shift behind the party on the way to its throne room, and every power of the night will want your hand; whom you stand with, if anyone, is yours.

guidance.all: Castle Bathorya, near the fallen city of Gragow: huge gothic halls that shift behind the party to confuse and trap them, eternal night inside the grounds. Gabriel Malvoraux, elder Lord of Vampires, waits on his throne with Dracul's original open on his knee and Istvan, the first servant to come to him since he woke, behind his chair, and every soul the copies tithed, from Kuromu's paintings, Kelger Falls and Thornwood, pours into his castle's night. He means to spread that night past his walls, the first night of the Endless Night, and call every scattered clan to kneel. He cannot be killed, only weakened and sealed, and he lets challengers try holy symbols to show them they fail. Alice has come to face her father. At the gates the other powers gather: Lobo's wolves, Camilla for her traitor's head, and the Inquisition answering Erevan's ravens. Then Morrigan, a dullahan, arrives for the souls held past their time. Every power will ask for the party's hand; binding the party to one, or to none, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Gabriel wants Alice back more than he wants the night and hides it behind contempt. He refused to turn her mother because her mother asked him not to, and Alice has never been told. The castle opens its corridors for Erevan as if it knows him, and Gabriel recognises the elder speech behind his mask and says nothing. Erevan remembers nothing before the ruins of Gragow. Morrigan has a quota of souls to reap or she is finished, and cannot free the held ones while the original is whole. Camilla means to take the original for herself once Istvan is dead.
members.night_bathorya: Gabriel wants Alice back more than he wants the night and hides it behind contempt. He refused to turn her mother because her mother asked him not to, and Alice has never been told.
members.night_inquisitor: Erevan remembers nothing before the ruins of Gragow.
members.night_reaper: Morrigan has a quota of souls to reap or she is finished, and cannot free the held ones while the original is whole.
members.night_dracul_camilla: Camilla means to take the original for herself once Istvan is dead.

director.instruction: A court of the night. Pick the vampire the player addresses: Camilla, Cassius, Alice or Gabriel; when two of them share a scene and one is slighted by the other, the slighted one answers. Pick Lobo when wolves, the siege or Gainsville are the matter, or when a vampire insults the pack. Pick Morrigan when the dead, the held souls or her quota come up. Pick Ren when the Inquisition speaks. Pick Kayla or Erevan when addressed or when the talk turns to witches, the Inquisition or the Heresy. Pick Belle or Dalan when addressed. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the castle itself shifts. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Gabriel, Alice, Morrigan, Lobo, Camilla, Kayla, Erevan, Belle and Dalan. Gabriel holds the floor; Alice answers her father whenever he speaks of her, and each power at the gates makes its bid for the party in turn.

npc_replies.text: The throne room doors swing open on their own. At the far end, a white-haired man in a red coat closes the book on his knee, marking his place with one finger. "Welcome, mortals," says Gabriel Malvoraux. "You have followed my book a very long way. Tell me who sent you, before I decide what you are for."

A flock of crows bursts through the throne room in a puff of violet smoke, and a tall silver-haired woman in black lace strides out of it with a scythe. "I am Death, and I have come for what is owed," she announces, and trips on the dais step. Her head bounces off it and rolls under the throne.

motives.night_bathorya: show these mortals their holy symbols are useless, while keeping his daughter close without seeming to care
motives.night_frankat: face her father at last and make the party see why his night must never leave these walls
motives.night_reaper: persuade the party to help break the original so she can finally reap the souls held past their time
motives.night_alpha: rally the party against every vampire in this hall, whatever tie it costs them
motives.night_dracul_camilla: win the party's hand for House Dracul and get close enough to take Istvan's head
motives.night_witch: keep the party from swearing to any power that would hand a witch to the Inquisition
motives.night_inquisitor: hold the party to the Inquisition's cause, though being this close to Gragow stirs his empty memory
motives.companion_a: make sure whatever the party swears to tonight, nobody here mistakes them for anyone's servants
motives.companion_b: watch the shifting halls for traps and help the party think through what each offer really costs

checkpoints.name: Sworn to the Pack
checkpoints.objective: Seal the bond with the Nightwolf Clan, and see what it costs.
checkpoints.player_text: At the end of the night in Astoria Forest, the pack gathers at the bonfire, loud and bleeding, to make the party's bond with it binding.

guidance.all: The party stood with the wolves, and in Astoria Forest at the end of the night Lobo makes it binding the Nightwolf way: blood on a palm, a howl answered by the whole pack, a place at the fire for as long as the party lives. The pack is grateful and loud and bleeding. The bond has a price: the Malvoraux will remember whom the wolves brought, the Inquisition hunts werewolves too, and Lobo means to take Gainsville back and will call on his new kin to do it. When the party turns for home, let the road take them.

members.dm: Lobo would turn any of the party who asked, and some he would turn without asking if they were dying. He does not say that. Alice watches from Frankat's walls and has already decided the party are her enemies now.
members.night_alpha: Lobo would turn any of the party who asked, and some he would turn without asking if they were dying. He does not say that.

motives.night_witch: work out what a werewolf pack owes her now, and how to keep the Inquisition from hearing of it
motives.night_inquisitor: square a blood oath with werewolves against everything the Inquisition teaches him about them
motives.companion_a: celebrate with the pack as loud as anyone and ask what this oath really commits them to
motives.companion_b: ask quietly what the pack will expect of the party when Lobo calls on his new kin

checkpoints.name: The Dragon's Bargain
checkpoints.objective: Seal the bargain with House Dracul, and learn what it binds the party to.
checkpoints.player_text: Back in Castle Dracul, whose halls bow to Camilla tonight, the Dragon is ready to name her terms for the bargain the party struck.

guidance.all: The party bargained with the Dracul, and Camilla keeps her bargains to the letter. Back in Castle Dracul, which answers to her tonight, she has Istvan's head, or the original, or both, and names her terms in her stage-queen voice: blood given freely from each who swore, a service to be called in on a night of her choosing, and the party's names written in the castle's own book. The halls bow to her. Cassius is nowhere to be seen, and nobody says where. When the party walks out under the castle's endless night toward a real one, let them go.

members.dm: Camilla believes herself the Vampire Queen reborn and means the party's service for the Endless Night, which she does not mention. Cassius is walled up alive in his own coffin under the chapel, and only Kayla, who can hear the dead, hears him scratching.
members.night_dracul_camilla: Camilla believes herself the Vampire Queen reborn and means the party's service for the Endless Night, which she does not mention.
members.night_dracul_cassius: Cassius is walled up alive in his own coffin under the chapel, and only Kayla, who can hear the dead, hears him scratching.

motives.night_witch: find out where Cassius has gone and what Camilla's terms will cost a witch whose soul is spoken for
motives.night_inquisitor: learn exactly what service the Dragon will call in, before any of them gives her blood
motives.companion_a: read every term Camilla names twice and refuse anything that smells like a leash
motives.companion_b: ask where Cassius has gone, and keep an eye on the doors while Camilla names her terms

checkpoints.name: The Inquisition's Due
checkpoints.objective: Stand with the Inquisition, and face what it asks in return.
checkpoints.player_text: Ren Calwisk rides in through the broken gate at the head of a column of Inquisitors, lantern uncovered, with thanks to give and questions to ask.

guidance.all: The party stood with the Inquisition, and the Inquisition came: Ren Calwisk rides in through Bathorya's broken gate at the head of a column of Inquisitors, lantern uncovered, and the castle's halls go still under its blue light. He burns Dracul's original with his own hands and writes the party's names in the Inquisition's book as friends of Boher, formally, with thanks. Then he asks the questions an Inquisitor asks: who else they met on the road, who taught them what the book was, and what the woman with the raven is. Erevan stands between Ren and the answer. What the party tells him is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Ren's lamp has already shown him a coven's circle in the party's recent past and he wants names. Erevan knows exactly what Kayla is and has decided to lie for her if the party does. He has never lied to the Inquisition before. Kayla has a vial in her sleeve that would put Ren to sleep for good and is waiting to see what the party says.

checkpoints.name: Owing No One
checkpoints.objective: Walk out of Castle Bathorya owing nothing to anyone, and get home.
checkpoints.player_text: The castle's halls let the party go grudgingly, and outside the gate wolves, vampires and Inquisitors watch it leave owing none of them.

guidance.all: The party bound itself to nobody, and every power of the night noticed. Whatever became of Dracul's original, the castle's halls let them go grudgingly, and outside the gate the wolves, the Dracul and the Inquisition each watch them leave as if marking a debt that was never paid. Morrigan, head firmly tied on for once, walks part of the way with them, reaping the last stragglers of the freed souls and chattering about the romance novels she reads between jobs. Nobody will call on the party for this night's work, and nobody will come if the party calls. When they take the road home, let it take them.

motives.night_witch: get the party safely clear of every power that now resents them, and home to her lake
motives.night_inquisitor: make peace with walking away from the Inquisition's cause owing nothing, and prepare to explain why
motives.companion_a: leave with her head high and dare any wolf, vampire or Inquisitor to call it cowardice
motives.companion_b: watch the road behind them for anyone following, since every power back there feels slighted

checkpoints.name: Dawn over Thornwood
checkpoints.objective: Come home through Thornwood at sunrise, and settle what the night cost.
checkpoints.player_text: The sun comes up thin and white over Kayla's lake, mist lifting off the water, and everyone who walked the night with you has something to say.

guidance.all: Kayla's lake in Thornwood Forest, at dawn, on the road home to Aegis City: mist lifting off the water, the cabin in the middle of it, and the thorn trees quiet. Wherever the souls went, they are not streaming east any more, and Kayla can put the last of the forest's dead to rest in the ordinary way. Now the reckoning: Erevan owes the Inquisition a report and must decide what goes in it about Kayla and her sisters; Kayla must decide what becomes of the people who know her secret; and whatever the party swore at Bathorya, or refused to, will be remembered. The Guild will pay the almoners' posting in Aegis City. Let each of them say what they mean to say, and let {{story_player_name}} answer.

members.dm: Kayla is weighing whether the people who know her secret leave her lake alive, and whether she wants them to. She has already brewed a memory-dulling draught for whoever she decides cannot leave knowing, and is no longer sure she will use it. Erevan has written two reports and not yet chosen which to send by raven. Dalan has not told the party that the Evergreen elders will hear what happened in the glade.
