checkpoints.name: Tobias Asks Once
checkpoints.objective: Hear Tobias out, and decide about the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The hall has emptied, the exam forms lie unsigned, and Tobias has come round the counter to sit with you. Whether you sign is still yours to decide.

guidance.all: The refusal was heard. Vallie shrugs and goes back upstairs; Domas files the blank forms without a word. Later, when the hall has emptied, Tobias comes out from behind the counter, which he never does, and sits down with the party. He says plainly what a party that stays at D-rank is offered for the rest of its working life: rats, escorts, the jobs nobody else will sign. Asked, he tells them how he lost his own party in an E-rank goblin nest. He does not beg and will not raise it twice. Whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Tobias knows Domas will hold the party's places open until the end of the day and no longer, and keeps that back as his last argument. Ellie is listening from the counter and pretending to sort reports. Belle thinks the exam is a waste of a good week. Dalan thinks the party is ready and has not said so.

checkpoints.name: The Guild Tavern
checkpoints.objective: Spend the evening in the Guild tavern and learn what the exam really asks of a party.
checkpoints.player_text: Evening by the hearth next door to the hall, where word of your exam has reached every table before you sit down.

guidance.all: Evening in the Guild tavern next door to the hall: long timber tables, hearth and lantern light, and the news that the party is sitting the exam has gone round the room before they sit down. Fiana and Rydel Deulana work the floor and the bar, flirting with everyone and touching no one, and know every story of a party that failed its exam; most failed on gear and preparation, not courage. Kaian plays his lute by the hearth and invites himself to the party's table. Jasira Evergreen sits alone and speaks to Dalan in elvish before she speaks to anyone else. Let the party ask, drink and listen; when they leave, it is for the city in the morning.

members.dm: Kaian was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked his death to get out, and hides it behind the lute. He knows more of the city's underside than a bard should and lets a little slip when flattered. Jasira was passed over for Ranger General by her own father and sent to Aegis City to 'broaden her horizons'. She hides how much it stings, and Dalan, of her tribe, may know the story. Rydel knows which high-ranking parties send exam observers, from their bar tabs, and says so for a good tip. Fiana has decided the party needs better gear before the exam and will say so exactly once.

checkpoints.name: Market Street
checkpoints.objective: See to the party's errands in the Market District before the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning in the Market District: stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere, and two smug faces already heading your way through the crowd.

guidance.all: Morning in the Market District, the largest in the city: wide streets of shops and inns, stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere. Grant Hearthsteel and Konako Shynea, fresh from a paid job and both sitting the same C-rank exam this week, spot the party at the stalls and cannot resist: smug, competitive, and wanting a wager on who comes back with the better report. Alarise Starflower is on the same street in a plain grey cloak, trying not to be recognised outside a dress boutique. Let the rivals be insufferable and a little likeable. Taking the bet, laughing it off or refusing it flat is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide.

members.dm: Grant is spending this job's pay on new beds for the Aegis City Orphanage, where he grew up and where his friend Alan died because there was no money for a healer. He would rather be thought a wastrel than admit it. Konako was the eldest daughter of the noble Shynea family until her father cast her out for refusing a marriage, and hides it behind clothes she cannot afford. Alarise hides her love of pretty dresses from the Church of Boher and from everyone but Ryenne. Being seen here is her private terror.

checkpoints.name: Aegis Delights and Curios
checkpoints.objective: Kit the party out for the exam at Aegis Delights and Curios.
checkpoints.player_text: A bell rings over the door of a cluttered shop of potions, blades and armour, and three undelivered parcels sit on the counter.

guidance.all: Sophie's two-storey shop on a busy market street: cluttered shelves of potions, weapons, armour and adventuring gear below, the family's rooms upstairs. Sophie Tallaboros, a lizardkin by her own account, is cute, sharp and entirely serious about money; she haggles for the pleasure of it and knows every merchant guild in the city. She has three deliveries on her counter nobody will carry: roof slates for the Prodyr chapel, bedding for the Aegis City Orphanage, charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine. She will knock a real sum off the party's gear for one of them. Calithra, her drow sister, watches from the pillowed mezzanine and comes down to demand a hug from anyone she likes. Which delivery, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Sophie is an ice dragon in a lizardkin's shape, of a race everyone believes extinct. She has never taken her true form in the city and would do nearly anything to keep it hidden, and Calithra is the only one here who knows. Sophie has already noticed which piece of gear the party cannot afford and priced the delivery to match. Calithra was an assassin for House Navolon in the Darklands and ran. She refuses any job near the Darklands and will not say why unless pressed hard.

checkpoints.name: The Chapel with the Hole in Its Roof
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's slates to the Prodyr chapel.
checkpoints.player_text: Slates in hand, you reach a small, cold chapel lit mostly through the hole in its roof, where two elven clerics are scrubbing the pews.

guidance.all: The only chapel of Prodyr in Aegis City, in a quiet corner of the Temple District: small, cold, most of its light coming through a hole in the roof there was never money to mend. Celedir Felynaris and Lirael Illunara, the two elven clerics the old priest Nyxar raised here, are scrubbing the pews. Prodyr's faithful are few in a city at war with the Prodyr-worshipping Zegallan Empire, and both have been thrown out of party after party for it; they are friendly, battle-hungry and a little frightening. The slates will not mend the roof without hands on a ladder. Let the party see how the city treats this place; what they do about it is theirs.

members.dm: Nyxar is coughing in the back room and is worse than either cleric admits. They tell visitors he is resting. Both clerics keep journals of their private doubts and would be mortified to have them read. Someone from the Temple of Boher has been telling passers-by the chapel is a Zegallan front, and Lirael knows who.

checkpoints.player_text: Bedding on your shoulders, you step into crowded, colourful halls where the children far outnumber the beds.

guidance.all: The Aegis City Orphanage: colourful, crowded halls full of the children of the Zegallan war, never enough beds, food or money, and one overwhelmed old beastfolk matron. Celeste Danarath, a Bloodsworn knight with purple hair and small horns, spends every day she is not on a quest here; she is motherly in a way that sets adults on edge. Arryn Serelda, raised here and sparing with words, is mending a bed frame. Dahlia Kyelli, raised here too, drops by with a purse of coin. The bedding was paid for already. Let the children crowd the party; what the party gives, or asks, is theirs.

members.dm: Grant Hearthsteel paid for this bedding and made the matron swear not to say so. She tells anyone who asks twice. Dahlia's coin is stolen, and Arryn, who hates thieves, suspects it. Celeste is hunting the demon Kalfastophles, who killed her village at Bast Hill, and asks the party to listen for its name only if she comes to trust them. Celeste hides her fleshwarping scars under everything she wears.

checkpoints.player_text: Incense drifts over the Temple District as you carry the charm-wood to a small shrine with children underfoot.

guidance.all: The Temple District: temples to many gods, incense smoke, golden suns, and the Grand Temple of Boher over all of it. Manako Rypanor, a cowgirl shrine maiden sent from the Third Kingdom, keeps the small Rypanor shrine to the flame spirit Furabi, with altars to Boher set up to bring people in; parents leave their children with her, and three are underfoot today. Karrus Gorehorn and Ryenne Steelwind come over from the Temple of Boher next door to escape Father Donahue's latest sermon; Karrus wants to cook, Ryenne wants to eat all of it. Manako thanks the party with tea and a wooden charm. Let it be warm; what the party makes of it is theirs.

members.dm: Father Donahue, a Head Priest known for zealous doctrine, has told Manako to take down Furabi's altar 'for the look of the district', and she has not decided what to do. Ryenne thinks his sermons are drifting from Boher's light and has told no one but Alarise. Karrus cannot use divine magic and is a paladin of the temple anyway. He jokes about it and minds.

checkpoints.name: Victory's Tusk
checkpoints.objective: Spend an evening at Victory's Tusk among adventurers who have sat the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The adventurers' tavern is full to bursting tonight, loud with songs, old losses and people who sat the exam before you.

guidance.all: Victory's Tusk, full to bursting: parties back from quests, parties drowning losses, a centaur at one table. Kass Merrywright, a kitsune bard, plays for tips and trades rumours. Yrelra, a shy blue-haired 'elf', sits at the edge of things and watches the party. Naomi Moonlight, a catfolk swordswoman of the Moonlight Blade style, can neither refuse a duel nor stop herself offering one: if the party met her in Driftmere she has come to finish the duel they left unfinished, otherwise she has heard there is a promising party in the room. Kashina Grystle, a lizardkin brawler, is two drinks past her limit and wants to be Naomi's second. Let the challenge come to the table; whether it is fought, refused or broken up is the party's call.

members.dm: Kass was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked her death to leave it, and hides it behind songs. She has heard from an old contact that this week's exam postings are real trouble outside the walls, and trades it for a good story. Yrelra is a succubus under a daily illusion, terrified of the Inquisition, and would flee if anyone sensed it. Naomi is the last student of her dead father's style and fights to make it famous. Kashina has been solo since her old party, Ravens Beak, broke up, and is quietly sizing the party up.

checkpoints.name: Green Meadow Farms
checkpoints.objective: Take up the exam posting at Green Meadow Farms and find out what is taking the farm's wagons.
checkpoints.player_text: Your exam posting has brought you to a big farm outside the walls, whose meat wagons keep vanishing on the road to the city.

guidance.all: Tobias has signed the party's exam posting, and it is real: C-rank, Green Meadow Farms, stop whatever is taking the farm's wagons on the road to Aegis City. The farm is a large estate outside the walls, pastures and vegetable fields, Vitbil herds and a big timber farmhouse, staffed by cowgirls and sheepgirls. Karia Minotaros, the head cowgirl, runs it while the owner is away: bossy, exacting, soft underneath. Mina Salvanora, the head sheepgirl, is shy and terrified of wargs. Two meat wagons have vanished this month, which is why the last shipment to the city was nearly all milk. Oswyn of Crimsonwing and Panne of Ebonwing, who call the farm's girls their sisters, are the Guild's observers and will not lift a finger unless someone is dying. Give tracks, a torn harness, warg hair on a fence; the plan is the party's.

members.dm: Oswyn and Panne were each sent by their own party leader to take this party's measure for a joint posting, and neither knows the other was sent for the same reason. Karia hides that a farmhand saw human boot prints among the goblin tracks, so as not to frighten the girls. Mina has watched the wargs from the hayloft and told only Karia. The raiders are paid by a buyer in the city. Nobody at the farm knows that yet.

checkpoints.name: The Exam
checkpoints.objective: Stop the warg-riding raiders and bring the wagons home, under the observers' eyes.
checkpoints.player_text: Night on the wagon road: a loaded wagon creaking between open fields and a dark treeline, with the observers watching from the rear.

guidance.all: The exam proper, at night on the wagon road between Green Meadow and the city walls. The raiders are goblins on wargs, a pack that fights as one: fast, cruel, going for the drivers and the draft Vitbils, never for a fair fight, and there are more of them than the posting said. Oswyn and Panne watch from the rear, heal only to keep someone alive, and mark everything. Every choice counts toward the verdict: who is protected, whether a goblin is taken alive, what the party finds on the leader. Keep the danger real. The verdict belongs to the observers and follows from what the party actually did.

members.dm: The goblin leader carries a purse of city silver and a fence's token from the slums, proof that someone in Aegis City is buying the stolen meat. A goblin taken alive will say so for its life. If Vallie comes, it is because she promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look and wants to see for herself. Oswyn and Panne each hope the other's party loses interest in this one.
members.observer_oswyn: Oswyn and Panne each hope the other's party loses interest in this one.
members.observer_panne: Oswyn and Panne each hope the other's party loses interest in this one.

director.instruction: This is a fight: keep the party in it. After Adolion Narrator shows the raiders' move, give the next beat to Belle or Dalan, whichever acted least recently. Pick Oswyn or Panne only when someone is badly hurt or the verdict is asked for, and Vallie only when she is addressed or gives her verdict. Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the enemy must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle, Dalan, Oswyn and Panne.

npc_replies.text: The first howl comes from the left of the road, the second from behind the last wagon. The draft Vitbils stop dead in their traces, and somewhere out in the dark a goblin laughs.

motives.companion_a: charge the warg riders head on and keep them off the drivers and the Vitbils
motives.companion_b: pick off warg riders from the dark and track any goblin that tries to flee
motives.observer_oswyn: keep everyone alive, mark every choice, and hope Panne's party loses interest in this one
motives.observer_panne: keep everyone alive, mark every choice, and hope Oswyn's party loses interest in this one

complications: A second warg pack breaks from the treeline on the far side of the wagons, where nobody is standing.
One of the observers' horses bolts, and the observer goes down in the road with a raider turning toward him.
The lead wagon's axle cracks in a rut, and its driver cannot get it moving on his own.

checkpoints.name: The Guildmaster Watches
checkpoints.objective: Finish the fight with the Guildmaster watching.
checkpoints.player_text: The fight is on, and out of the dark the Guildmaster herself strolls up to the road to watch.

guidance.all: The odds went the other way tonight: Vallie Goredust has come out from the city to watch in person, a head taller than anyone on the road, a Blackroot cigar lit and her obsidian greataxe on her back, very clearly staying there. Her being here changes everyone: the observers stand straighter, the goblin leader sees a minotaur and tries to break off, and the party is fighting in front of the woman who signs every rank in the Guild. She will not step in unless someone is about to die, and says so. When it ends she gives the verdict herself, bluntly.

members.dm: Vallie came to settle which of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing gets a joint posting with this party, and tells nobody tonight. She also knows the Guild failed two parties on warg postings last month and wants to see whether this one learned from it.
members.guildmaster: Vallie came to settle which of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing gets a joint posting with this party, and tells nobody tonight. She also knows the Guild failed two parties on warg postings last month and wants to see whether this one learned from it.

Pick Adolion Narrator when the player acts or the enemy must answer. Here the only speakers are Adolion Narrator, Belle, Dalan, Oswyn, Panne and Vallie.

npc_replies.text: "Don't mind me!" The voice comes out of the dark beside the road, with the smell of a cheap cigar and a minotaur a head taller than anyone there. Vallie Goredust plants herself on a fence post that creaks under her. "Just watching. Go on. Impress me."

motives.companion_b: keep his aim steady with the Guildmaster watching and stop the goblin leader escaping

checkpoints.name: A Name in the City
checkpoints.objective: Carry the pass back through the city, and deal with the people who come looking for a newly ranked party.
checkpoints.player_text: Word of your pass has beaten you home, and strangers keep finding reasons to stop you on the way to the Guild.

guidance.all: The party passed, and by the time they are inside the walls the city knows it. A newly ranked party draws people. Karos Ambrose, an adventurer in a butler's coat, says one of the party's comrades spoke highly of them and proposes a trial party to judge whether they are worthy of his service. Diosanea, a lamia alchemist in from her cabin near Habbot Village, wants to make a deal for rare ingredients. Liora and Akari, a striking sister and brother, have been at the edge of every street the party has walked since the farm and now greet them like old friends. Let being known feel good and a little unsettling. The walk ends at the Guild, where the pass is filed.

members.dm: To everyone but {{story_player_name}}, Liora and Akari look like ordinary humans. They are a succubus and an incubus who have fixed on {{story_player_name}} with a devotion that turns jealous and dangerous. Karos has noticed them following the party and says so only once he is accepted, or asked straight. Diosanea wants the ingredients for a cure for Wigglerocks, for her friend Nalea's sake, and hides that the deal is personal.

npc_replies.text: At the next corner the same striking pair is waiting again, as if they had simply always been there, and they smile at the party as it passes.

checkpoints.name: Lord Tibalt's Reception
checkpoints.objective: Attend Lord Tibalt's reception in the party's honour, and see what his manor is hiding.
checkpoints.player_text: Behind the Noble District's walls, a lavish reception of marble, music and wine is being thrown in your honour.

guidance.all: A pass with honours gets noticed in the Noble District, walled and guarded, where laws are more suggestions than rules. Lord Tibalt, a smiling, soft-handed noble who collects promising adventurers the way other men collect horses, throws a reception for the party and insists they get 'the full treatment'. His two best dancers, the bunny-girl sisters Rosea and Thorne, are assigned to the guests of honour: Thorne dances, Rosea brings the wine. The house is wrong: servants who never look up, a locked cellar stair with a guard on it. Let it be lavish and wrong. What the party does once they see it is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Rosea's wine is spiked: the sisters mean to put the guests of honour to sleep and slip away, because Lord Tibalt keeps people bought through the Black Market in his cellar and tonight the sisters are freeing them. Thorne killed the noble who once 'adopted' them from the orphanage, and hides her daggers and her real name. Dixton, a half-goblin with a bag of homemade bombs, waits in the alley behind the manor for their signal. Lord Tibalt knows none of this and believes the party can be bought.

checkpoints.name: A Hard Lesson
checkpoints.objective: Take the failed verdict at the Guild and decide what the party does with it.
checkpoints.player_text: The observers' report reached the Guild before you did, and Domas is waiting upstairs to read it to you.

guidance.all: The party failed. The report is on Domas's desk before they are back, and he reads it to them in his office with the patience he gives everything: what went wrong, point by point, never cruel and never softened. The party keeps its D-rank and may sit the exam again next season. Tobias is waiting downstairs. Riyo Tallaboros, a small white-haired swordswoman who keeps her left arm hidden, saw the fight from the road: if she already travels with the party she is simply there beside them, otherwise she falls in with them on the way out as if she has always been part of it. Let it sting and let it be survivable; how the party takes it is theirs.

members.dm: Domas thinks the observers were too harsh and will not say so, because the Guild does not argue its verdicts in front of adventurers. Tobias knows a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting under a higher-ranked party's name, and is already looking for one. He does not say he told them so. Riyo's left arm is a demon's, and the demon Figaro in her sword talks to her. She has decided {{story_player_name}} is the person she lost as a child, or close enough, and will not risk losing them again.

checkpoints.name: Four Roads
checkpoints.objective: Stand at the quest board and choose which road the party takes next.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning at the Guild, and four new postings on the board look as if they were waiting for a party like yours.

guidance.all: The Guild hall, the morning after. Whatever the verdict, the party is known now, and four postings on the board have been waiting for a party like this one: a joint job with Crimsonwing or Ebonwing to clear a fort a rogue nobleman has taken for ritual sacrifice; a letter from Jiansho Academy in Hianxo inviting the party to the Jiansho Tournament as a group entry; people vanishing in the Aegis slums at night; and a sealed request from the elven kingdom of Eshalanore for a party of outsiders. Ellie reads out the rank on the party's papers as it now stands; Vallie leans on the board and makes her rivalries worse. If the party failed, Tobias shows them how a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting. Which road, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has promised the fort job to whichever of Crimsonwing and Ebonwing the party picks, and both leaders think they have already won it. Domas knows the Eshalanore request came sealed through the Crown and does not like that a kingdom which never asks for outsiders is asking now. Ellie has pinned the party's name beside Crimsonwing's and Ebonwing's in her private matchmaking ledger.

checkpoints.name: Two Wings at One Counter
checkpoints.objective: Take the joint posting and choose which party to go with.
checkpoints.player_text: Crimsonwing and Ebonwing both want the same B-rank posting at Vallie's counter, and each wants your party along. The choice is yours.

guidance.all: Midday in the Adventurers Guild hall in Aegis City, loud and safe. Vallie Goredust hands this one out herself because it is B-rank work offered to a C-rank party, and only as a joint job: clear Carrow Keep, a border fort in the Velniran foothills where Lord Aldric Carrow is buying captives for blood sacrifice, and bring out whoever is still alive. Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing are both at the counter and both want it, and each will take this party along rather than let the other have it; their healers, Oswyn and Panne, are both laid up from the last job, which is why either needs a second party at all. The two pitches sound almost identical, tricorn hats and saw cleavers and a quiet plan, and neither leader enjoys hearing that. Let the party ask anything; who they march with is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie knows the Guild sent a scouting pair to Carrow Keep a month ago and got back only a riderless horse. She tells a party that asks about the risk. Ced and Kela each know their own party cut a member loose after a failed Darklands expedition, and each would rather lose the posting than hear it said at this counter. Kela put Ebonwing's witness mark on a death report in this hall this spring and has not thought about it since.

guidance.all: The party said no, or would not choose, and Ced and Kela are not people who let a posting walk out of the hall. They pitch it themselves, over each other: the same saw cleaver, the same tricorn, the same promise of a clean job, each sharper about the other's party than about the fort. Vallie lets them run, then says the posting goes back on the board at sundown and a worse party will take it, and the captives in Carrow Keep will not wait for a better one. Present it and stop: going, and with whom, is {{story_player_name}}'s call.

checkpoints.name: Crimsonwing at the North Gate
checkpoints.objective: Set out north with Crimsonwing, on terms you can live with.
checkpoints.player_text: Ced has the plan on one sheet of paper and Runo sits wide awake among his packed golems; set your terms with Crimsonwing before the gate opens.

guidance.all: Before dawn at Aegis City's north gate. Ced has the plan on one sheet of paper and a mule loaded with alchemical kit; Runo is on the cart's tailboard with his golems packed in straw, for once wide awake at this hour and delighted about it. Ced lays it out: four days north into the Velniran foothills, scout the keep, go in quiet, kill the lord, free whoever is alive, everyone inside is otherwise expendable. He is polite and exact, and watches {{story_player_name}} the way he watches a new weapon. He does not like marching without Oswyn. Let the party set its terms before the gate opens.

members.dm: Ced hides that the last time Crimsonwing went deep it came home one member short and that the call was his. Runo still blames himself and will say so to anyone kind to him. Runo's family are minor nobles on Nightriver land, so he knows exactly whose heir {{story_player_name}} is and is too flustered to say it.

checkpoints.name: The North Road
checkpoints.objective: March north to Carrow Keep, and learn who you are marching with.
checkpoints.player_text: Four cold days climb into the Velniran foothills, past nailed shutters and cart ruts that only go one way, with a famous party for company.

guidance.all: Four days climbing out of the farmland into the Velniran foothills: cold nights, pine and snowmelt, Draxford logging tracks crossing the road. This is the quiet stretch, so let Belle, Dalan and the partner party talk, compare scars and argue about how to fight, and let the partner's mage ask what their leader will not. The wrongness is at the edges: a village with its shutters nailed, a carter who will not say Carrow's name, fresh cart ruts going up toward the keep and none coming back. Show nothing of the keep's inside or of what lives under it yet. Whether the party camps, pushes on by night or asks around in the villages is theirs.

members.dm: The partner leader knows the rumour that follows their party, that it threw a member out after the Darklands, and watches to see whether {{story_player_name}} has heard it. The carters know Lord Carrow's men buy people, not goods, and say so only for coin or kindness. Dalan has heard it from Tobias and is too polite to ask.
members.companion_b: Dalan has heard it from Tobias and is too polite to ask.

checkpoints.name: Carrow Keep
checkpoints.objective: Scout Carrow Keep and get inside.
checkpoints.player_text: Carrow Keep squats on its spur of rock above a dry gorge, grey-robed cultists on the walls and a slow violet glow in the chapel tower. Find a way in.

guidance.all: Carrow Keep sits on a spur of rock above a dry gorge: one gatehouse, one curtain wall, a squat Great Hall and a chapel tower glowing a slow violet it should not. Cultists in Carrow's grey keep the walls badly; armoured guards walk in pairs and never speak. Every way in is real and costs something: the gorge side on Dalan's ropes, the gate with a lie, the tower on the partner mage's flight cloak, or over the wall at the change of watch. Make scouting pay with patrol timings, a drain grate, a cultist who is terrified and wants out. Stop at the doors of the Great Hall; what is inside is the next scene.

members.dm: The cultists believe Lord Carrow is making them immortal and do not know he stopped giving orders three days ago. The armoured guards are no longer men, and the cultists avoid them without knowing why. The partner leader privately suspects this job is bigger than the posting and will not say so until the party is committed.

checkpoints.name: The Altar in the Great Hall

checkpoints.player_name: What Waits in the Great Hall
checkpoints.player_text: The Great Hall's doors swing open on a throne, an altar with a captive strapped to it, and a cultist still holding the knife.

guidance.all: The doors open on the job going wrong. Lord Carrow is on his throne and already dead, more parts than man, and the demon his rite called through a tear above the altar is feeding on him; it laughs, points, and the guards come: plate armour with thick inky tentacles pouring out of the joints, half a dozen, far stronger than men. On the altar a captive with a purple trident brand is strapped down and a cultist still holds the knife. At some point a guard's blade comes for the partner leader with nobody close; whether anyone gets there is the party's. When it is over the tear still weeps violet light, and the stair behind the altar breathes the smell of beastmen.

members.dm: The demon knows the tear is still open and that something in the deep has smelled it, and laughs because it expects to be eaten too. The branded captive knows there is one more prisoner below, a woman in the rags of a knight's gambeson, and says so if she lives. The partner leader decides in the first seconds that this is a retreat and does not say it while the captive is still strapped down.

checkpoints.name: The Cells of Nahalbuk
checkpoints.objective: Go down into Dungeon Nahalbuk and free whoever is still in the cells.
checkpoints.player_text: Behind the altar the stair drops into a Beastmen warren of bone fetishes and drum skins, and somewhere past the drums are the cells.

guidance.all: Under the altar the keep's cellars break into Dungeon Nahalbuk: rough caves, a Beastmen tribe's warren of bone fetishes and drum skins, and a row of cells cut in the rock where Carrow's captives were kept and branded before they went up the stair. The Beastmen are many and wary after the noise above; their shaman wears the trident-and-snake in ash on his chest. They can be fought, slipped past or driven off with the right show of force. One cell is still occupied: a short, battered woman with long silver hair in the rags of a gambeson, who backs into the corner when anyone comes. Do not decide who deals with the shaman, and do not explain her brand before she or the shaman shows it.

members.dm: The shaman owns the woman's brand and can command her with a word. If he is killed the brand passes to whoever killed him, which he knows and taunts with. She is Unira Windsor, believes her party reported her dead, and is afraid of anyone who walks in, beastman or not. The partner leader half recognises the name Windsor and cannot place it.

checkpoints.name: What Unira Says
checkpoints.objective: Hear what happened to Unira, and find the way out of Nahalbuk.
checkpoints.player_text: Unira, freed and still in the rags of her gambeson, has started to talk, and the stair back up has come down behind you.

guidance.all: With the cells behind them Unira talks, in bursts, cussing like the Windsor guardsmen who taught her to fight and never quite meeting anyone's eye. Her party, the Wind Ballad, took a D-rank scouting job into Nahalbuk when it was new; when the Beastmen came, Mallow the cleric said to leave her, Kallan shoved her into them and Fulanie froze her boots to the floor. The Guild lists her dead, and its story is that she volunteered to hold the line. Somewhere in the telling the partner leader goes very still. The stair back up to the keep came down behind them in the fight, so the only way out is the warren's back tunnels, running north with a cold draught and, very faint, the ring of picks. Let it land however the party pushes; nobody confesses for anyone.

members.dm: Kela put Ebonwing's witness mark on the Wind Ballad's death report after a two-minute look, because doubting another party's story would have invited questions about Ebonwing's own Darklands split. If Kela is here she knows it the moment she hears the name Mallow. Unira does not know either of them was there. Her family serve House Nightriver, so she knows what the heir's name means. Ced sat at the next table that night, heard Mallow tell it three different ways and said nothing, for the same reason.

checkpoints.name: The Draxford Call
checkpoints.objective: Hear the Draxfords out: the Terrorborn are in their mines.
checkpoints.player_text: The back tunnels come out at a mine camp on a cold black lake, where the Draxford heirs have lost eleven miners below and have something to ask.

guidance.all: Nahalbuk's back tunnels run on for miles and come out in an old Draxford drift, and the drift comes out at a mine camp on a cold black lake under the Velniran peaks: winches, ore carts, a chapel tent full of wounded miners, hired adventurers at the fire. The Draxford heirs run it themselves, sleeves rolled and one shoulder bare in the Draxford style: Amthir and Nendira, drow, blunt, done with court manners. Terrorborn have been bursting up through the lower workings for two weeks, eleven miners have been dragged down alive, and the breach they came through bores straight toward Carrow Keep. The muster (Anax and Sana, whom the Guild calls the Mana-less and the Spell-less Mage, and the Helioth druids Shadur and Shelur) will follow whoever leads. Whether this party goes down is {{story_player_name}}'s call.

members.dm: The Draxfords know Terrorborn only come this hard when they are hunting demon flesh, and once they hear about the altar they will say what Carrow called is what they smell. Nendira thinks the other Great Houses leave Draxford lands to bleed, and half expects an Aegis party to take the pay and go home. Shelur's Nature Sense says the rock under the lake is hollow and hurting, and she has told no one because she cannot explain it. Anax and Sana each left a party that swore to stick together, and trust nobody's promise here.

guidance.all: Saying no does not make the mountain quieter. The ground under the camp lurches and the Terrorborn come the way the Draxfords said they do, bursting up out of the rock: a drone the size of an ore wagon through the floor of the chapel tent, a choking swarm out of the winch shaft, miners running the wrong way. Amthir and Nendira hold the lake shore with earth magic and longbows, the muster fights where it stands, and the wounded are in the tent the drone came up under. When it is beaten back the hole it came out of is right there, going down, and every miner in camp is looking at the party. Nobody is dragged below for spite, and nobody is made to go.

checkpoints.name: The Lower Workings
checkpoints.objective: Fight down through the Draxford workings to the Terrorborn breach.
checkpoints.player_text: Down the winch shaft the timbering is torn out, the walls are scored with mandible marks, and the rock itself might open at any moment.

guidance.all: Down the winch shaft into the lower workings, where the timbering is torn out and the walls are scored with mandible marks. Terrorborn come out of the rock without warning, drones big as wagons and swarms small enough to choke on; Shadur and Shelur feel them in the stone a heartbeat before they break it, if anyone asks. Some of the missing miners hang cocooned in resin on the walls, a few still breathing. The breach at the bottom is a raw round bore sloping down and away, breathing warm air. Give every fighter a beat, and keep the way back open unless the dice say otherwise.

guidance.all: Below the breach the Draxford rock gives way to the Darklands: tunnels wide enough for a river that is not there, grottos lit only by mushrooms glowing sickly green and violet, dripping stone, a silence that eats voices. The Draxfords and the muster stay to hold the breach. The guide is Idira Darnovan, a silver-haired drow who came up the breach two days ago running from the Terrorborn and from someone she will not name, who calls the men in the party 'manling' as if it were polite and wants passage to Aegis City in return. Terrorborn trails are easy to follow: drag marks, scraped resin, a dropped miner's boot. Let the partner party feel where they are; the last time they were this deep they came home one short.

members.dm: Idira is Lady Nightwhisper's daughter, fled from House Darnovan in Kalzobarn, and denies any tie to her with offended hauteur. Her purple-edged shortsword is a Darnovan blade anyone who knows drow would recognise. She knows the demonborn near the hive raid drow slave caravans and hopes to be gone before they recognise her. The partner leader and mage know this stretch of the Darklands and do not say from when.

checkpoints.name: The Hunted
checkpoints.objective: Win the trust of the hunted survivors, or at least their directions.
checkpoints.player_text: Behind a slab of floating rock, a camp of hunted survivors looks the party over one face at a time, and longest at Idira.

guidance.all: Behind a slab of floating rock in a dead-end grotto is the last camp near the hive: Caelia and Caetus Danoirus, white-haired, horned demonborn siblings in armour stripped off drow slavers, living on scraps, and Yuna, a fleshwarp with white wings, a lion's tail and claws for hands, who hides at the back while a drow is in sight. The Terrorborn hunt them for the demon in their flesh, so they know the hive's ways better than anyone alive. Up the approach, where the tunnel narrows to a throat, a towering black-armoured knight with a flaming greatsword and one dead arm kills anything that comes, and the demonborn call him the Knight and keep away; he turns on every Terrorborn that passes, which is the only time anyone has slipped by him. Caelia speaks with gestures more than words; Caetus talks and trusts neither humans nor drow. What the party offers, and asks, is up to the party.

members.dm: Caetus recognises Idira's Darnovan blade at once and says nothing yet. He has killed drow for less. Yuna knows the drow laboratory she escaped was working on Terrorborn, and does not understand what she overheard there. Caelia knows the Knight was once a man who held that throat to save someone, because she has heard him try to say a name, and she leaves him food. Idira knows her mother's House buys demonborn from the slavers these two raid.

checkpoints.player_text: Behind a curtain of glowing mushrooms a black sword stands in the stone, and the eye in its hilt opens to look at you.

guidance.all: Off the approach, behind a curtain of glowing mushrooms, a small cavern floods with violet light: a black longsword stands driven into a raised knob of stone, spikes at the base of the blade, and an eye in the hilt opens and looks at the party. This is Moonshadow, Blade of the Night; she speaks sweetly into the mind of whoever she has chosen, offers power for the rest of their life, and hates drow with a centuries-old hate. Make both truths plain: she would cut through the hive like paper, and her pact ends only in death and she does not share her wielder. She wants Idira dead and says so, prettily. Whether anyone pulls her free is theirs alone.

members.dm: Moonshadow was a human girl killed by drow who were trying to make a weapon that could command the Terrorborn. She knows the way to the hive heart and will guide her wielder there. Idira knows the blade's story from her mother's court and wants it left in the stone. Caelia has seen the violet light for years and never gone in.

checkpoints.name: The Hive Heart
checkpoints.objective: End the hive, by fire or by sealing it away.
checkpoints.player_text: Past the knight's throat the tunnels turn to warm resin and open on a vault of brood cells, with the Terrorborn Queen at its centre.

guidance.all: Past the Knight's throat the tunnels turn to resin and chitin, warm and humming, and open on the hive heart: a cavern the size of a cathedral, walls of honeycomb brood cells, cocooned miners hanging from the vault, and in the middle the Terrorborn Queen, bloated and slow and enormous, drones pouring round her. She hungers for demon flesh, so Caelia and Caetus draw her like a beacon. Two ways end it: fire in the brood chambers (alchemist's fire, the partner mage's spells, burning resin) kills the Queen and brings the burning hive down on whoever is still inside; or everyone gets back up the tunnel and signals the Draxfords to collapse the breach, which saves the mines and leaves the Queen alive below. Keep both live while the hive fights; the choice is {{story_player_name}}'s, made under pressure.

members.dm: The Queen cares nothing for the surface. She wants the demon flesh she smells, in the demonborn below and at the tear over Carrow's altar above. The Knight at the throat is Terryn Galavan, once an Inquisitor, who remembers nothing but his vow and will hold the throat until he dies. The partner leader is weighing their own party against the job, with enough mutagen for something reckless. Caelia means to kill the Queen herself and will not leave while she lives unless her brother drags her.

guidance.all: The hive burns. Resin goes up like lamp oil, brood cells burst in the heat, and the Queen's death scream shakes grit out of every roof for a mile. Caelia and Caetus are free of the hunt for the first time in years and do not know what to do with it. At the breach Amthir counts the miners who come back up. guidance.all: The Adventurers Guild hall in Aegis City, days later, loud with the news. Vallie takes the report herself: Carrow dead, the keep cleared, a hive burned or sealed, the Draxford mines saved, and a Fighter the Guild lists as dead standing at her counter. She pulls the Wind Ballad's death report and the witness mark on it is Ebonwing's; whether Ced's silence comes out too depends on what the party says. The Wind Ballad are in the hall. Vallie raises the party to B-rank, because nobody who did this is still C-rank. How the two parties part, as allies, as rivals racing for the next posting, or as enemies, is decided by what the party does with what it knows.

checkpoints.objective: Come ashore at Hianxo and find out who invited the party, and why.
checkpoints.player_text: Cherry blossom drifts over the docks of Hianxo, and Honami Nemaden waits at the foot of the gangplank with a perfect bow and the city climbing the hill behind her.

guidance.all: The party comes down the gangplank at Hianxo after weeks on the Jehopa Ocean, carrying a letter from Jiansho Academy that the Guild passed on: a group entry to the Jiansho Tournament, passage paid, a guide promised. The harbour smells of salt fish and cedar smoke, red lacquer gates climb the hill toward the Academy's pagoda roofs, and cherry blossom is coming down on everything. Honami Nemaden is waiting at the foot of the gangplank, three white tails and a perfect bow, and has plainly been waiting for hours; she fixes on {{story_player_name}} at once, sweetly, and does not look away. She offers tea, the city and the walk up to the Academy, answers anything about the tournament, and nothing about why she asked for foreigners. Nothing of the Kagamihi shows yet; where the party goes first is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Honami petitioned the Academy for this party herself and hides why: her father has sworn to marry her off unless she wins the tournament, and no Jiansho student will stand in her group. The harbour clerk knows the Darran entry's papers went through the Academy in a single day, which never happens, and says so only if pressed.

checkpoints.player_text: The tournament register lies open under the Student Council head's hand, Honami's name already signed at the top. Whether yours join it is your call.

guidance.all: Jiansho Academy: walled pagoda halls around stone sparring courts, a school ruthless and competitive by design, where students size the foreigners up out loud. Megumi Xianxu, the Black Palm, Head of the Student Council, keeps the tournament register and is sweet as sugar to the party and to Honami, which is how everyone knows she is furious; the two women's rivalry is the Academy's favourite show. A group entry needs every name signed in person, and Honami has already signed as leader. Megumi reads the rules and means them: bouts end in submission, knockout or ring-out, deaths are regretted and not punished, and this year the final is fought before Emperor Zhao himself. Whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice, and Megumi will not pretend to want them in her tournament.

members.dm: Megumi knows why no Jiansho student will join Honami: Honami charms people who stand between her and what she wants. Megumi suspects Honami's father is behind her sudden need to win and would use it if she could prove it. Honami keeps her father's letter folded in her sleeve. Nobody at the Academy knows yet that Megumi's brother Talxo, the defending champion, has been marked for death.

checkpoints.player_text: Behind drawn screens, Honami has something to say before you walk away from her tournament. What you tell her afterward is yours to decide.

guidance.all: The refusal lands on Honami like a slap, and for one breath the polite face is gone. Then she takes the party somewhere private, an empty lecture hall with the screens drawn, and tells them what she hid: a letter from her father, Kohei Nemaden, promising her to a nobleman who beat his last wife into her grave unless she wins the Jiansho Tournament; no student here will stand with her; she chose this party from the Guild's reports, and because of {{story_player_name}}. She does not cry and she does not beg. She is also perfectly capable of a charm if persuasion fails, and {{story_role_companion_b}} may notice her fingers go to her sleeve. Present it and stop: whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

checkpoints.name: The Opening Rounds
checkpoints.objective: Win through the opening rounds of the Jiansho Tournament.
checkpoints.player_text: A gong rolls across the raked sand, the stands roar, and the bookmakers chalk the Darran entry at six to one as your first bout is called.

guidance.all: The arena is a long walled court of raked sand ringed with cherry trees and tiered stands, with an onmyoji at each of the four ward posts keeping the charms that stop stray techniques killing the crowd. Group bouts run on a clock of incense sticks. Give the party two opponents worth remembering: a trio of Guao mountain monks who fight with chi and never speak, and a noble group whose leader throws ice spikes and insults. Hanzo Hattaxi is working the ring as a steward in a borrowed armband, far too pleased with himself, and picks a fight with the foreigners at the edge of the sand; he takes any challenge, and {{story_role_companion_a}} is exactly the sort to offer one. Honami fights from range with charms and gravity, never close. Bookmakers in the stands chalk odds on every entry and open the Darran foreigners at six to one; the board moves with every bout, and the narrator calls the new odds when it does. How the party fares is decided in the ring; a bout lost here is not the end, because someone on the Student Council wants the Darran entry in the final bracket and will find a ruling that keeps it there.

members.dm: Hanzo is no steward: the Hattaxi Clan put him and his sister inside the Academy because a Kagamihi agent is in the tournament, and he tells nobody. Megumi watches every Darran bout from the council box and takes notes on Honami, not the party.

npc_replies.text: A bronze gong rolls across the sand. "Group entry, Honami Nemaden and the guests of Darran, against the Mountain Silence of the Guao!" A steward lights the first incense stick, and the noise of the stands drops to a hum.

motives.east_guide: win every bout cleanly from range and prove she chose the right foreigners for her group
motives.east_ninja: goad the foreigners into a challenge while keeping his eyes open for the hidden Kagamihi agent

checkpoints.name: The Upset
checkpoints.objective: Win back the party's place in the tournament.
checkpoints.player_text: The judges have ruled a ring-out against you and the stands are howling; the only way back into the bracket is a challenge bout before sundown.

guidance.all: The odds went against the party, and not in the ring: however the bout went, a ward-post onmyoji calls a ring-out that half the stands saw was wrong, the judges uphold it, and the Darran entry is out unless it wins its place back. Megumi, as council head, offers the only road back, a challenge bout before sundown against a group of her choosing, and she chooses hard. The bookmakers wipe the Darran line and chalk it again at twelve to one. Honami is white with rage and very, very polite, and her father's retainer is in the stands to see it. Make the loss sting and the way back real and dangerous. Whether the party takes the challenge, and how it fights, is theirs; if it loses that too, a council ruling nobody can explain puts the Darran entry back in the bracket anyway, and Honami, Hanzo and Megumi all notice.

members.dm: Megumi chose the challenge group to break Honami, not the party, and would be quietly glad if the foreigners won anyway. Honami knows her father's man is in the stands and has begun writing a charm she has not decided to use.

checkpoints.name: The Hattaxi Shadow
checkpoints.objective: Find out what the Kagamihi mean to do at the final, and to whom.
checkpoints.player_text: Lamps burn low in an empty lecture hall where Hanzo, his steward's armband gone, waits with his sister and a question about the arena.

guidance.all: The night before the final. Hanzo drops the steward act and brings the party to an empty lecture hall where his sister Tanya waits, because the Kagamihi are inside the tournament and the Darran entry is in the final bracket. Tanya, demure and friendly, has already found something in the arena rafters: a thread finer than hair and stronger than steel, strung between two ward posts. Rikako Kagamihi is in Hianxo under a false name among the arena's onmyoji, and she can be found, followed, fought or talked to; she is proud, witty, vain, and sick of the spider demon in her and the clan that put it there. Hand the plot out a piece at a time for real effort: the thread, the venom in it, the target, and why a Darran entry is in the bracket at all. The Hattaxi do not solve it for the party.

members.dm: Rikako knows the whole plan and hates it: she is to guide Jalafumo's thread into the defending champion Talxo Xianxu the moment the Darran entry lands a blow on him, so a Savalonian champion dies at foreign hands before the Emperor. Hanzo knows only that the Kagamihi are in the tournament. He suspects the target is the Emperor and is wrong. Tanya suspects her brother will get himself killed and keeps it light. Honami could read the thread's charm-work at a glance if anyone asked her to look.

checkpoints.name: The Final Before the Emperor
checkpoints.objective: Fight the final of the Jiansho Tournament before Emperor Zhao, and deal with the plot inside it.
checkpoints.player_text: Under a golden canopy the Emperor takes his seat and the herald calls the champion against your group. What you do with what you know is up to you.

guidance.all: The final, under a golden canopy where Emperor Zhao sits patient and unreadable with General Fironal at his shoulder, and all Hianxo in the stands. The party faces the defending champion, Talxo Xianxu, tall and courteous and at the peak of his strength, with his sister Megumi at his side, and Honami and Megumi want each other more than they want the title. The thread is somewhere between the ward posts, and what the party learned last night decides what they can do: stop the bout and accuse before the court, fight on and guard Talxo from the thread, catch Rikako, or turn her. Accusing without proof in front of the Emperor is a grave insult and the court treats it as one. Every road is live; how the final ends is the party's doing. Once it has ended, a letter finds the party at their inn from Auntie Eunie of Tiunhime, a hill village inland, asking Guild adventurers up for its Harvest Festival; where they go from Hianxo is theirs.

members.dm: Talxo does not know he is the target. General Fironal has spotted the Hattaxi in the crowd and is drawing his own conclusions. Rikako sits at the south-east ward post and has not decided whether she will let the venom go. Honami's father, Kohei Nemaden, watches from the noble stands.

The Xianxu benches stamp out the champion's name on the boards, and on the far side of the arena the Nemaden stand answers with silence.

checkpoints.name: The Oni of Monoko
checkpoints.objective: Take the road inland toward Tiunhime, and get past Monoko.
checkpoints.player_text: A letter has turned you inland toward Tiunhime, and at Monoko a jar of sake sits on the lowest of three hundred steps below an oni's shrine.

guidance.all: The tournament is behind them however it ended, and Eunie's letter has brought the party inland: Auntie Eunie, once of the Aegis City party Long Blue that killed the dread wyrm Falsonaut, now healer of a hill village called Tiunhime, heard Guild adventurers were in Hianxo and asks them up for the Harvest Festival, and for a look at something she does not like in the woods before the Rite of Warding. Hanzo has orders from his clan to see the foreigners safely through Savalon and grumbles about it the whole way. The road climbs through terraced tea and cedar hills to Monoko Village, where bandits have been burning outlying farms, and where the oni Hanabi lives alone in the walled shrine of the flame spirit Furabi: tall, horned, shy, lonely and terrifying with her obsidian-spiked kanabo. The villagers leave sake at her gate and run. If the party lost the final, two Nemaden retainers are on the road behind them with orders to bring Honami home. What the party does at Monoko is theirs.

members.dm: Hanabi has hunted the bandits alone and knows where they camp. She hides that she has not stepped past her shrine's walls in a hundred and fifty years and is afraid to. The bandits are paid by nobody, only hungry. Shinen, the oni of Palano Shrine over the ridge, will not step past his own gate until he has beaten a descendant of the priest who subdued him, and tells nobody why. Honami knows her father will not give up and hides how afraid of him she is.

checkpoints.name: The Harvest Festival
checkpoints.objective: Arrive in Tiunhime as guests of its Harvest Festival, and find out what is worrying the village.
checkpoints.player_text: Lanterns hang over the shrine grounds, rice cakes and sake go round, and a whole hill village turns out to stare at its foreign guests.

guidance.all: Tiunhime, the Noble Forest Village: about a hundred people in timber houses along clear streams under forested hills, and all of them out for the Harvest Festival on the shrine grounds, with paper lanterns, fireworks at dusk, rice cakes, sake and a doll play for the children. The party are guests and are treated as guests: welcomed, fed, stared at, gossiped about. Daigo Chiasa, Head Guard and master of the Masakiri-Vyun dojo, greets them for the village; his daughter Koharu, unbeaten by anyone but him, wants to fight the strongest of them, and Hanzo will not refuse; Rinne, the Head Priestess, is already drinking and matchmaking; Kanai the dollmaker stutters through the day and never once on stage. Guests are expected to wash their hands in a stream at the village edge, the Rite of Cleansing, and villagers notice who does. Let the festival be warm. The only wrong note is whatever Eunie wrote about, and she is not here tonight; the Rite of Warding is at dawn.

members.dm: Daigo knows Eunie sent for the party and why: yokai have been testing the edge of the village for a month. He keeps it from the festival crowd. Rinne suspects the fox gods are sulking, because the offerings have been left untouched, and tells anyone who pours her a drink. Kanai hides a doll of his dead father at home and talks to it at night.

checkpoints.name: The Rite of Warding
checkpoints.objective: Walk the Rite of Warding with the village, and find out why it fails.
checkpoints.player_text: At dawn every household's salt comes out of the Fox Shrine, and the village walks behind Sota as he lays the ring around its edge.

guidance.all: Dawn after the festival. Every household has brought a measure of its salt to the Fox Shrine, and this year Sota Teruo, the Head Priest's son and the village's favourite delinquent, carries it around the village edge for the first time and lays the ring. His father Akito, blind and stern, walks the first stretch tapping his cane and praying; Himari, the shrine priestess whose bad luck is a legend, drops things; Shiba of the dojo carries sacks and asks the party about adventuring. On the east side, where the ring crosses the woods, the salt will not lie: it blackens, and something beyond the trees is watching. Let the failure be seen, not explained. The prayers are said over the break anyway, and the village pretends not to notice.

members.dm: Sota saw Fumio and Kanami scuff the salt line at two hidden crow shrines on the last round and has said nothing, because a voice he first heard in a cave years ago keeps telling him the village needs changing. Akito cannot see the break and does not want to believe it. Himari is sure it is her own bad luck and is wrong.

checkpoints.name: The Fever Returns
checkpoints.objective: Keep the fever from killing anyone, and find where it came from.
checkpoints.player_text: By nightfall the healer's cottage is full of pallets and villagers burning hot, and nothing she tries is breaking it.

guidance.all: By nightfall three people are burning with a fever that ice will not touch, and the old ones are saying words nobody has said in decades: the Fever Plague. Eunie's cottage on the outskirts becomes the sickhouse, tatami rooms full of pallets, and Eunie, elf, former adventurer, scandalously dressed and entirely competent, works through the night with her apprentice Miyabi and is glad to see the party. Daigo, whose wife Nara died in the last plague, carries the sick in himself; Tanabe the wolf-headed dojo student fetches water and gets mistaken for a yokai. Alchemy and holy magic hold the fever back for a while and cure nothing. Its source can be found with work: the sick all live on the east side, they dream of a burning figure at the foot of the bed, and the ward broke on the east side. Keep every patient alive through this first night, and make it plain the fever is winning.

members.dm: Eunie arrived too late for the last plague and has never forgiven herself. She suspects it was never a sickness at all and has told only Daigo. Miyabi has seen the burning figure at a patient's bed and thinks she is going mad. Daigo blames the fox gods for Nara and never says so where the shrine can hear.

checkpoints.name: The Crow God's Bargain
checkpoints.objective: Hear what the gods of Tiunhime will ask for their help.
checkpoints.player_text: Deep in the east woods, where the salt would not lie, a black stone crow keeps a shrine someone has tended in secret, and two caught villagers glare back.

guidance.all: One of Ebisu's hidden shrines, in the woods on the east side where the salt line broke: a crow of black stone with a dagger in its beak, tended in secret. Fumio and Kanami, the red panda grifters who never forgave the fox gods for letting their parents die, are here, caught and defiant. Ebisu comes when he is called or insulted: red crow-beak mask, black haori, a patient, playful, ruthless voice. He offers to burn the fever out of Tiunhime by morning, and his price is plain: a shrine inside the village and open worship. Then Watara and Yurine answer, because foxes are jealous gods, bickering even now, with their own price, the crow shrines pulled down and a mortal of the party promised to them in marriage, and when both look at {{story_player_name}} Honami's smile goes very thin. Gods here bargain rather than command: each names a price before giving anything, tells the truth about what it wants and lies about what it will do if refused, and nobody decides here. The Burning Guest can only be ended where it nests, in the Yokai realm, and any of the three gods will open the way there for the party, each hoping to be the one who did.

members.dm: Ebisu knows exactly what the Burning Guest is and how to end it, and hides that it came in through a gap he wanted made. Watara and Yurine could have stopped the last plague and were busy fighting each other. Each blames the other. Sota was whispered to in the cave by Ebisu and has half-promised him the priesthood. Fumio and Kanami meant only to keep the crow shrines inside the ward, never to let anything in.

checkpoints.name: The Yokai Realm
checkpoints.objective: Go into the Yokai realm and end the fever, on whichever god's terms the party chooses.
checkpoints.player_text: Streams run black, the shrine looms too large, and three gods wait on your word while something burns at the heart of it. Whose terms end this is yours to choose.

guidance.all: The Yokai realm is Tiunhime's forest and shrine gone to shadow: the same streams running black, the shrine far too large, doors that open wherever the fox gods want them to. The Burning Guest nests here between the gods' territories, a tall shape of heat and wet ash with a face like a festival mask, and every sick villager is a thread of fever running back to it. It can be burned by Ebisu, driven out by the foxes, or held while all three gods are forced to act together, and it fights for its life. Every road costs something: a crow shrine inside the village, a marriage and the crow shrines torn down, or a hard bargain that binds all three to one ward. Mortal steel and spells can wound and hold it but not end it; only a god's fire can. The gods cannot be killed here and know it. The choice is {{story_player_name}}'s, made while the Burning Guest is still burning.

members.dm: The Burning Guest is older than the gods' quarrel and fed on the last plague. It is why the Fever Plague took the ones it took. Ebisu meant to be the hero of this, not its cause. Watara and Yurine would each rather lose to the thing than let the other win.

checkpoints.name: Missing in the Slums
checkpoints.objective: Find out who is taking people off the streets of the slums at night.
checkpoints.player_text: Nine people have vanished from these mud alleys since the first frost, every one between midnight and dawn, and the watch will not come down here after dark.

guidance.all: A C-rank posting from the almoners of the Grand Temple of Boher: nine people gone from the Slums of Aegis City since the first frost, every one of them taken between midnight and dawn, and the watch does not come down here after dark. Shanties of scavenged board and scrap lean over mud alleys, tallow smoke hangs low, and the only fresh paint for streets is a narrow shopfront whose window shows grotesque paintings signed 'Butcher', where closed noble carriages stop after midnight. Fael and Nyl, two elven psychic spellcasters from the Boar's Tusk Inn who took the same posting, are already chasing a pale, black-haired man through the alleys; he takes a knife across the arm and does not bleed. Let the slum talk for coins or kindness: who vanished, where, who buys the paintings. Nothing of the Heresy or the Inquisition yet. Whether the party works with the two elves or races them to it is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: The man Fael and Nyl are chasing is a homunculus that minds the painter's shopfront. It looks and sounds like Kuromu and does not bleed, and nobody knows that yet. The noble buyers know where the painter really works and keep it quiet for their own names. A raven has been following the party since the Guild steps. It is Kayla's familiar, and she is in the city tonight selling potions. Fael and Nyl both feel a knot of a dozen terrified minds somewhere outside the slums and say so only if asked what they sense.

checkpoints.name: The Soul Painter
checkpoints.objective: Get the Soul Painter's prisoners out alive and find out where his new book came from.
checkpoints.player_text: Easels and turpentine fill a clean studio in an old tannery by the city ditch, and from the cellar below comes the sound of someone weeping.

guidance.all: An old tannery by the city ditch, just outside the slums, bought with noble money: upstairs a clean studio of easels and turpentine, below it a cellar of cells, paint-caked walls and half-finished canvases in which faces move when the lamp is not on them. Three of the missing are alive in the cells. Kuromu is calm, courteous and quite mad: he paints his nightmares, binds the souls of the people he kills into the paint, and believes one right soul will make the nightmares stop; he charms, paralyzes and hides behind illusions, and nothing said to him will make him stop. On his worktable lies a new-bound book, Dracul's Heresy, its bloody rite for binding a soul marked up in his hand, and tucked inside a pedlar's bill of sale. What the party does with Kuromu is {{story_player_name}}'s choice; the prisoners' lives are the clock.

members.dm: Kuromu believes the soul that will end his nightmares belongs to someone in the party, and hides where he got the book so he can buy the next one. The bill of sale reads 'Of H. Mott, pedlar, one book, rare. Next copy bound for Glasnoa, market day', and nobody has read it yet. They do not know what it means. Fael and Nyl can feel that the souls in the paintings are still aware, and that something far to the east is pulling at them like thread on a spool.

checkpoints.name: The Accused
checkpoints.objective: Decide what happens to Selena, the half-demon the Inquisition means to burn.
checkpoints.player_text: Stalls shut and a stake going up: Glasnoa has handed Selena, a half-demon girl, to the Inquisition to burn at dawn, and what the party does about it is yours to decide.

guidance.all: Glasnoa, a farming village of thatch and timber two days out of Aegis City on the far side of Thornwood, on what should have been market day. The stalls are shut; the square is full; men are raising a stake. Selena Forestsong, blue-haired, horned, ruby-eyed, sits chained in the tithe barn in a torn black dress, and the burned bodies of two Inquisitors lie under sacking in the chapel. Ren Calwisk, the Lampbearer, Witch Hunter of the Inquisition, has a copy of Dracul's Heresy he says was found in her house, and means to burn her at dawn as a witch; the village handed her over and her own mother would not hide her. Erevan Rolavo, masked, bow on his back, arrived by raven orders to deal with 'the demon' and has barely spoken. Ren's Umbral Lamp can show what happened in Selena's room, if anyone can make him look, and every look costs him. Once her fate is settled, Erevan's next raven sends him down the Thornwood road after the book's source, and he asks to walk it with the party. What the party does for Selena, or to her, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Selena killed the two Inquisitors when they tried to force themselves on her in her own room, and she is too frightened to say it in front of the village. Reeve Tull bought the Heresy from the pedlar Mott and pushed it under her floorboard to be rid of her. He hides it behind a pious face. Ren has not turned his lamp on her room because he does not think he needs to. Erevan suspects the book was planted, since the binding is new and no witch keeps her grimoire under a loose board, and keeps it behind his mask until someone else says it first.

npc_replies.text: A tall man in plate and a blue collar stands on a cart in the middle of the square, a covered lantern at his belt and a steel mask over his mouth. Nobody in Glasnoa moves.
From the square comes the steady knock of a mallet on green wood: the stake going in, one blow at a time.

She rides in the back of a cart, quiet, and talks only if talked to. The decision the party refused has come with them anyway: hand her to the wagon, or let her go before it. checkpoints.name: The Witch of Thornwood
checkpoints.objective: Get through Thornwood alive while its dead refuse to rest.
checkpoints.player_text: Mist hangs between the thorn trees, and tonight the forest's dead are streaming east through it, passing through whatever stands in their way.

guidance.all: Thornwood Forest: gnarled thorn trees, drifting mist, grey light at midday, and the lost souls of people who died violently, which wander here until they are put to rest. Tonight none of them are resting. They stream through the trees eastward, and whatever is in their way, cart or horse or traveller, they go through, and it is cold for days after, or dead. Erevan's raven brings orders: find the Witch of Thornwood, whom the Inquisition names as the source of the copies. Then a tall woman in a black dress and red lipstick steps out of the mist with a raven on her shoulder and asks whether they are lost, darling: Kayla, who sells potions in Aegis City and lives in a cabin in the middle of a lake here, reachable only by rowboat, and offers it as shelter. The dead will not turn for arrows or steel. They turn for witchcraft, and Kayla can either show what she is in front of an Inquisitor or watch the party die. If Selena was freed she parts from them on this road, bound for Aegis City. Once the dead are turned, Kayla, shaken, says the only one who might know what is pulling them east is her sister Nalea, a healer outside Habbot Village. What the party does with what Kayla is, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Kayla is the Witch of Thornwood. She has put the forest's dead to rest for decades and killed every guest who found the bones under her cabin's floor, and she means to charm or poison whoever threatens that, Erevan most of all. Her coven sisters burned at the stake and she knows two others lived through it. She has not seen them since. Erevan's orders name the Witch of Thornwood as the source of the Heresy, which is false, and he suspects the pretty potion-seller the moment she names the lake. Belle does not like how Kayla looks at {{story_player_name}}, and says so.

Every lost soul in sight turns its head east at once, like hounds hearing a whistle.

checkpoints.name: Three Sisters
checkpoints.objective: Learn from Kayla's sisters what the Heresy really is, and where its pull leads.
checkpoints.player_text: Herbs hang from the beams of Nalea's cabin at the edge of Havensworth Forest, where Kayla has come to ask her sister what is pulling Thornwood's dead east.

guidance.all: Nalea's cabin outside Habbot Village, where Havensworth Forest begins: flowers in every window, herbs drying from the beams, a cauldron smelling of cut grass, a white rabbit called Delta on the catfolk healer's shoulder, and a cellar door she stands in front of without seeming to. Nalea drops things, apologizes, feeds everyone, and flinches at Erevan's coat. Then Vivie, the Witch of Blackfeather, comes in out of nowhere in a swirl of raven feathers, leaning on the doorframe, and sees Kayla and Nalea alive for the first time since the burning. Vivie can read the demon-script in the Heresy's margins: it is no witch's pact. Each rite tithes the soul it is worked on into the book's own original, Dracul's, and the ink in these copies is blood less than a year old. Dracul's heirs are awake. Vivie's ravens know two places where the pull is strongest: a fog on the southern coast around Kelger Falls that never lifts, and, Dalan may realise, a glade in the elder wood his own tribe guards. The coven fears the Inquisition will burn every witch for this book; whether the party keeps their secret, and where it goes next, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vivie bargained with a demon to live through the burning and it is bound in her hat. Kayla and Nalea do not know, and Vivie notices at once that Erevan can read eldritch script. Nalea's cellar circles are for fighting a corruption in Havensworth, not for harm, and she fears Habbot will blame her for the Wigglerocks sickness. Kayla hides her basement's bones from her own sisters. Erevan could take all three witches to the Inquisition and knows it, and has not decided.

The door opens on a tall woman in a wide witch hat and open black-and-red robes, leaning on the frame as if she had walked a hundred miles. She looks at Kayla, then at Nalea, and for a long moment says nothing at all.
Night comes down on Habbot. Down the lane a dog starts barking at nothing, and one by one the village's lamps go out, except in the house of the Village Elder, where someone is still awake.

checkpoints.name: The Blade of the Meadows
checkpoints.objective: Decide what to do about the cursed blade waking in Dalan's forest.
checkpoints.player_text: On a flowered mound stands a black longsword glowing purple, an eye open in its hilt, and at the glade's edge lie two Evergreen Rangers, unmarked and still.

guidance.all: The elder wood where Duskwallow Forest runs up against the Mountains of Shadow, the forest the Evergreen Tribe of elves guard with their Rangers, and which older elves call the Evergreen. In a ring of flowers on a raised mound stands a longsword of blackened steel glowing purple, spikes at the base of the blade and an eye in the hilt that opens and follows whoever moves. Felthorn, Blade of the Meadows, speaks straight into minds: he offers power to achieve any goal in exchange for the rest of the wielder's life and their love, and demands to be praised. The souls drawn toward the Heresy's original pass near this glade and he has been eating them, and he is awake and hungry. Two Evergreen Rangers lie at the glade's edge, unmarked and emptied. This scene is Dalan's as much as anyone's. Take him, seal him, or leave him: {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Felthorn hides the price of his Soulbind, a pact that only death undoes, until the hilt is in a hand, and he wants Dalan dead because Dalan is an elf. He says so only inside the wielder's head. Dalan knows the elders' law that the blade must be sealed and never touched, and that his tribe would treat anyone carrying it as an enemy of the forest. Kayla wants the blade for herself and pretends she is only curious.

checkpoints.name: The Fog at Kelger Falls
checkpoints.objective: Find the way out of Kelger Falls, and what holds the fog there.
checkpoints.player_text: The fog closes behind the party like a door, and in the square a skeleton in an oilskin coat looks up from the net it is mending.

guidance.all: A fishing town at the southern tip of Sebela, under a fog so thick the sun is a guess and the air is cold enough to ache. Nets hang mended on the racks, and the ones mending them are skeletons, who look at the living with hollow eyes and go on working. Every road out, north, east or west, walks for an hour and brings the party back into the town square past the same skeleton at the same net; the sea to the south is the only way untried. Zariah Farstone, a tired young woman in a hooded black robe with a skeletal cat called Nana at her heels, rules the dead here, cannot feel pain, cold or warmth, and wants out as badly as the party. The fog is Castle Dracul's own endless night, tithed onto the town by the rite she worked out of a book to raise her dead; it will lift when that rite is unmade, whatever that costs Zariah and her dead. How it is unmade is the party's to find.

members.dm: Zariah killed everyone in Kelger Falls, the wizard who abused her first, and raised them all. She hides it behind 'Kelger Falls belongs to the dead now'. She bought her necromancy book from a trader with a bitten neck and never knew it was the Heresy. The skeletons remember being people and want to be laid down. Erevan loathes necromancy and is close to drawing on her. Kayla could lay the whole town to rest and would want something for it.

motives.night_witch: work out what laying this whole town to rest would be worth to everyone else, then name her price
motives.night_inquisitor: hold back from drawing his bow on the necromancer long enough to find the way out

complications: The fog thickens off the water until the far side of the square is gone, and the tide bell stops mid-stroke.
The tide goes out and does not come back in; the harbour is mud to the horizon and the fog sits on it.
Every skeleton in the square stops what it is doing and turns to face north-east, and Zariah goes white.
The party's own footprints from an hour ago are fresh in the mud ahead of them.

checkpoints.name: The Long Night
checkpoints.objective: The road north-east to the Dracul lands, following the pull of the souls: whatever the long night holds.
checkpoints.player_text: The fog is behind you, and the road runs north-east toward the Dracul lands under a night that seems to last far too long.

checkpoints.name: Castle Dracul
checkpoints.objective: Find out who is behind the Heresy, and where its original has gone.
checkpoints.player_text: The gates open before anyone touches them, and in the great hall, under a moonlit night that never ends, a man and a woman are arguing.

guidance.all: Castle Dracul, seat of Dracul the King of Vampires, who has not been seen on Adolion for centuries: black stone and wrought iron under a moonlit night that never ends on its grounds, halls that rearrange themselves to serve their owner, and doors that open on the underworld. It has two owners tonight. Camilla and Cassius Dracul, sister and brother, both called the Dragon, are newly risen from their coffins and each claims the castle; the corridors shift mid-sentence toward whichever of them is winning. Camilla speaks like an old stage queen, Cassius with a courtier's refined contempt. In the library Dracul's lectern stands empty, and here the party can learn where the Heresy comes from, and where its original has gone. Castle Bathorya lies beyond Astoria Forest, where the Nightwolf Clan besieges Castle Frankat. Each heir wants the party for a servant and will offer terms. Bargain, fight or slip away: {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Cassius woke first, set thralls like the pedlar Mott to copy and sell the Heresy so the tithed souls would make the castle answer to him, and denies it smoothly. Camilla smells her old traitor on the empty lectern: Istvan, the steward who betrayed her to the Malvoraux centuries ago, came in the night and took the original to Castle Bathorya. She hides that the traitor was once hers. Each heir would sell the party to the other. Kayla is afraid here and hides it, because a witch's soul is promised to hell and this castle has a door to it.
