beats.title: The Ridge Over Carrow
beats.objective: Let the party lie on the ridge above Carrow Keep and read the fort before anyone moves: count the wall, the towers, the gatehouse, the ground between the tree line and the wall, and the traffic in and out.
beats.guidance: Ced counts three guards on the wall and two at the gatehouse and wants the count confirmed before dark. Runo can send a small golem down the slope to listen at the wall, but the golems are loud and the mule is louder. Dalan reads the ground and the brush for a covered approach; Belle wants to go down now and says so. The Keep is black stone on a rocky promontory, two guard towers, a weathered wall, and a gate that opens onto a switchback road. Let the players choose how close they get and what they give up to get there.

beats.title: The Gatehouse Watch
beats.objective: Get the party inside Carrow Keep: through the gate, over the wall, or by whatever route the scouting above the fort opened.
beats.guidance: The gatehouse is the only way in that keeps the mule and the golem cart with the party; the wall is quieter but leaves the supplies behind. Ced wants the gate guards dealt with before they can raise the towers, and Runo can put a golem against the gate leaf if the party buys him the time. Belle will take the first guard she reaches. Dalan can pick the tower archers if the party gets him a line. Whatever the party does, the fort answers: the wall is manned, the gate is barred, and the lord inside does not intend to be surprised.

entries.text: At the Guild counter, Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing each pitched their crews for a joint contract to rescue captives from a fort in the Velniran foothills. Max Nightriver chose Crimsonwing, and Kela departed without protest. Ced offered Max a stimulant vial, which Max declined, and they agreed to meet at the north gate within the hour.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: We'll go with Crimsonwing.
Ced: Ced's expression didn't shift, but his posture relaxed fractionally, a tension leaving his shoulders. He looked at Max, his red eyes flat and unreadable. "We leave at dawn. Bring any gear that helps you stay alive and kill faster."
*He reached out and took the contract from Vallie's hand, his movement efficient and brief. His gaze flicked toward Kela—not quite a look of victory, but the acknowledgment of one.* "Runo will expect punctuality."
Kela: Kela's red eyes didn't follow Ced's look. Instead, her hand went to the brim of her tricorn hat, a small gesture that was the closest she'd come to showing any reaction at all. "Understood."
*She stepped back from the counter with a measured grace, her cape settling around her shoulders. Then she turned toward the exit, her voice flat and final.* "Ebonwing has work to do."
Ced: Ced watched her leave without a word, then turned back to Max. "Runo and I will be at the north gate in an hour. You can meet us there, or I can send a messenger to fetch you."
*He reached into his coat and produced a small glass vial, the liquid inside a clear, pale amber that caught the light. He set it on the counter between them with a soft click.*
"This is a stimulant. It keeps you sharp for twenty-four hours with no crash. Consider it a down payment on your performance."
Max Nightriver: I leave the vial on the counter. We'll meet you at the north gate within the hour, then we march.
Ced: "We'll be waiting."
*He didn't argue or press the vial further. He simply turned and walked toward the Guild's exit, his tattered black cape sweeping behind him in a single fluid motion.*
Max Nightriver: An hour later we're at the north gate. We set out with Ced and Runo up the north road.
Adolion Narrator: The north gate's grey stone arch looms overhead, still damp from the overnight mist. Ced waits by a mule loaded with crates of alchemical supplies, his saw cleaver strapped to his back. Beside him, a covered cart rattles slightly as it idles—packed inside are Runo's magitech golems, their brass joints gleaming in the pre-dawn light.
Runo sits on the cart's tailboard, his owlkin tufts twitching as he watches Max Nightriver approach. For once he is wide awake, clutching a map and a sheet of vellum. "The road's clear," he says, his grey eyes darting to the Nightriver heir with a mix of recognition and nervousness. "Four days north, then we break for the foothills."
Ced steps forward, his expression as neutral as stone. "We march in silence until we hit the tree line," he says, gesturing toward the open road that leads directly into the dark silhouettes of the Velniran range. "Save your energy for the Keep."

entries.text: Runo nervously babbled about pre-charged golems and the map until Ced silenced him with a sharp look and a quiet command to save technicals for the march. As they prepared to leave the city, Ced assessed Max with a measured glance, instructing them to keep distance from the mule and cart for clear lines of sight on the road.
entries.evidence:
Runo: "Right, right. Silence. Got it." *He nods too quickly, nearly falling off the cart. He's fidgeting with the vellum in his hands, eyes flicking between Max and the map.* "The golems are already pre-charged, by the way. Should be no trouble getting them up to speed by day three."
*Ced shoots him a look—one sharp glance—and Runo immediately stuffs the map into his tunic.* "Sorry. Silent now."
Ced: "Runo." *His voice isn't raised, but the way he says it is enough to make the owlkin freeze mid-fidget.* "Save the technicals for the march. Right now we need to focus on getting out of the city."
*He adjusts the strap of the Saw Cleaver on his back, the movement crisp and efficient. His red eyes fix on the road ahead, then slide sideways to Max—not quite a glance, more of a measurement. He's assessing how this new partner carries themselves, how they move, whether they'll be a liability or an asset when the fighting starts.*
"We'll stick to a steady pace. Keep your distance from the mule and the cart. If anything happens on the road, I want clear lines of sight."

entries.text: Max Nightriver and Runo left the city behind the cart, and a few miles out Max dropped back to ask Runo what his leader had not said about the last expedition. Runo's tufts spiked as he glanced toward Ced ahead, then broke down, blaming himself for failing the last member and everyone else by not making the golems faster or stronger.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: We fall in behind the cart and leave the city. A few miles out I drop back beside the cart. Runo, what does your leader not say about the last expedition?
Runo: *Runo's tufts spike upright, and he makes a soft squawking sound.* "I-I don't—" *He shoots a glance forward, watching Ced's broad shoulders a few dozen paces ahead.* "Ced's... he's very thorough with his plans, but—"
*The words tangle in his throat, and his grey eyes go wet. He looks away, staring at the churning cart wheel.* "It's my fault. All of it. I-I should have made the golems faster, or stronger, or—" *He wipes at his eyes with the back of his hand, voice cracking.* "Ced didn't want to cut anyone, but it's better if... if we're small. Efficient. I failed the last member. I failed everyone."

entries.text: Ced halted the party at a fork in the road within a day's march of the Keep, tracing a steeper, less-watched path through the foothills on a vellum map. After days of disciplined travel north from Aegis City through thickening forest, he instructed Max Nightriver to keep his eyes on the horizon and Runo to walk behind the mule. The tone remained tense and watchful as clouds gathered and Ced scanned the treeline for movement.
entries.evidence:
Ced: *The distance between Ced and the cart has been closing for the past few minutes—not rushing, but narrowing with an efficient, steady stride. He stops and turns, his red eyes fixed on Max as his voice carries back across the road.*
"Runo."
*The owlkin immediately straightens, nearly spilling off the tailboard.*
"Walk behind the mule. You're too far back."
*Ced doesn't elaborate, doesn't acknowledge the conversation that clearly just happened. He simply waits for Runo to comply, his gaze sliding to Max with the same unreadable assessment it's carried since the gate. Then he gestures forward.*
"The road ahead is more dangerous than the one we've traveled. Keep your eyes on the horizon and not on the cart."
Max Nightriver: I nod to Ced and keep my eyes on the horizon. We keep marching north for the next few days.
Adolion Narrator: The road gradually ascends as they move farther from Aegis City, the air growing thinner and colder with each passing day. On the second day, the tree line begins to thicken, the forest swallowing the road in a canopy of pine and dark fir. On the third, the road narrows to a rutted track through the woods.
Ced maintains the same disciplined pace, his eyes constantly scanning the treeline for movement. The mule plods ahead, carrying its crates of alchemical supplies, while Runo walks in silence behind it, his owl-tufts twitching at every snap of a twig or call of a bird. The cart's golems remain packed under the canvas, their brass joints clicking softly as the vehicle jostles over roots and stones.
On the morning of the fourth day, the forest begins to thin, revealing a glimpse of the Velniran range. Grey granite peaks rise in the distance, their summits capped in year-round snow. The foothills are closer now—a broken landscape of rolling hills and jagged outcrops.
Ced halts the party at a fork in the road. He retrieves a sheet of vellum from his coat and spreads it across the cart's tailboard, his finger tracing a line upward toward the foothills.
Adolion Narrator: Ced's finger stops at a marked point on the map—a small square representing the fort. "We're within a day's march of the Keep." He traces a finger along a thinner line that snakes upward through the hills. "This path avoids the main valley roads. It's steeper, but less likely to be watched."
*He glances at the sky, where thin clouds are beginning to gather. Then his eyes slide to the treeline, watching for any sign of movement in the shadows.*
"We'll make our final push into the foothills from here."

entries.text: Max Nightriver led the group up Ced's steep path into the foothills toward the Keep, the ascent grueling through jagged granite and cold, thin air. By mid-afternoon the grim black-stone Keep came into view, and Ced halted them behind a shale ridge, quietly reporting three guards on the wall and two more at the gatehouse. The tone was tense and wary as they studied the fortress before them.
entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: We take Ced's steep path into the foothills and press on toward the Keep.
Adolion Narrator: The ascent is grueling, the path twisting upward through jagged granite and scrub brush. The air grows cold, biting, and thin. Ced sets the pace, climbing without a sound, his Saw Cleaver catching the light of the gathering storm clouds. The mule and cart struggle on the incline, brass joints of the golems grinding behind the canvas.
*By mid-afternoon, the Keep comes into view: a grim structure of black stone perched on a rocky promontory, overlooking the valley below. Two guard towers flank its gates, and a wall of weathered masonry stretches between them.*
Ced signals for a halt behind a ridge of shale. He doesn't pull out the map this time; his eyes simply fix on the Keep's silhouette. "Three guards on the wall," he says quietly. "Two more at the gatehouse."

entries.text: Ced senses something wrong because the food in the Great Hall is fresh.
entries.evidence: \"Something's wrong,\" he whispers. \"The food's fresh.\"

entries.text: Ced prepared a plan to infiltrate Carrow Keep and rescue captives, but Max Nightriver urged caution, so the group held on the ridge to observe patrols. Dalan scouted the west wall and reported a twenty-heartbeat gap in the watch change, and the group entered over the wall at Ced's signal. Inside the Great Hall, they found fresh food on the banquet table, and Ced sensed something was wrong.
entries.evidence:
Dalan: *Dalan's voice drifts up from the ledge below, soft and clear as a brook.* "Roughly twenty heartbeats. The new watch takes the wall while the old one's still descending the stairs."
*He shifts his weight, eyes never leaving the curtain wall.* "They don't overlap. It's a sloppy rotation. The west wall is blind for a few seconds while the guard's descending. I could probably get a rope up and down in that window."
*He glances back toward the gorge side of the Keep.* "The cliffs are steep but the stone's good for anchors. If we use the gorge side, we could slip in and out before they even notice we're missing."
Max Nightriver: Good. Dalan sets the rope on the west wall. Over the wall at the change of watch, everyone.
Dalan: "Understood," *Dalan murmurs, already slipping away from his vantage point. He moves with practiced economy, his green capelet fluttering as he disappears into the shadows of the cliffs below.*
Ced: "Make sure your footing is solid. We move on my word." *He doesn't look back at the others, his red eyes fixed on the west wall with predatory focus, calculating the seconds until the watch change.*
Max Nightriver: When Ced gives the word I climb the rope, drop onto the wall walk, and we make for the doors of the Great Hall.
Ced: "Now."
*He's the first to move, ascending the rope with a fluid, unnatural speed that speaks of alchemical enhancement. He clears the wall walk in a single explosive motion, his red eyes immediately locking on the patrol's rotation. The grey-robed guards don't react—they simply continue their plodding circle, oblivious.*
*Ced doesn't waste a second. He drops into a low crouch, his Saw Cleaver held in its closed form, ready to spring. His voice comes as a barely audible breath.* "Hall doors. Move."
Max Nightriver: We keep low, cross the yard behind the patrol, and push open the Great Hall's doors.
Adolion Narrator: The yard is quiet, save for the rhythmic crunch of boots and the soft *thrum-thrum* of the violet light above. Ced leads the way, his movements as precise and efficient as a machine. The patrol passes, their faces blank and vacant in the flickering torchlight, and then they are gone.
The Great Hall's doors groan as they're pushed open, releasing a smell of rotting flowers and cold stone. Inside, the violet light pulses through high windows, casting everything in an unsettling, living shade. A single chair faces the door, and beyond it, a long banquet table groans under the weight of fresh food and drink—uncorrupted by the stench of decay.
*Ced freezes, his saw cleaver half-drawn, his red eyes narrowing.* "Something's wrong," he whispers. "The food's fresh."

entries.text: Max Nightriver and his companions entered the Great Hall, where they found Lord Aldric Carrow dead on his throne and a many-eyed demon feeding on him. When the demon laughed and guards with tentacles attacked, Runo summoned a defensive golem, Dalan covered the exit, and Max freed a branded captive from the altar. With the front cut off, they fled through a side door and descended a spiral stair, the captive warning of another prisoner below.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The demon-thing on the throne screeches—a sound like metal tearing—and its too-many eyes fix on Max Nightriver. It doesn't move toward them, just watches, its jaw clicking shut over what remains of Lord Carrow's chest.
Runo's defensive golem shell hums and cracks as two armored guards slam into it, inky tentacles lashing out to grip the brass joints. The owlkin wizard yells something in Arcane, and the shell erupts in a wave of force that knocks the guards back a dozen feet, their boots scraping against stone.
On the altar, the cultist's knife descends—three inches from the branded captive's throat.
Max Nightriver: I lunge for the cultist's knife arm and wrench it away from the captive's throat.
Adolion Narrator: The knife stops an inch from the captive's skin as Max Nightriver's hand clamps around the cultist's wrist. The cultist is gaunt, his face a mask of sallow skin and vacant eyes, his fingers clawing for the knife with a weak, desperate strength. He doesn't fight back with skill—just with the mindless determination of the dead.
*From across the hall, the demon lets out another shriek, and this time something answers from deeper within the Keep.*
Max Nightriver: I cut the captive's bonds with my own knife and haul her off the altar. Dalan, the door! We run!
Dalan: *His head snaps up from the door, green eyes wide as he catches the order. He's already firing as he speaks, another arrow punching through a tentacled guard's shoulder with a meaty crack.*
"On it!"
*He doesn't look back, his hands working the string and bow with an automatic, practiced rhythm. His feet shift in the mud by the threshold, carving out a fighting stance as he watches the hall.*
"Go! Get her out of there—I'm holding them as long as I can!"
Adolion Narrator: The captive stumbles as her bonds part, and she catches Max Nightriver's arm with a trembling grip. Her face is gaunt, marked by the purple trident brand that sears across her brow.
The demon on the throne stands, its too-many eyes tracking the movement, but it doesn't rush forward—just watches, laughing softly as more armored guards emerge from the corridors, tentacles coiling and snapping.
A low, grinding sound echoes from below the Great Hall, like stone sliding on stone, and a wave of demon-reek washes over the room, thick and cloying.
Max Nightriver: The front's cut off. We drag her through the side door and down the stair below the hall, away from the guards.
Adolion Narrator: The side door is a narrow gap in the stone, half-shrouded in the pulsing violet shadow from the chapel. Beyond it lies a spiral stair descending into the heart of the Keep, where the grinding stone-on-stone echoes from below grow louder.
The air here is thick with the smell of old blood and stale incense, and the stone walls weep with condensation. Behind them, the shrieks of the demon and the metallic clatter of armored guards echo through the Great Hall as they retreat into the dark.
The captive grips Max's arm tighter as they descend, her breath coming in short, ragged gasps. "There's another one," she rasps, her voice thin and raw. "One more prisoner below... a woman in knight's rags."

She stumbles slightly as they descend the spiral stair, the violet light above fading and being replaced by a damp, oppressive darkness. "She's in the lowest cell. They... they branded her like me, but she wouldn't break. They've been starving her for weeks."
From somewhere below, another grinding sound echoes up the stair—heavier this time, as if a massive stone door is being forced open. The smell of demon-reek is stronger here, carrying a sulfurous tang that stings the nostrils.
The spiral stair ends at a iron-barred gate that leads into a dark corridor. A single torch gutters in a wall bracket nearby, its flame barely reaching the bars.

The air is different here—colder, carrying the thick musk of something wild and predatory beneath the demon-reek. Rough-hewn rock walls give way to a series of cells cut directly into the stone, their doors barred from the outside.
From deeper in the corridor comes a sound—rhythmic, guttural drumming that thrums through the stone beneath their boots, and a voice calling out in a language that sounds like bones grinding together. The captive flinches at the sound, pulling closer to Max's side. "The Beastmen," she whispers, her voice trembling. "They're still here."
The torchlight flickers across the cells as they pass—most are empty, littered with straw and filth—until they reach the far end of the corridor. In the last cell, a figure hunches in the corner, her long silver hair hanging in tangled curtains around a gaunt face. entries.text: Max Nightriver freed the branded captive, who caught his arm and revealed another prisoner below—a woman in knight's rags held in the lowest cell. Max led the group through a side door and down a spiral stair into the Keep's dungeons, where the captive warned that Beastmen still occupied the warren. At the last cell they found Unira, a gaunt silver-haired woman with red spiral-irised eyes, who confirmed she couldn't walk and warned that a shaman was coming as her Tahanna Brand pulsed with purple light.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The captive stumbles as her bonds part, and she catches Max Nightriver's arm with a trembling grip. Her face is gaunt, marked by the purple trident brand that sears across her brow.
The demon on the throne stands, its too-many eyes tracking the movement, but it doesn't rush forward—just watches, laughing softly as more armored guards emerge from the corridors, tentacles coiling and snapping.
A low, grinding sound echoes from below the Great Hall, like stone sliding on stone, and a wave of demon-reek washes over the room, thick and cloying.
Max Nightriver: The front's cut off. We drag her through the side door and down the stair below the hall, away from the guards.
Adolion Narrator: The side door is a narrow gap in the stone, half-shrouded in the pulsing violet shadow from the chapel. Beyond it lies a spiral stair descending into the heart of the Keep, where the grinding stone-on-stone echoes from below grow louder.
The air here is thick with the smell of old blood and stale incense, and the stone walls weep with condensation. Behind them, the shrieks of the demon and the metallic clatter of armored guards echo through the Great Hall as they retreat into the dark.
The captive grips Max's arm tighter as they descend, her breath coming in short, ragged gasps. "There's another one," she rasps, her voice thin and raw. "One more prisoner below... a woman in knight's rags."
Max Nightriver: A knight below? We keep going down. Where is she held?
Adolion Narrator: The captive's grip on Max's arm tightens. "The dungeons... beneath the Great Hall." She stumbles slightly as they descend the spiral stair, the violet light above fading and being replaced by a damp, oppressive darkness. "She's in the lowest cell. They... they branded her like me, but she wouldn't break. They've been starving her for weeks."
From somewhere below, another grinding sound echoes up the stair—heavier this time, as if a massive stone door is being forced open. The smell of demon-reek is stronger here, carrying a sulfurous tang that stings the nostrils.
The spiral stair ends at a iron-barred gate that leads into a dark corridor. A single torch gutters in a wall bracket nearby, its flame barely reaching the bars.
Max Nightriver: I take the torch from the bracket and we push through the gate into the corridor, looking for the lowest cell.
Adolion Narrator: The iron bars screech against the stone floor as Max Nightriver shoves them open, and the torchlight spills into the corridor. The air is different here—colder, carrying the thick musk of something wild and predatory beneath the demon-reek. Rough-hewn rock walls give way to a series of cells cut directly into the stone, their doors barred from the outside.
From deeper in the corridor comes a sound—rhythmic, guttural drumming that thrums through the stone beneath their boots, and a voice calling out in a language that sounds like bones grinding together. The captive flinches at the sound, pulling closer to Max's side. "The Beastmen," she whispers, her voice trembling. "They're still here."
The torchlight flickers across the cells as they pass—most are empty, littered with straw and filth—until they reach the far end of the corridor. In the last cell, a figure hunches in the corner, her long silver hair hanging in tangled curtains around a gaunt face. She doesn't look up as the torchlight reaches her, just draws her knees tighter to her chest.
Adolion Narrator: Somewhere deeper in the warren a drum starts, slow, and the Beastmen voices under it are counting.
Max Nightriver: Is that the knight? I kneel by the bars and speak softly. We're here to get you out.
Unira: The woman doesn't react at first, then slowly, mechanically, her head lifts. Red eyes with spiral irises stare at nothing beyond Max. She flinches when the torchlight hits her face—then her gaze slides to the captive beside Max, and back to Max.
"Fuckin' nightmare," she rasps, voice dry as dust. "How many of you? Are you—" She stops, swallowing hard. "Are you here for the brand?"
Her hand moves to her outer thigh, clutching at the tattered fabric covering the Tahanna Brand. Her fingers shake.
Max Nightriver: No, we're not here for any brand. We're here to take you home. Can you walk? I'll break the lock.
Unira: Her eyes widen slightly, then narrow. A tremor runs through her thin frame, but she forces herself to look Max in the eye—just for a heartbeat—before her gaze drops to the floor again.
"Home," she echoes, the word sounding foreign and impossible on her tongue. She swallows hard. "Can't... can't walk. Not yet. Legs feel like shit."
*The drumming grows closer—a guttural, counting voice calls out in the distance, and the Tahanna Brand beneath her skirt begins to pulse with a faint purple light.*
"The shaman," she breathes, her voice dropping to a whisper. "He's coming. If you're really gonna get me out, you better do it fuckin' now."

arcs.text: The party must choose which leader — Ced of Crimsonwing or Kela of Ebonwing — to accompany on the joint posting to the Velniran foothills fort.
arcs.summary: A fort in the Velniran foothills had been taking captives, and the Guild wanted a joint party to bring them out, so Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing each offered to take Max's party on the posting. Max probed both leaders' pitches directly rather than letting them posture, hearing Ced cite over a dozen B-rank contracts in the last six months with a ninety-eight percent success rate and a dawn departure that Runo would expect punctuality for, while Kela said Ebonwing cleared B-ranks and tracked success by results rather than percentage points. Max's party chose to accompany Ced of Crimsonwing, and Max chose Crimsonwing over Ebonwing for the joint posting to the Velniran foothills fort.

arcs.summary: Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing each pitched their party to Max for a joint Guild posting to a fort in the Velniran foothills that had been taking captives, and neither leader would speak first while the other listened, leaving the choice of partner open. When the player probed both pitches directly rather than letting them posture, Ced cited Crimsonwing's dozen-plus B-rank contracts in six months at a ninety-eight percent success rate and a dawn departure with Runo expecting punctuality, while Kela said Ebonwing cleared B-ranks and tracked success by results rather than percentage points. Max's party ultimately chose to accompany Ced of Crimsonwing on the joint posting, resolving the standoff in Crimsonwing's favor.

arcs.summary: Ced of Crimsonwing won the joint contract over Kela of Ebonwing, and Max Nightriver's party departed Aegis City's north gate with Ced and Runo of Crimsonwing, hauling a mule of alchemical supplies and a covered cart of Runo's magitech golems north toward the Velniran foothills fort. Over four days of disciplined march, Runo confessed to Max that the failed last expedition was his fault and that he had failed the last member of Crimsonwing, while Ced chose a steeper, less-watched path through the hills and ordered Runo to walk behind the mule. Reaching a shale ridge above Carrow Keep, the party observed three guards on the wall, two at the gatehouse, and a slow violet light breathing from the chapel tower, with Runo noting the guards' irregular posture and silence. Ced then ordered Runo to deploy the first golem as a distraction to open the side gate, Max to take the gatehouse while he handled the wall guards, and set the ridge as the retreat point, resolving the arc into the assault on the Keep.

After Runo broke down over his failure on the last expedition, the party reached the Keep, where Dalan scouted the west wall and found a twenty-heartbeat gap in the watch change, and Max ordered a rope set for entry at the change of watch. Inside the Great Hall they found fresh food on the banquet table, and Ced sensed something was wrong as a slow violet light pulsed from the chapel tower and the grey-robed guards failed to react to it. Ced gave the word and ascended the rope first, clearing the wall walk with alchemical speed while the guards continued their plodding circle, oblivious. canon.text:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Max Nightriver's party chose Ced of Crimsonwing over Kela of Ebonwing for a joint Guild posting to a Velniran foothills fort taking captives, swayed by Crimsonwing's record and Ced's dawn-departure discipline. Ced led Max, Runo, and Dalan north from Aegis City with a mule of alchemical supplies and a covered cart of Runo's magitech golems, taking a steeper, less-watched path to Carrow Keep. On the march Runo confessed the failed last expedition was his fault and that he had failed Crimsonwing's last member. At the Keep, Dalan scouted a twenty-heartbeat gap in the west wall watch, and the party climbed over at Ced's signal. Inside the Great Hall they found fresh food, Lord Aldric Carrow dead on his throne, and a many-eyed demon feeding on him; tentacled guards attacked, and Dalan's arrow through one guard's chest did not stop it. Runo raised a defensive golem, Dalan held the threshold, and Max wrenched a cultist's knife from a captive's throat, cut her bonds, and fled with her down a spiral stair as grinding sounds and demon-reek rose from below. The branded captive revealed a second prisoner below: a woman in knight's rags. In the lowest cell the party found a gaunt, silver-haired woman who did not look up. Max smashed the lock and carried her out; she is Unira, branded with the Tahanna Brand, too weak to stand. A Beastman shaman bearing the same brand and three Beastmen cornered them, demanding Unira's surrender. Unira revealed her own party, the Wind Ballad — Kallan, Fulanie, and Mallow — deliberately abandoned her in Nahalbuk, froze her boots, shoved her into the horde, and reported her dead.

CURRENT STATE:
Max and Unira are trapped at the lowest cell by the shaman and three Beastmen. Unira cannot walk; her legs have given out, and she clings to Max. The shaman's brand can compel her obedience, and the Tahanna Brand pulses with her breathing. Unira warns the shaman is coming and urges the party to free her immediately. She asks that the Wind Ballad be allowed to keep believing she is dead. The party must hear what happened to Unira and find the way out of Nahalbuk.

ESTABLISHED FACTS:
Ced of Crimsonwing commands Crimsonwing, with Runo as magitech golem specialist and Dalan as scout. Max Nightriver leads his own party. Unira is red-eyed with spiral irises, scarred, branded on the outer thigh with the Tahanna Brand, and too weak to stand. The Beastman shaman carries the trident-and-snake brand and the same Tahanna Brand, which can compel Unira. The Wind Ballad — Kallan, Fulanie, Mallow — abandoned Unira and reported her dead. A massive stone door is being forced open below, demon-reek grows stronger with a sulfurous tang, and Beastmen still inhabit the dungeon corridor.

removed.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: Two tricorn hats sit across the Guild counter from Vallie: Ced of Crimsonwing and Kela of Ebonwing, each standing beside a saw cleaver and refusing to look at the other. A fort in the Velniran foothills has been taking captives, and the Guild wants a joint party to bring them out. Both leaders offer to take yours, and neither will speak first while the other is listening.
Max Nightriver: Ced, Kela, why should we pick either of you?
Ced: Ced's eyes flick to Max, then away, his face a mask of studied composure. "Crimsonwing has completed over a dozen B-rank contracts in the last six months alone. We maintain a ninety-eight percent success rate." He gestures subtly to the Saw Cleaver at his side. "Runo's golems provide crowd control while I eliminate high-priority targets. We're efficient, disciplined, and we don't leave our partners behind."
*He pauses, his voice dropping perhaps a fraction in volume, measured but not soft.* "You'll receive fair payment, clear objectives, and a leader who prioritizes the party's survival above all else."
Kela: Kela didn't move, didn't react to Ced's pitch. She waited until he stopped speaking, then let her voice carry that same flat, controlled tone. "Ebonwing clears B-ranks too. We track our success by results, not by percentage points." She adjusted her glove, her gaze on Max and not the rival across the counter. "Safie's magitech golems handle siege and crowd control. I handle the rest."
*A short silence, then the next statement came as a fact, not a promise.* "We don't waste time with statistics. We take the contract, we clear the Keep, and we bring out whoever's alive. That's the job. You'll get your cut, and you'll come back in one piece."
Max Nightriver: We'll go with Crimsonwing.
Ced: Ced's expression didn't shift, but his posture relaxed fractionally, a tension leaving his shoulders. He looked at Max, his red eyes flat and unreadable. "We leave at dawn. Bring any gear that helps you stay alive and kill faster."
*He reached out and took the contract from Vallie's hand, his movement efficient and brief. His gaze flicked toward Kela—not quite a look of victory, but the acknowledgment of one.* "Runo will expect punctuality."
Kela: Kela's red eyes didn't follow Ced's look. Instead, her hand went to the brim of her tricorn hat, a small gesture that was the closest she'd come to showing any reaction at all. "Understood."
*She stepped back from the counter with a measured grace, her cape settling around her shoulders. Then she turned toward the exit, her voice flat and final.* "Ebonwing has work to do."
Ced: Ced watched her leave without a word, then turned back to Max. "Runo and I will be at the north gate in an hour. You can meet us there, or I can send a messenger to fetch you."
*He reached into his coat and produced a small glass vial, the liquid inside a clear, pale amber that caught the light. He set it on the counter between them with a soft click.*
"This is a stimulant. It keeps you sharp for twenty-four hours with no crash. Consider it a down payment on your performance."
Max Nightriver: I leave the vial on the counter. We'll meet you at the north gate within the hour, then we march.
Ced: "We'll be waiting."

Dalan: *His head snaps up from the door, green eyes wide as he catches the order. He's already firing as he speaks, another arrow punching through a tentacled guard's shoulder with a meaty crack.*
"On it!"
*He doesn't look back, his hands working the string and bow with an automatic, practiced rhythm. His feet shift in the mud by the threshold, carving out a fighting stance as he watches the hall.*
"Go! Get her out of there—I'm holding them as long as I can!"

WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Ced of Crimsonwing won the joint Guild contract over Kela of Ebonwing, and Max Nightriver's party departed Aegis City with Ced, Runo, and Dalan, hauling alchemical supplies and Runo's magitech golems north to a fort in the Velniran foothills that had been taking captives. Tentacled guards attacked; Runo raised a defensive golem, Dalan covered the exit, and Max cut the bonds of a branded captive and fled with her down a spiral stair. In the dungeon corridor, the captive told Max a second prisoner—a woman in knight's rags—was held in the lowest cell. Max smashed the lock and carried out the gaunt, silver-haired Unira, branded on her thigh with the Tahanna Brand, too weak to stand. sections.label: Where you are
lines: At the dungeon under the keep.
Unira, freed and still in the rags of her gambeson, has started to talk, and the stair back up has come down behind you.

sections.label: About this story
lines: Your C-rank party is back at the Aegis City Adventurers Guild, and the counter is offering work above your rank: a joint posting with one of the Guild's two famous high-rank parties, Crimsonwing or Ebonwing, to clear a border fort in the Velniran foothills where a rogue lord is buying captives. Expect a hard, dark delve beside partners who are polite, ruthless and proud of their record. Play the Nightriver heir who leads the party, with Belle and Dalan at your side.

sections.label: Recently
lines: You left The Prisoner in the Cells behind and moved into What Unira Says.

Max Nightriver and the captive descended the spiral stair beneath the Great Hall, past an iron-barred gate, into a dark corridor of stone cells where the demon-reek was stronger and the captive revealed that the Beastmen were still present. At the far end, in the lowest cell, they found a gaunt, silver-haired woman hunched in the corner who did not look up as the torchlight reached her. The tone was tense and oppressive, heavy with fear and foreboding.

sections.label: Open threads
lines: A Beastman shaman and three Beastmen have cornered the party at the lowest cell and demand they surrender Unira.
Unira cannot walk and must be carried out while the shaman closes in.
The Beastman shaman's brand can compel Unira, and the party must get her out before he can give her an order.
The party must decide whether to expose the Wind Ballad's betrayal and the Guild's false report of Unira's death, or honor Unira's plea to let them keep thinking she is dead.

sections.label: The story so far
lines: Max Nightriver's party chose Ced of Crimsonwing over Kela of Ebonwing for a joint Guild posting to a Velniran foothills fort taking captives, swayed by Crimsonwing's record and Ced's dawn-departure discipline. Ced led Max, Runo, and Dalan north from Aegis City with a mule of alchemical supplies and a covered cart of Runo's magitech golems, taking a steeper, less-watched path to Carrow Keep. driver.title: Adolion: Crimsonwing & Ebonwing
driver.activeObjective: Hear what happened to Unira, and find the way out of Nahalbuk.
driver.canon:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
Max Nightriver's party chose Ced of Crimsonwing over Kela of Ebonwing for a joint Guild posting to a Velniran foothills fort taking captives, swayed by Crimsonwing's record and Ced's dawn-departure discipline. Ced led Max, Runo, and Dalan north from Aegis City with a mule of alchemical supplies and a covered cart of Runo's magitech golems, taking a steeper, less-watched path to Carrow Keep. On the march Runo confessed the failed last expedition was his fault and that he had failed Crimsonwing's last member. At the Keep, Dalan scouted a twenty-heartbeat gap in the west wall watch, and the party climbed over at Ced's signal. Inside the Great Hall they found fresh food, Lord Aldric Carrow dead on his throne, and a many-eyed demon feeding on him; tentacled guards attacked, and Dalan's arrow through one guard's chest did not stop it. Runo raised a defensive golem, Dalan held the threshold, and Max wrenched a cultist's knife from a captive's throat, cut her bonds, and fled with her down a spiral stair as grinding sounds and demon-reek rose from below. The branded captive revealed a second prisoner below: a woman in knight's rags. In the lowest cell the party found a gaunt, silver-haired woman who did not look up. Max smashed the lock and carried her out; she is Unira, branded with the Tahanna Brand, too weak to stand. A Beastman shaman bearing the same brand and three Beastmen cornered them, demanding Unira's surrender. Unira revealed her own party, the Wind Ballad — Kallan, Fulanie, and Mallow — deliberately abandoned her in Nahalbuk, froze her boots, shoved her into the horde, and reported her dead.

CURRENT STATE:
Max and Unira are trapped at the lowest cell by the shaman and three Beastmen. Unira cannot walk; her legs have given out, and she clings to Max. The shaman's brand can compel her obedience, and the Tahanna Brand pulses with her breathing. Unira warns the shaman is coming and urges the party to free her immediately. She asks that the Wind Ballad be allowed to keep believing she is dead. The party must hear what happened to Unira and find the way out of Nahalbuk.

ESTABLISHED FACTS:
Ced of Crimsonwing commands Crimsonwing, with Runo as magitech golem specialist and Dalan as scout. Max Nightriver leads his own party. Unira is red-eyed with spiral irises, scarred, branded on the outer thigh with the Tahanna Brand, and too weak to stand. The Beastman shaman carries the trident-and-snake brand and the same Tahanna Brand, which can compel Unira. The Wind Ballad — Kallan, Fulanie, Mallow — abandoned Unira and reported her dead. A massive stone door is being forced open below, demon-reek grows stronger with a sulfurous tang, and Beastmen still inhabit the dungeon corridor.
driver.recentChat:
*The purple glow of her brand burns brighter as it pulses in time with her ragged breathing.* "Fuckin' traitors. That's who left me. My own goddamn party."
*She presses her weight against Max, her hand clutching their shoulder tight enough to bruise. Her eyes are locked on the shaman, wide and terrified.*
"The shaman's brand—it's the same as mine. If he gives an order and I don't—" *She chokes back a sob, her voice cracking.* "Please. Just get me outta here. I can't... I won't go back there."

The stair back up to the keep came down behind them in the fight, so the only way out is the warren's back tunnels, running north with a cold draught and, very faint, the ring of picks. Let it land however the party pushes; nobody confesses for anyone.

[Earlier scenes]
Max Nightriver and Runo left the city behind the cart, and a few miles out Max dropped back to ask Runo what his leader had not said about the last expedition. Runo's tufts spiked as he glanced toward Ced ahead, then broke down, blaming himself for failing the last member and everyone else by not making the golems faster or stronger.
Ced halted the party at a fork in the road within a day's march of the Keep, tracing a steeper, less-watched path through the foothills on a vellum map. After days of disciplined travel north from Aegis City through thickening forest, he instructed Max Nightriver to keep his eyes on the horizon and Runo to walk behind the mule. The tone remained tense and watchful as clouds gathered and Ced scanned the treeline for movement.
Max Nightriver led the group up Ced's steep path into the foothills toward the Keep, the ascent grueling through jagged granite and cold, thin air. By mid-afternoon the grim black-stone Keep came into view, and Ced halted them behind a shale ridge, quietly reporting three guards on the wall and two more at the gatehouse. The tone was tense and wary as they studied the fortress before them.
Ced prepared a plan to infiltrate Carrow Keep and rescue captives, but Max Nightriver urged caution, so the group held on the ridge to observe patrols. Dalan scouted the west wall and reported a twenty-heartbeat gap in the watch change, and the group entered over the wall at Ced's signal. Inside the Great Hall, they found fresh food on the banquet table, and Ced sensed something was wrong.
Max Nightriver and the captive descended the spiral stair beneath the Great Hall, past an iron-barred gate, into a dark corridor of stone cells where the demon-reek was stronger and the captive revealed that the Beastmen were still present. At the far end, in the lowest cell, they found a gaunt, silver-haired woman hunched in the corner who did not look up as the torchlight reached her. The tone was tense and oppressive, heavy with fear and foreboding.
